News.title: Andy Burnham urges shops to pause disposable barbecue sales after Cobra heatwave meeting
News.content:
Andy Burnham urges shops to pause disposable barbecue sales after Cobra heatwave meeting

Prime Minister Andy Burnham convened ministers, officials and agencies as scorching temperatures persist across the country in the fifth heatwave of the summer

View 2 Images The PM convened ministers, officials and agencies as scorching temperatures persist across in the fifth heatwave of the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has urged all retailers to pause the sale of disposable barbecues in order to prevent more wildfires raging this summer.

‌



It came as the Prime Minister warned extreme heat conditions "could be with us for some weeks yet" after chairing an emergency Cobra meeting in response to the fifth heatwave this summer.

‌



Speaking on Wednesday evening, he said: "The big risk in terms of risk to the wider regions across the country is the risk of wildfires. What we are seeing is multiple serious incidents across the country.

‌



"Fire services by and large are supporting each other through mutual aid to deal with those incidents, but we are keeping a very close watching brief on them."

He added: "There is advice to the public here not to use disposable barbecues. We have today confirmed through the National Fire Chiefs Council that the framework restricting the retail sale of those disposable barbecues is being extended.

"Now I would ask all retailers big and small to adhere to that framework. Longer term we will look at whether a temporary ban in the summer months is justified." Most major UK supermarkets have already suspended sales of disposable barbecues in recent weeks in line with voluntary guidance from the NFCC.

‌



NHS must plan for heatwaves like winter crises to protect frail and vulnerable, Yvette Cooper says READ MORE :

View 2 Images Andy Burnham is looking at whether a temporary ban of disposable barbecue in the summer months is justified (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

The message followed Wednesday's Cobra meeting with the PM convening ministers, officials and agencies as scorching temperatures persist across the country in the fifth heatwave of the summer. They included representatives from the Environment Agency, the Met Office, and the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

Earlier this week, the Environment Agency said 71.3% of England is now experiencing "flash drought", following the country's driest July on record.

‌



Before the Cobra meeting, Mr Burnham also said people should not be using single-use grills "at this time" amid a "significant problem" of wildfires in the south, where a blaze hit protected heathland in the New Forest, Hampshire.

The Prime Minister said he was "certainly going to consider" a ban, adding: "I do believe we need to get the message out loud and clear. People should not be using those barbecues outside at this moment in time."

On Tuesday, a firefighters' union sounded the alarm, warning that the country is facing a "national emergency" amid the ongoing wildfire crisis. General secretary Steve Wright said: "Lives are being put at risk. This is only going to get worse unless we get a grip of it now and put in place a proper national strategy".

Article continues below

The Cobra meeting on Wednesday was the second this summer on heatwaves after one took place amid high temperatures in June.

The Met Office has said the UK is on course for its hottest summer on record. Rare amber "extreme heat" warnings have been issued by the forecaster for London and parts of the South East, East Midlands, East of England, West Midlands and South Yorkshire from 9am to midnight on Thursday.

News.title: Bus driver, 25, shot dead outside London pub named as devastated family pay tribute
News.content:
Bus driver, 25, shot dead outside London pub named as devastated family pay tribute

Auguste-Marie Bile-aka Amoa was described as an 'amazing person' and 'kind man' who died from being in 'the wrong place at the wrong time'

View 3 Images (Image: Metropolitan Police/PA Wire)

A 25-year-old bus driver who died after being shot outside a pub in Clapham, south London, on Monday has been named as Auguste-Marie Bile-aka Amoa.

‌



The victim died after he was attacked outside a venue by an assailant who was also hospitalised with a gunshot wound and was arrested on suspicion of murder, according to the force.

‌



The suspect remains in hospital under police guard.

‌



Paramedics raced to the area outside the Landor Pub in Clapham North, within three minutes of the incident, but despite their best efforts, the man was pronounced dead at the scene, a London Ambulance Service spokesperson said.

View 3 Images Bile-aka Amoa was shot outside a pub in Clapham on Monday (Image: Jonathan Brady/PA Wire)

Speaking near the scene, a fried of Amoa described him as a "cool guy" who was "in the wrong place at the wrong time."

‌



“I don’t have bad things to say about him.

“He’s a cool guy, like I said, bus driver, hard-working.

“It’s shocking because of who he is and his character.”

‌



The man, who also works as a bus driver, said the death is “going to hurt a lot of people”.

Another friend of the victim, who asked to remain anonymous, said he was a “great guy”, adding: “It’s been hectic, everyone’s very hot-headed right now, everyone’s obviously grieving and I feel extremely bad for his mother as well, she’s in bits.

“It hurts me as well.”

‌



Prior to his death, Amoa also worked as a volunteer at a local school, and helped to mentor young people, a staff member told The Metro.

View 3 Images Friends described the victim as a 'kind man' who was 'in the wrong place at the wrong time' (Image: Jonathan Brady/PA Wire)

"He was a lovely kid; he had played around the area when he was young and wanted to give something back.

‌



"He was a lovely guy, great with the kids who would look up to him."

Another family member told the publication: "He was an amazing person and a best friend. He loved driving, so bus driver was the perfect job. He was living his dream.

"I have a daughter, and he would buy her gifts and was such a kind man.

‌



"He loved music and dancing; he was just wonderful. I heard about the shooting yesterday, and I know he is in that area.

"I texted him and got nothing back, then I found out the news. I’m heartbroken.’

Detective chief inspector Claire Guiver, who is leading the investigation, said: “Our thoughts remain with Bile-aka’s family as they come to terms with this tragic incident.

‌



“We continue to appeal for anyone with information to come forward.

“If you were in the area at the time of the shooting, witnessed anything suspicious or have any CCTV, dashcam or doorbell footage that could assist our investigation, we urge you to get in touch.

“Any piece of information could prove vital in helping us piece together the full circumstances.”

Article continues below

It is understood the alleged gunman was hospitalised by injury inflicted by his own gun.

News.title: Once-in-a-generation solar eclipse wows millions in UK and Europe
News.content:
The UK and Europe have enjoyed their most dramatic solar eclipse for nearly 30 years, with millions thought to have witnessed the once-in-a-generation event.

Those watching the astronomical phenomenon from the UK were treated to a partial eclipse, which peaked shortly after 19:00 BST, when most saw more than 90% of the Sun covered by the Moon.

But parts of Greenland, Iceland and Spain experienced the complete darkness and spectacle of a total eclipse.

Large crowds at viewing sites across the UK and Europe reacted with gasps and cheers, with astronomy enthusiasts saying it served as a reminder of how "amazing" the universe is.

The path of the total eclipse began at the northern tip of Siberia in Russia, far away from crowds and telescopes.

But it soon began curving around the Arctic Ocean arriving in Iceland in the early evening before sweeping southwards to treat the UK to part of its wonder.

The partial eclipse began at about 18:00 BST in northern Scotland and just before 18:20 on the south coast of England.

It was imperceivable at first, but for those blessed with cloud-free skies, crowds noticed the Moon nibbling away at the Sun.

News.title: Watch: Solar eclipse seen over UK skies
News.content:
Millions of people across the UK have witnessed the most significant solar eclipse since 1999.

People gathered across the country on Wednesday to watch the spectacle, as more than 90% of the Sun was obscured by the Moon.

News.title: Students wait for A-level, T-level and BTec results
News.content:
Hundreds of thousands of students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive A-level, T-level and BTec results on Thursday morning.

Another record number of students are expected to find out they have secured a place at their first choice of university.

The cost of going to university has been in the spotlight this year, with mounting pressure on the government to reform student loan repayments, and there has been a renewed focus on technical education under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

But the chief executive of Universities UK, which represents more than 140 vice-chancellors, urged students to not "let politicians make your decision for you".

About 40% of 18-year-olds in England receive A-levels every summer.

Around 250,000 grades for vocational and technical qualifications are also expected to be released to students in England, including BTec National, Cambridge Technical, Cambridge Advanced National and T-level results.

AS-levels, which will count towards students' final A-level results next summer in Wales and Northern Ireland, will also be released.

This year, the pass rate for National 5, Higher and Advanced Higher exams in Scotland rose across the board.

And last year, the proportion of students getting top A-level results reached a record high, with 28.3% of all grades across England, Wales and Northern Ireland marked at A* or A.

News.title: Double killer and rapist given whole life sentence
News.content:
A serial sex attacker who had a "morbid fascination" with sex has been jailed for the rest of his life after he was found guilty of murdering two women and raping a third.

Simon Levy, 40, killed Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53, in March 2025 and 39-year-old Sheryl Wilkins five months later. Earlier that year, he raped a third woman in the same Tottenham car park where Wilkins was later found dead.

At the Old Bailey on Wednesday, Judge Mark Lucraft KC sentenced Levy to a whole life order, meaning he will never be released.

The sentence comes after police and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) apologised over a series of disastrous decisions that left him free to roam the streets.

When Levy carried out the attacks, he was on bail and being monitored by the Met.

The police watchdog is currently examining how he was managed over a four-year period, from his first conviction in September 2021 for sexual assault up to his final arrest in September 2025.

Following Wednesday's sentencing, Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said the handling of Levy's case was a "whole system failing".

News.title: Burnham urges shops not to sell disposable BBQs over wildfire risks
News.content:
Andy Burnham has urged shops to stop selling disposable barbecues amid increased wildfire risk driven by this summer's droughts.

The prime minister said he was urging "all retailers big and small" to adhere to voluntary guidance to suspend sales during extreme heat.

He added that in the "longer term" the government would look at potentially banning the single-use grills during summer months.

It comes after a potential ban was discussed at an emergency Cobra meeting on the government's response to record temperatures.

A number of large retailers and supermarkets have voluntarily stopped selling the devices under a framework, external agreed in 2023 between fire chiefs and the British Retail Consortium (BRC).

This says that retailers should suspend sales once an extreme heat event has been declared as imminent, or in response to "reasonable, evidence based" requests from local councils.

Earlier, Burnham told reporters single-use grills had been behind a number of recent blazes and people should not be using them "at this moment in time".

"We do want people to take the greatest possible care when they are out in the countryside, both in terms of cigarettes, but also those temporary barbecues that we know are causing risk of fires."

After the Cobra meeting, Burnham said: "We would say to retailers do not put disposable barbecues on sale at this moment in time."

Nearly three-quarters of England and all of Wales have been officially declared in drought, creating conditions rife for fire to spread.

The Met Office has issued a rare amber extreme heat warning for Thursday, with temperatures peaking in the mid-to-high 30s across the Midlands and south-east of England, and a high of 38C possible.

News.title: Jasper Carrott says family is 'so proud' of Lucy Davis after cancer diagnosis
News.content:
Actor and comedian Jasper Carrott has spoken about his pride and love for daughter Lucy Davis after she announced she has incurable breast cancer.

The actress, best known for playing receptionist Dawn Tinsley in BBC sitcom The Office, has received an outpouring of support since she revealed her diagnosis on Tuesday.

Carrott, who was one of the most familiar faces on British television over several decades, told BBC News: "This is a very difficult time for the whole family and we have been supporting her in every way possible since her diagnosis.

"We are so grateful for all the support we have had over this trying time and we are very hopeful for her future being what she wants it to be."

He added: "We are so proud of our daughter and love her so much. The way she has conducted herself through many traumatic health issues is a lesson to us all.

"We would request privacy for the coming months, but thanks once again for the love and concern shown by so many people."

Carrott, whose real name is Robert Davis, became a household name in the 1970s thanks to his stand-up comedy and novelty songs.

He has presented programmes such as Canned Carrott, Golden Balls and Carrott's Commercial Breakdown, and acted in comedy series such as The Detectives.

News.title: Eurovision Song Contest changes rules for countries at war
News.content:
Organisers of the Eurovision Song Contest have updated their rules to state that if a country involved in an armed conflict wins the competition, it will be ineligible to host it the following year.

The amendment was approved by the contest's governing body, following feedback from participating broadcasters after Eurovision 2026 in Vienna.

It states that winning countries will also be disqualified from hosting if a "sensitive geopolitical situation" affects the "security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region".

The update will be interpreted as a reaction to Israel's continued presence at the contest, amid criticism of its military actions in Gaza and the Middle East.

Last November, following a failed attempt to have Israel suspended, five broadcasters announced they were boycotting the competition - including Eurovision powerhouses Spain and Ireland.

Despite the protests, Israel's Noam Bettan ultimately took second place with his song Michelle.

It marked the second year in a row that Israel had taken the runners-up position - and some participating broadcasters have privately expressed safety concerns over the contest being staged in Jerusalem or Tel Aviv, should the country win in the future.

Although Israel will undoubtedly be seen as the target of the rule change, it will also affect Ukraine, which has been engaged in a protracted war since it was invaded by Russia in 2022.

Ukrainian group Kalush Orchestra went on to win Eurovision that same year, in a symbolic show of public support.

Following their victory, Eurovision organisers undertook a "full assessment and feasibility study" to decide whether the 2023 contest could proceed in Kyiv.

They ultimately decided the security risks were too great, and the UK stepped in to host the competition in Liverpool.

News.title: GB's Evans wins European gold in 100m breaststroke
News.content:
Great Britain's Angharad Evans won her first European Championship gold in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.

The 23-year-old comfortably finished first in a championship record time of one minute and 4.87 seconds, which was also a lifetime best and British record.

Having also broken the championship record in the semi-final, Evans claimed gold ahead of Ireland's Mona McSharry in second, while Italy's Benedetta Pilato took bronze.

Great Britain's Filip Nowacki, who made history for Jersey by claiming gold in the 200m breaststroke at the Commonwealth Games last month in Glasgow, was the fastest qualifier in the semi-final of the same event at the European Aquatics Championships.

The 18-year-old's time of 2:08.60 held off GB team-mate Greg Butler in the first semi-final, with the 25-year-old also progressing to the final.

GB's Amalie Smith picked up a silver medal in the 400m individual medley final, finishing 0.7secs behind Ireland's Ellen Walshe, with Poland's Justina Kozan claiming bronze.

The 16-year-old Smith, who won gold on Monday in the 4x200m freestyle relay, was also part of the part of the 4x100m freestyle relay team that finished fifth.

Another teenager, Italian Sara Curtis, also shone as she broke the women's 50m backstroke world record with a time of 26.63 seconds.

The 19-year-old bettered the world record set by Australia's Kaylee McKeown three years ago by 0.23secs in her semi-final.

News.title: New Forest wildfire continues as temperatures rise
News.content:
Firefighters on the fourth day of battling a wildfire in the New Forest are facing "challenging" weather conditions with temperatures set to rise again

The blaze began on Sunday 9 August when a van caught fire on the A31, with 23 drivers abandoning their vehicles as the fire took hold.

Hampshire & Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service (HIWFRS) said crews had implemented fire breaks and had a 'good hold' of the perimeter of the fire, while changing wind conditions were proving challenging.

National Highways said repairs to the A31 were not expected to be begin until Friday 14 August at the earliest.

News.title: Ministers push ahead with housing asylum seekers on ex-military sites
News.content:
Home Office minister Anna Turley has said the government is sticking with plans to accommodate asylum-seekers on former military bases despite protests from local residents.

She told the BBC the government's priority was to ensure asylum-seekers were looked after in a "secure" and "appropriate" place.

That included disused Ministry of Defence properties because they had on-site facilities and were "more contained," she added.

But campaigners in areas earmarked for asylum centres have said small communities with limited infrastructure would not be able to cope with large numbers of people.

There have been protests in Piddington, Oxfordshire, over plans to house more than 1,000 asylum seekers at a site near the village.

Mike Nixon, the vice-chairman of Piddington Parish Council, said there was a "huge amount of concern and worry" among residents and that an asylum centre would have a "dramatic effect" on the way they lived their lives.

The proposal has prompted Piddington to hold a symbolic independence referendum, asking its 400 or so residents if they want to remain part of the UK.

Nixon said: "We're still very frustrated. Andy Burnham did say that he's willing to listen, but we've had no formal contact. No consultation, nothing from the Home Office.

"We felt that the only way of making our views felt was to say 'well if we're not going to be listened to, what's the point of being a part of the country?'"

The government has promised to end the use of hotels for asylum seekers, announcing on Wednesday that a further 13 across England had been closed.

It plans to use former military sites instead with two already up and running - RAF Wethersfield in Essex, and Crowborough Training Camp in East Sussex.

In June, it announced proposals to open three more, including the site near Piddington.

The two other planned sites are a former RAF base in Barnham in Suffolk where there were protests last week and RAF Linton-on-Ouse in North Yorkshire where the area's Labour mayor said it was "simply the wrong place".

Defending the proposals on BBC Breakfast, Turley said the public wanted the government to end the use of hotels, pointing to how an "iconic" hotel in Blackpool, the Metropole, was no longer being used to accommodate asylum-seekers.

She said it sent "an important message" that the government wanted the hotel to be part of Blackpool's future.

"The priority is to ensure we look after asylum seekers in a secure place that is more appropriate and we limit the impact on communities."

Asked what she meant by secure, she said: "Examples we are looking at is former military bases and we have two up and running and possibly another three.

"They have have facilities on site and are more contained and it limits the impact on on communities.

"We are looking at other sites such as former industrial sites, student accommodation - accommodation that is more more appropriate than hotels."

News.title: I share concerns over Arday appointment, says Cambridge University head
News.content:
The vice-chancellor of the University of Cambridge has said she understands the concerns raised by the appointment of Jason Arday and shares them too.

In a letter to staff, Prof Deborah Prentice acknowledged the "anger and anxiety around this damaging and difficult case".

The university head also announced Cambridge's investigation would be independent and carried out by senior academics from within and beyond Cambridge and will begin "as soon as possible".

Arday resigned as a Cambridge professor of sociology of education last week amid allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements.

The 41-year-old - who became Cambridge's youngest ever black professor in 2023 - denies any plagiarism and said the recent furore had led to "an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack".

In a letter to university staff, Prof Deborah Prentice said: "I fully understand the concerns being raised across the University and well beyond it, regarding Jason Arday's appointment and I share them...

"We will now investigate the circumstances around his appointment by the faculty of education back in 2022 and his time here in Cambridge since his appointment nearly four years ago.

"That investigation, as you say, should be thorough and transparent, and will be carried out independently by senior academics from within and beyond Cambridge."

The findings of the investigation, previously announced on Friday, will inform a review into the process for the appointment of senior academic roles, the university has said.

Prentice added "our staff of colour are highly valued, for their scholarship, their achievements, and the contributions they make" and said the case "should not be used to cast aspersions on their work or the legitimacy of their roles at Cambridge".

Cambridge had previously said allegations of plagiarism regarding Arday's thesis and some journal publications had been investigated by Liverpool John Moores University (LMJU) and the journals in question.

LJMU - which awarded his PhD in 2015 - had investigated the allegations that were made last year, and found he did not commit plagiarism.

In an interview with the Times, Arday defended himself by arguing that he had not received adequate supervision during his PhD given his autism and "learning disabilities".

The University of Cambridge said it had advised people to contact the relevant institution or pass on complaints.

But after Cambridge announced its own investigation, some academics pushed for the inquiry to be independent, questioning whether the university could adequately investigate its own processes.

It is not yet clear how the independent investigation will work or who will lead it. The university said it will look at the circumstances around his appointment by the faculty of education in 2022 and his time in Cambridge since his appointment.

Arday worked as a PE teacher before earning his doctorate at LMJU and going on to become an associate professor at Durham University and professor of sociology of education at the University of Glasgow.

Glasgow has also announced a review into Arday's previous academic post.

When he resigned from his post, Arday said he was not a "liar" and that his resignation "should not be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me."

News.title: Green councillor charged with assaults
News.content:
A Birmingham Green Party city councillor has been charged with attacking a member of the public, three police officers and a member of police staff.

Siobhan Harper-Nunes, 66, was arrested on suspicion of assault after police were called to the junction of Monument Road and Hagley Road in the city, at about 17:00 BST on Thursday.

Harper-Nunes, of Monument Road, was charged on Friday.

West Midlands Police said that she was arrested again at Monument Road on Wednesday morning on suspicion of harassment.

She remained in custody while inquiries continued, police said.

Harper-Nunes will appear at Birmingham Magistrates' Court on 10 September on the assault charges, the force said.

The councillor was elected in May to represent the Ladywood ward for the city council.

She previously stood as the Green Party's candidate for West Midlands mayor in the 2024 election.

The Birmingham Green Party has been approached for comment.

News.title: Man bled to death after being bitten by American XL Bully, court hears
News.content:
A man died from extreme blood loss after suffering "catastrophic injuries" when he was bitten on the leg by an American XL bully in his daughter-in-law's garden, a court has heard.

Keven Jones, 62, from Chester, who was in poor health, taking methadone and blood thinning medication, was staying at Chanel Fong's house at the time of the incident.

The incident took place before XL Bullies were added to the banned dog list in October 2023.

Fong, 33, denies being the owner of the dog, which the prosecution said was dangerously out of control at the time, and also denies an alternative charge of being the person in charge of a dog at the time of the attack.

Opening the case at Caernarfon Crown Court, prosecutor Mark Connor said it was a "sad and tragic case for everyone concerned" and told the jury they would be shown some "graphic images" of Jones' injuries during the trial.

He said it was not a case of whether the XL Bully, named Cookie, was a banned breed, but rather that the dog had been "dangerously out of control" and whether Fong was legally responsible for it, either as its owner or the person responsible for it at the time.

The court was told the dog was owned by Fong and her partner, Joshua Jones, the son of the victim, but that he was not present at the time of the attack.

Connor added that, in her police interview, Fong said on paper Cookie belonged to her partner.

He went on to describe how there were a number of dogs at the property on Holt Road in Wrexham, including Cookie and another XL Bully called Fire, who were in the back garden at the time.

Cookie's mother, an XL Bully called Rogue, was inside the property and was "in season" meaning she had been kept separate from the other dogs in the house.

News.title: Ann Widdecombe's loved ones gather for her funeral
News.content:
Police officers and sniffer dogs were in the grounds of the abbey ahead of the service, which lasted about 90 minutes.

The private requiem mass included a homily from the Rt Rev David Charlesworth, Abbot of Buckfast.

He said: "In the midst of the shock, clamour and sometimes unwarranted comment surrounding her death, our response is to pray for the repose of her soul, to give thanks for her fortitude, and offer Holy Mass in this Abbey Church which Ann called her safe haven."

A statement from the Abbey Church earlier said Widdecombe would be "missed and fondly remembered" and "many in our worshipping community knew her as a kind and warm character".

"Ann was a woman of profound faith, a faith which found expression in the public forum of politics," it said.

It added: "Ann was unafraid to express her unwavering convictions, formed through her Roman Catholic faith. She had a sharp intellect and was a dedicated public servant."

The order of service also included tributes paid by the Rev Roger Widdecombe, Widdecombe's nephew, and Sir Christian Sweeting, a close friend.

A public memorial for Widdecombe is due to be held later this year.

News.title: Victim of fatal Clapham shooting named
News.content:
A man who was shot dead in south-west London has been named by police as Auguste-Marie Bile-aka Amoa.

Officers and paramedics were called to Willington Road, Clapham, just before 22:00 BST on Monday following reports of gunshots near The Landor pub.

The 25-year-old, who worked as a bus driver, was pronounced dead at the scene, the Metropolitan Police said.

A 22-year-old man was later arrested on suspicion of murder after attending hospital with a gunshot wound on Tuesday. He remains in hospital under police guard.

Det Ch Insp Claire Guiver said her thoughts were with the victim's family as they "come to terms with this tragic incident".

News.title: Windermere signs to warn of algae poisoning risk
News.content:
Dozens of signs warning people about the dangers of algae poisoning are to be placed around England's largest lake.

About 40 notice boards alerting visitors to blue-green algae blooms, which can produce toxins that make humans ill and be fatal to pets, will be installed at Windermere, in the Lake District.

Blooms occur naturally but are more frequent during warm, dry weather and are exacerbated by nutrients from phosphate in pollutants such as sewage.

Funded by the Environment Agency (EA), a further 40 signs will be placed at other locations across Cumbria.

The Love Windermere Partnership, which includes organisations such as the EA, Lake District National Park Authority and United Utilities, said it was installing the permanent signs in response to requests for "clearer and more consistent public information".

As well as explaining what blue-green algae looks like, the notices will provide guidance on where to find current information about blooms and how to report suspected sightings using the Bloomin' Algae app, external.

The microscopic organisms can look like blue-green paint, scum or greenish-brown discolouration.

News.content:

A bus driver who was shot dead outside a south London pub has been named by police.

Gunshots were heard near the venue in Willington Road, Clapham, on Monday.

Auguste-Marie Bile-aka Amoa, 25, was named by the Metropolitan Police as the victim of the attack.

Shortly after the shooting, a 22-year-old man attended hospital with a gunshot wound and was arrested on suspicion of murder, the Met said.

He remains in hospital under police guard.

Detective chief inspector Claire Guiver, who is leading the investigation, said: “Our thoughts remain with Bile-aka’s family as they come to terms with this tragic incident.

“We continue to appeal for anyone with information to come forward.

“If you were in the area at the time of the shooting, witnessed anything suspicious or have any CCTV, dashcam or doorbell footage that could assist our investigation, we urge you to get in touch.

open image in gallery Gunshots were heard near the venue in Willington Road, Clapham, on Monday ( PA Archive )

“Any piece of information could prove vital in helping us piece together the full circumstances.”

Speaking near the scene, a friend of the victim described him as a “cool guy”, adding that he believed the death was the result of “wrong place, wrong time”.

He said: “I don’t have bad things to say about him.

“He’s a cool guy, like I said, bus driver, hard-working.

“It’s shocking because of who he is and his character.”

The man, who also works as a bus driver, said the death is “going to hurt a lot of people”.

A police forensics tent was still in place across the road from The Landor pub on Tuesday while several bouquets of flowers were laid and a candle was lit near its entrance.

Staff from The Landor are understood to have helped the victim after the shooting.

A 26-year-old woman living nearby said she heard four gunshots and initially thought it was the sound of a car backfiring.

Two other residents described hearing four gunshots at around 10pm on Monday and seeing a car with a broken window.

One man, who did not wish to be named, said he heard three gunshots and saw someone run out of the pub and shout “call the police”.

He said he saw a moped and white car drive off before the police arrived, and that women could be heard “screaming and crying” outside.

Xavi Hernandez has been named the new head coach of the Netherlands.

The 46-year-old Spanish manager has signed a deal to lead the national side until the 2030 World Cup.

He takes over from Ronald Koeman, who resigned after the Dutch were defeated by Morocco in the last 32 of this summer’s tournament.

As a player, former Barcelona midfielder Xavi won the 2010 World Cup with Spain alongside the European Championship in 2008 and 2012.

He guided Barca to the LaLiga title in 2023, having previously started his coaching career with Qatari side Al Sadd.

“I consider it a tremendous honour to become head coach of the Dutch national team,” he said in a statement released by the Dutch Football Association (KNVB).

“As someone who received his training at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, among others, I feel a special connection to Dutch football.

open image in gallery Xavi Hernandez managed Barcelona between 2021 and 2024 ( Martin Rickett/PA )

“You could say that I am a bit of a son of Dutch football.”

Xavi’s appointment marks his first return to management since leaving Barcelona in 2024.

He took over the Catalan giants in November 2021, also succeeding Koeman, after making 767 appearances for the club.

“The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that also appeals to me enormously: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion, and conviction,” he continued.

“Of course, the most important goal is and always will be to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy.

“The potential for this is there, as well as a solid foundation to build upon.”

Explaining Xavi’s appointment, KNVB director of football Nigel de Jong said: “As a coach, he has been shaped by years of working with top coaches who espouse a football vision that aligns very well with the way we want to play with the Dutch national team: taking initiative, dominant and attractive football, combined with the flexibility that modern elite football demands.

“Xavi believes in those basic principles, has embraced that vision, and made it his own. All of that, combined with his personality and the way he knows how to connect with players and get the best out of a group, makes him the right choice for the coming years.”

Clacton constituents will head to the polls this Thursday in one of the stranger modern by-elections as Nigel Farage attempts to win his seat back.

The Reform UK leader resigned as an MP to force the vote in protest at media and parliamentary scrutiny regarding financial backing from his donors.

While major Westminster parties are boycotting the contest, dismissing it as a stunt by the Reform UK leader, a record 34 candidates are standing.

Mr Farage wanted it to be a "people versus the establishment" showdown, but his opponents now include satirical candidate Count Binface, actor-turned-politician Laurence Fox, three candidates from the Official Monster Raving Loony Party, and an array of independents.

open image in gallery Reform UK leader Nigel Farage will seek to win back the Clacton seat he vacated ( James Manning/PA )

The contest is expected to cost taxpayers roughly £250,000, with the 90cm-long ballot paper creating logistical hurdles for Tendring District Council and returning officer Ian Davidson.

Because of the sheer size of the ballot paper, larger counting tables than usual will be needed.

The result will be announced on the floor of Clacton Leisure Centre rather than on a stage due to the number of candidates who must fit on it.

Mr Farage was being investigated by the parliamentary standards commissioner Daniel Greenberg over a £5 million gift from cryptocurrency tycoon Christopher Harborne, which he received before taking his seat in the Commons.

Under the Commons’ rules, new MPs are required to register any gifts worth more than £300 they received in the previous 12 months, except where the gift “could not be reasonably thought by others” to relate to their political activities.

open image in gallery The 90cm-long ballot paper has created logistical hurdles for Tendring District Council and returning officer Ian Davidson ( Tendring District Council/PA )

That investigation was paused when Mr Farage resigned his seat, but will resume if he wins the by-election – as bookmakers have made him the firm favourite to do.

Mr Farage could also face an investigation over support provided by George Cottrell, a long-term ally.

Mr Cottrell reportedly recruited and paid three staff to work on Mr Farage’s social media before the general election, and has continued to allow him to use a five-storey Georgian property he rented near Buckingham Palace.

Mr Farage said: “At the beginning of summer we called this by-election to give the people of Clacton the chance to have their say on the endless political attacks on me, my family and those around me.

“It’s given us the opportunity to knock on tens of thousands of doors, making the affirmative case for what I’ve done for the area, and what Reform will do for Britain.”

He said “it’s not just about me, it’s about the people versus the establishment” and the vote “is our chance to send a stunning message to the political class: Britain needs Reform, Britain wants Reform, and Britain demands a general election”.

open image in gallery Count Binface ( PA )

The main Westminster parties refused to take part in this contest but could stand if the outcome of the standards investigation into Mr Farage results in another by-election.

If he is found to have broken the rules and a suspension of more than 10 days is imposed, it could trigger a recall petition and the prospect of Mr Farage losing his seat, forcing a second contest.

In the 2024 general election, Mr Farage won Clacton with 46.2% of the vote and a majority of 8,405 over his Conservative rival.

In a message to the people of Clacton, Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has said if there is a by-election triggered as a result of the standards investigation, her party will field a “serious candidate” and “when the real choice comes, the Conservatives will be there and I hope we can earn your support”.

The 34 candidates in Clacton beat the previous record of 26 candidates, set at the Haltemprice and Howden by-election in July 2008, which was triggered by Tory Sir David Davis in his own seat and similarly ignored by the main Westminster parties.

A Nevada man claims a Lyft driver dragged him the length of a football field during a freak mishap that unfolded when his wedding ring got caught in a door handle.

David Morris of Clark County is suing the online ride-hailing company for more than $30,000 in damages over the injuries he suffered in the alleged August 2024 incident, according to the Las Vegas Review-Journal.

His lawsuit reportedly says that the vehicle's door were locked when the unidentified driver arrived to pick him up.

When Morris knocked on a window, the driver allegedly “accelerated at a high rate of speed while plaintiff's left hand was stuck in the door handle, caught by his wedding ring,” the Review-Journal said, quoting from the court filing.

“Plaintiff was dragged and slammed against pavement by defendant John Doe, Lyft driver, before plaintiff was able to get loose,” the lawsuit adds.

David Morris says Lyft should have known its driver ‘was incompetent, unfit and dangerous’ ( Reuters )

Morris reportedly accuses Lyft of negligence, alleging the company should have known the driver “was incompetent, unfit and dangerous.”

In response to an inquiry from The Independent, a Lyft spokesperson said, “We cannot comment on the specifics of ongoing litigation.”

Morris' lawyer didn’t immediately respond to an inquiry.

Lyft's website says that anyone who wants to qualify as a driver in Nevada must have a valid driver's license, be at least 25 years old and pass a criminal background check and a review of their driving history.

Would-be drivers can be disqualified for being listed in the National Sex Offender Registry or convictions for crimes of violence, sex crimes including possession of child pornography, acts of terror and other offenses.

Applicants also have to get a state business license and their vehicles must be no older than a 2010 model, have four doors and five to eight seatbelts, including the driver's, according to Lyft.

Scots across the country have come out in the hope of witnessing a once-in-a-generation solar eclipse – but many were left disappointed when it was covered by a blanket of cloud.

More than 90% of the sun was obscured by the Moon between about 6pm and 8.15pm on August 12, the most it has been blocked above UK skies since the total eclipse in 1999.

It is expected to be the fullest eclipse over local skies until 2081.

Crowds of skywatchers gathered at viewing events across Scotland on Wednesday evening eagerly awaiting the rare celestial phenomenon.

open image in gallery People gathering to watch the solar eclipse on Calton Hill, Edinburgh (Jane Barlow/PA) ( PA Wire )

People packed onto the summit of Calton Hill in Edinburgh, where the city’s astronomical society had organised a viewing event.

People formed a long queue at the observatory gates at the start of the evening hoping to collect a sought-after pair of eclipse glasses – but supplies ran out at about 6pm.

Others had brought kitchen colanders or home-made devices made from cereal boxes or sheets of paper for viewing the eclipse indirectly.

The eclipse began shortly after 6pm, with the “peak” extent of the sun’s coverage happening at slightly different times in different areas of the country.

It peaked in Inverness 7.03pm, when 90.74% of the sun was obscured, while in Edinburgh the peak came at 7.06pm, when 90.71% of the sun was covered.

open image in gallery Sophie Harju and Jack Nevin watched the eclipse with the aid of a colander and home-made pinhole camera (Nick Forbes/PA)

Some western areas of the country saw more than 92% coverage.

Ahead of the eclipse, the Met Office said cloud cover across the country meant people in the bulk of Scotland had a “reasonable chance” of seeing the eclipse.

However, those in the far north west of the country were described as having only a “low chance”.

The forecaster said: “North-west Scotland will see the poorest conditions, while cloud breaks across Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England should allow many to observe it.”

The skies above Edinburgh were covered by hazy clouds throughout the period of the eclipse, with the sun completely hidden behind thick cloud in the 15 minutes or so leading up to the peak.

People could be heard discussing the cloud cover, and whether there would be a gap in time for them to catch a glimpse of the phenomenon.

Cheers then broke out when the sun re-emerged shortly before 7pm, giving people a clear view of the partially-covered sun.

Sophie Harju, 26, and Jack Nevin, 27, both from Edinburgh, watched the eclipse using a homemade pinhole camera and a colander.

open image in gallery The solar eclipse as seen from Calton Hill, Edinburgh (Jane Barlow/PA) ( PA Wire )

Ms Harju, who works in the NHS, said she had not known what to expect, but that it had been “impressive”.

“It was a nice experience to see so many people out. But we maybe were expecting it to get a bit darker,” she said.

“It was a cool event to be part of and nice to see a little bit”.

She added: “This is the biggest Fringe show”.

Mr Nevin, who works in sustainability, said it was “cool” to see so many people come out to see it.

“People like the spectacle,” he said.

“They like when you can metric something, when you can say ‘this won’t happen again until this time’.

“I think people like to get together when there is something they can say is unique and novel”.

open image in gallery The solar eclipse as seen from Calton Hill, Edinburgh (Jane Barlow/PA) ( PA Wire )

David Ellis-Shea, who had come out to watch the eclipse with his wife and eight-month old daughter, said it was a “special moment”.

“We watched the Moon pass slowly in front of the sun, in between broken cloud,” the 34-year-old, who had been wearing eclipse glasses, said.

“We got very lucky to see it perfectly as it crossed over a sort of gap in the clouds. Almost perfect timing really.”

He added it had been important to bring his daughter to see it given the next eclipse of this scale is not due to happen until 2081.

“We were both reflecting that we probably won’t be here for that, but she may well be,” he said.

“And it was just a special moment to share with her, and hopefully she’ll be able to share that moment in the future with her family if she’s still around then, and remember the time she spent with us here.”

Temperatures are expected to soar to 37C in parts of England on Thursday as a fresh heatwave sweeps across the country bringing drought, wildfires and urgent health warnings.

Following persistent hot and dry weather this week, swathes of southern England can expect weather warmer than in the sunny Greek capital of Athens, which is forecast to see highs of 33C.

Temperature highs will peak across Oxfordshire and the Chilterns on Thursday afternoon before cloudy weather brings some relief on Friday. An amber extreme heat warning has been issued, covering part of London.

Almost three-quarters of England is now suffering from drought conditions, affecting 45 million people, with the country now on course to record its hottest ever summer.

open image in gallery The Met Office forecasts highs of 34C in the capital around 4pm. But in some parts outside the capital, temperatures could swell to 37C, they say ( Met Office )

The prime minister has now urged retailers to stop selling disposable barbecues while the dry conditions endure in a desperate bid to curb the risk of wildfires breaking out.

His comments came after chairing a meeting of the Government’s emergency Cobra committee in response to the prolonged spell of exceptionally hot and dry weather.

England and Wales have already seen as many wildfires this year as in the whole of 2025.

The Met Office’s deputy chief forecaster Mike Silverstone said the heatwave was expected to be fairly widespread across England and Wales.

open image in gallery London and Oxford can expect the worst of the weather on Thursday ( Met Office )

“A fairly widespread heatwave is likely across large parts of England and Wales, with hot conditions developing in places,” he said.

“Humidity levels are also expected to increase through the week, which may make conditions feel more uncomfortable, particularly overnight.”

The UK has experienced a consistent North-South split in the weather across this summer, with Scotland and Northern Ireland experiencing heavy spells of rain last weekend.

Rare amber “extreme heat” warnings have been issued by the Met Office for London and parts of the South East, East Midlands, East of England, West Midlands and South Yorkshire from 9am to midnight on Thursday.

The Met Office’s latest forecast for Oxford read: “Temperatures rising quickly under strong sunshine. Feeling hot or locally very hot. As a result, an amber extreme heat warning has been issued, and this covers part of London. Maximum temperature 37 °C.”

open image in gallery All of England is under a heat health alert ( UKHSA/gov.uk )

All of England is under an amber heat health alert lasting until 9pm on Friday.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) warned of risks to the lives of the elderly and vulnerable people and significant effects on health and social care services.

Train passengers are also being urged to only travel if necessary by some operators on Thursday as services will be disrupted because of hot weather.

open image in gallery The Chilterns and parts of Oxfordshire will bear the brunt of the heat on Thursday ( Met Office )

Chiltern Railways and East Midlands Railway issued alerts to “only travel if essential”.

Other operators will either run a reduced timetable or are warning about the potential for short-notice cancellations.

Southern Water has meanwhile applied for a rare drought order which would ban businesses from non-essential water use, including cleaning cars and filling non-domestic swimming pools, saying an “exceptional” lack of rain has threatened supplies in Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.

It warned that 165,000 people in the Southampton West supply area could face restricted supplies.

Met Office five-day weather forecast

Tonight

London and the south east can expect more dry conditions overnight from Wednesday with prolonged clear periods and variable cloud. The Met Office forecasts minumum temperatures of 16C.

Thursday

Very warm becoming hot or very hot across much of England and Wales. Chance of an isolated evening shower in the northeast. Heavier showers for Northern Ireland and Scotland later.

Temperatures quickly rising in the morning in the north west. Some cloud developing by afternoon, with maximum temperatures of 33C. Highs of 37C possible in Banbury, Oxfordshire.

Friday

Mixed conditions, with sunny spells in the south. More cloud, showers and occasional rain in the north. Temperatures near normal, but warm in the southeast.

Cloudier and fresher conditions can be expected in London and the northwest.

Saturday

A continuation from Friday into Saturday with some odd showers expected nationwide.

Sunday

Dry with sunny spells on Sunday, before clouding over from the west late afternoon. A spell of more organised rain could arrive in the north west later in the day as winds strengthen.

Dry with sunny spells in the middle of the country on Sunday, before clouding over through the afternoon.

News.title: Two custodians found shot dead in apparent murder-suicide at Chicago elementary school
News.content:
The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Two custodians have been found shot dead in an apparent murder-suicide at an elementary school on Chicago’s Southwest Side.

Police say that a 48-year-old woman and a 63-year-old man were found unresponsive, each with a gunshot wound to the head, inside Mark Twain Elementary School in Garfield Ridge on Monday, according to local media. They were taken to a local hospital in critical condition and later died, Fox 32 Chicago reported.

The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office told The Independent that the man had been identified as Theottis James Stigger. Officials have yet to release the name of the woman because her family had not yet been notified.

The custodians’ union, SEIU Local 73, said in a statement carried by news outlets: “Two families have lost a loved one and our prayers are with their families, and the staff, students, and families at Mark Twain Elementary School.”

The shooting unfolded Monday afternoon when the 63-year-old custodian, upset that he was going to be relocated from the school, walked behind his co-worker in a hallway and shot her at close range, according to a police report obtained by the Chicago Sun-Times.

open image in gallery Two custodians have been found shot dead in an apparent murder-suicide at an elementary school on Chicago’s Southwest Side ( Google Earth )

The suspected shooter, who had been a custodian for 20 years, then went to the school’s office and shot himself, according to the report.

There were no students at the school as they don’t return from summer break until August 24.

Mark Twain Elementary principal Matthew Moline said in a letter to the school community Tuesday, “We know that this news will be deeply concerning to our families and staff."

“Please know that we are taking this situation very seriously to ensure the safety of our school community,” Moline added in a statement shared by local media.

One concerned parent, Felicia Puga, said she was “appalled” by the shooting.

“This is ridiculous. Fourteen days until school. And janitors, people that are in the school with my child," Puga, whose daughter starts second grade in less than two weeks, told ABC 7 Chicago.

open image in gallery Police say that a 48-year-old woman and a 63-year-old man were found unresponsive, each with a gunshot wound to the head, inside Mark Twain Elementary School in Garfield Ridge Monday, according to local media ( Getty Images )

"Imagine if a new student wanted to come in here to the office. They're with their parents. ‘Hey, we want to register our kid for so-and-so,’ and then this just happens,” Puga said.

Edgar Ochoa, a former student of Mark Twain Elementary, told the outlet that the shooting was “kind of unexpected because when I came here it was never bad around here.”

Ana Medina, who lives near the school and is familiar with the custodial staff, said she feels sorry about what happened.

“I feel bad about them, and we know some of them,” she told Fox 32 Chicago.

Last weekend, at least five people were killed, and another 14 were wounded from gun violence in the Windy City, according to CBS News Chicago. The shooting victims reportedly ranged in age from 17 to 50.

News.content:

Astronomy enthusiasts are in for a double celestial display on Wednesday night, as a solar eclipse is followed by the annual Perseid meteor shower.

According to the Royal Astronomical Society, the shower ranks among the most impressive of the year and should be visible throughout the UK, provided weather conditions remain clear.

Skywatchers can catch the solar eclipse ahead of sunset on Wednesday evening, with the optimal window for spotting Perseids coming in the early hours of Thursday morning, between midnight and 5.30am.

The society noted that early observers may even spot a few meteors shortly after dusk.

Every summer, the Earth slams into a trail of debris from the Swift-Tuttle comet which causes the Perseids.

(PA Graphics) ( PA Graphics )

The meteoroids from the comet, mostly no bigger than a grain of sand, burn up as they hit the Earth’s atmosphere at 36 miles per second, to produce a shooting stream of light in the sky.

The shower meteors are named after the point in the sky where they appear to originate in the constellation of Perseus.

Those hoping to catch the shower have been advised to stay away from artificial light, avoid built-up areas if possible and try to find an unobstructed view of the sky.

Unlike many celestial events, meteor showers are easy to watch and no special equipment is needed, the society said.

Although the shower is set to peak overnight on 12 to 13 August, the shower will be active until 24 August.

Clear skies are forecast for much of the UK on Wednesday evening and into the early hours of Thursday, according to the Met Office.

For those wishing to view the solar eclipse, experts have warned that eclipse glasses are important for safe viewing and that sunglasses are insufficient.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Man Utd beat Leeds on penalties after selfie-seekers bring match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively but try explaining the half-hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only player the vast majority of crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breeched security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but, sadly, it shouldn’t have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold suggested they had taken a dim view.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle 1 Everton 3

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register, or login to an existing, telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.

When you see a + in the tracker it indicates how many other games start at that time.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, one exception is this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football will launch in the two weeks leading up to the start of the Premier League. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.
