Sports.title: Chelsea give Man City just 42 HOURS to complete Enzo Fernandez transfer as Barcelona have £55m Rodri bid rejected
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have told Manchester City they have until 5pm on Friday to seal a £120million deal for Enzo Fernandez.

The Blues vice-captain has been publicly pushing for a move away from the club since March, having flirted with Spanish giants Real Madrid.



Former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca, who has replaced Pep Guardiola at the Etihad, is keen on Fernandez.

Man City are keen to sign a replacement for Rodri, should the World Cup winner leave.



Rodri is desperate to move to Barcelona but City have rejected a bid of £55m from the Catalans.

City value him at £70m but there is a feeling in Spain they can be persuaded to do business if bidding goes over £60m as he has less than a year left on his contract.



And Chelsea’s deadline for Fernandez is likely to strengthen Barca’s hand in negotiations amid fears Maresca could be left without a star midfielder.

Enzo Fernandez criticised Chelsea for their decision to sack ex-boss Maresca in an interview conducted while on international duty in March.

However, the Blues will not budge on their £120m asking price and have informed City that if it is not met before 5pm on Friday, then he will be staying at Stamford Bridge.

Should the worst come to the worst, Elliot Anderson believes he has some of the same qualities as Rodri, so could help fill the gap in midfield.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

England star Anderson, 23, said: “Yeah, I can be quite similar. I can do various things within midfield.

“I’ll play anywhere — creating, driving forward or the other role.”

New Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has said he wants Fernandez to remain at the club.

However, deals for a replacement have been explored in case the 25-year-old were to leave.



Bournemouth rejected a £64million deal for Alex Scott earlier in the window and while the Blues have not returned with another offer, their interest in the England man remains.

City have also explored a move for French defender Malo Gusto.

Chelsea are open to selling the right-back following the arrival of Marco Palestra from Atalanta, however they have placed a £75m asking price on him.

Sports.title: ‘Diver’ Elliot Anderson reveals unique Haaland welcome to Man City after crushing team-mate’s World Cup dreams
Sports.content:
ELLIOT ANDERSON laughed off Erling Haaland calling him ‘The Diver’ as the club-record signing took the plunge at Manchester City.

The new team-mates clashed at the World Cup during England’s quarter-final showdown with Norway in Miami.



Haaland thought Norway had taken a second-half lead only for Torbjorn Heggem’s ‘goal’ to be ruled out by VAR after the striker’s push on City’s £116million signing Anderson in the build-up.

Nearly four weeks on, Haaland showed he had not forgotten the flashpoint, referring to Anderson as ‘The Diver’ on social media.



However, there was no ill feeling as both players reported for pre-season training yesterday.

Asked if he had seen his new team-mate’s post, Anderson, 23, said: “Yeah, it went viral. He’s been calling me a diver!

“It was funny. He has been really good today and has helped me settle in.

“He’s been spot on with me — a really good guy.”

The Three Lions went on to win the last-eight tie 2-1 – only to go out in the semis as Argentina staged a late comeback.

Ex-Nottingham Forest midfielder Anderson has had three weeks off but admits he is still not over the nature of that Atlanta exit.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

He added: “It’s really hard. I’m still sort of struggling with that.

“There are highs and lows in football. It’s about how you bounce back.

“I’ve had three weeks to reflect on it but now is a new season.

“But I take huge confidence knowing I can perform on a World Cup stage.”



Anderson briefly became the most expensive British player of all time this summer — only for England team-mate Morgan Rogers to take the record when he joined Chelsea a few days later.

The City new boy, 23, said: “The fee always will be mentioned. As long as I focus on myself and my performances, that’s all I can do.

“I’m sure I can show people what I can do. But I’m good friends with Morgan, I’m delighted he got the move he wanted.”

Anderson was also chased by Manchester United but never had any doubts he wanted City. And not even Pep Guardiola’s May departure could change his mind.

Anderson said: “I’ve been watching City for the past ten years or so.



“Pep leaving didn’t affect me at all. It’s such a huge club and the players they have are the best.

“I wanted to be surrounded by these sort of players, proving myself on a daily basis.

“I’ve done a bit of work with (City boss) Enzo Maresca on my first day and I’m really looking forward to more — you can see the details he goes into.”

As for United’s interest, he added: “I knew about it. You’ve got a big decision to make — and I’m confident I’ve made the right one.”

Before signing for City, he bumped into former United stars Ryan Giggs and Phil Bardsley while playing golf in Portugal.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

They tried to turn his head towards the red side of town but Anderson said: “We had a nice chat, I had a decision to make and I chose City.”

Asked if they had come close to changing his mind, the new Etihad star said firmly: “No”.

Sports.title: ‘Cannot be at our peak’ – Matthias Jaissle issues urgent transfer plea and reveals fears for Newcastle in Liverpool game
Sports.content:
MATTHIAS JAISSLE’S issued an urgent plea for new signings after Newcastle’s 3-1 thumping by Everton.

Harvey Barnes’ consolation failed to stop Thierno Barry, Iliman Ndiaye and Tyrique George condemning the German to a first defeat in the job.



Despite officially only being in charge a week, the 38-year-old admits his team will struggle to be ready to face Liverpool in the Prem opener unless he gets exactly what he needs.

Jaissle said: “For sure, we cannot be at our peak [against Liverpool], this is clear. We have just been working for a couple of days together, and Liverpool is already next week now.



“We use every day in the best possible way, that’s the only thing we can control to make progress.

“Then, it will be the same with the transfer market. Hopefully, there will be progress there too.



“We have already spoken about it in the press conference, and I think everybody has seen the matches and are smart enough to see the needs in the squad.

“I will always be consistent with my approach – we handle these things internally.

“We are aware of what we need, and as you know, there is still some time.

“It is not a case of just wishing for things to happen and then they happen – that is not the case in football or in life.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“But internally, we are really clear.”

Newcastle have just over ten days to go until they face Liverpool.

Jaissle acknowledged at his official unveiling on Tyneside he has inherited a “vacuum” of leadership in his squad.



But 24 hours later in Edinburgh, it was errors from two of the most experienced players left that sparked this bruising defeat to the Toffees – without new signing Brennan Johnson and Jarrad Branthwaite (hamstring rehab).

And as the skies eerily darkened over Murrayfield, so did the mood within the Toon Army.

Jaissle knows any hopes of eclipsing predecessor Eddie Howe’s success rest on what happens before the window closes in 19 days.

Barry pounced on a wild swing from Dutch defender Sven Botman, 26, to eventually break the deadlock, despite Manchester United target Lewis Hall’s best efforts, with his third of pre-season for Everton.



Then Brazilian midfielder Joelinton’s clumsy challenge on Kiernan Desbury-Hall allowed Ndiaye to double the lead from the spot before the break.

George brilliantly left midfielder Sean Steur, one of the three outfield signings this window aged under 20, for dead with a spin to rifle home a third.

Jacob Murphy teed-up Barnes, two of Howe’s trusted lieutenants, late on but it did little to lift the gloom.

Jiassle hopes to have Benfica full-back Amar Dedic, 23, on board before his St. James’ bow against Leverkusen on Saturday.



And asked if he was confident sporting director Ross Wilson would deliver what he wanted this month, he added: “It’s not a wish concert, not in football, not in life.

“But again, internally we’re really clear.

Sports.title: PSG 2 Aston Villa 1: Villans left to rue missed chances as Madjo, 17, nets in Uefa Super Cup but Doue has final word
Sports.content:
IN the heart of Red Bull country, Aston Villa did not get the lift-off they sought for their latest chapter.

They were not given the famous wings everyone talks about around here – but nor did they have theirs clipped.



And, even in defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, Unai Emery will be heartened by what the future may hold after speaking positively about a “new era”.

This was the fourth Super Cup defeat of the Spaniard’s managerial career and he will wonder quite how.



Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue struck either side of debutant Brian Madjo, 17, to secure the win for PSG.

But Villa, and especially Madjo, had plenty of chances to make this another European night to remember.



Madjo hit the post during a pulsating end to the first half and there were shades of the Villa from recent seasons – the one that loved to blood the noses of Europe’s elite.

That is promising given the team picked for this season-opener in Salzburg was very different to the side that booked a spot in it.

Just five of the players that started the Europa League final in Istanbul were in the XI for this game, and there was the added blow of new signing Alejandro Garnacho missing out due to concussion.

Emery had decided to leave World Cup stars Emi Martinez, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins out of the squad, giving them an extra week’s rest.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And that made for a weakened side, especially after the summer departures of key trio Lucas Digne, Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans.

PSG, in contrast, went strong, with nine of the 11 that beat Arsenal in May’s Champions League final starting.

Fabian Ruiz and Ousmane Dembele were the two to miss out, with new signing Maghnes Akliouche and Warren Zaire-Emery replacing them.

With these two sides just coming to the end of their pre-seasons, there were plenty of loose touches and passes on show in the opening stages.



But the one man who did not look rusty was Kvaratskhelia.

After a summer off where he was watching the top stars shine at the World Cup, the Georgian looked in the mood.

And it was his goal after 20 minutes that broke the deadlock, with a stinging shot leaving Villa keeper Marco Bizot no chance.

It was made by a lovely shimmy from Kvaratskhelia – showcasing hip movement that Shakira would be proud of – and the Villa defenders were left for dead.

PSG tried to kick on from there and a stunning clipped-pass from their star winger set left-back Nuno Mendes away, but no one was there to turn home the cross.



The floodgates did not open for the French side and, instead, Villa roared back into the game.

Madjo was excellent up top, bullying defenders and demonstrating why he cost £10million from Metz in January.

Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors meant he was unable to play until now after a successful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport earlier this month.



And we will surely see plenty of him this season after his goal levelled the game on the stroke of half-time.

John McGinn’s excellent cross to the back post made it and you could not argue that it was more than Emery’s side deserved.

It was a goal that will be remembered for some time.

Firstly, because Madjo became the youngest player to score in the Super Cup, overtaking Patrick Kluivert who was 19 when he bagged in 1996.

And secondly, because a Villa fan went viral on social media for celebrating it with a moony.



Before that it was Madjo feeling red-faced after missing some great chances. He had gone close with a header from another wicked McGinn delivery and struck the post after a rampaging run that left PSG defenders on the floor.

On another day, he could have had a hat-trick and Villa would have been in dreamland.

PSG had the luxury of throwing on Dembele at the break as they tried to regain some control.

It was his France team-mate Doue, however, that put the Champions League holders back in front just after the hour mark.

The winger’s curling effort was originally ruled out for offside, but VAR intervened to reignite the pyro party behind the PSG goal.



Villa were not disheartened by that and debutant Joao Gomes came close to an equaliser with less than 20 minutes to go.

The bench brought energy, too, with Alysson’s cross somehow not turned home by Tammy Abraham when the goal was gaping.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And even right at the death there was one more chance. This time it was Emi Buendia heading wide.

But Luis Enrique’s side held on to become only the second team in history to retain the Super Cup.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Myles Lewis-Skelly shows why Gunners MUST keep him but Gabriel Jesus should be first out of door
Sports.content:
MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY scored a crucial goal to see Arsenal’s pre-season end in victory over Como, with a 1-1 draw being decided by penalties after Alvaro Morata missed from the spot in the shootout.

He opened the scoring by capitalising on a horrific piece of goalkeeping by Jean Butez in the Como goal, cushioning the ball with his head before planting it in the bottom left corner.



Perhaps the most pleasing part of the goal for Arsenal fans will be that he celebrated by forming a heart with his hands to the Gunners in the stands amid rumours that he could be leaving.

Martin Baturina levelled things before half-time, with a wonderful cut onto his right foot before finding the roof of the net – something he seems to like doing to English fans after scoring against the Three Lions at the World Cup.



Bruno Guimaraes impressed on his Arsenal debut in the second half, in which Kai Havertz thought he had found a late winner, only for it to be offside.

With the score level at 1-1, a penalty shootout decided things

This is how SunSport reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the players…

KEPA ARRIZABALAGA – 6

Made one save in the first half before being replaced by David Raya.

Wasn’t massively tested and couldn’t do an awful lot to stop Martin Baturina’s fine leveller.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

THEO JULIENNE – 6

The youngster was really impressive at right-back, offering composure on the ball and solidity in his tackling against a really exciting young winger in Assane Diao.



Found it more tricky against Martin Baturina when he moved to the left and some will blame him for the goal, but he was still impressive.

MARLI SALMON – 8

Really solid at the back for such a young defender, he didn’t look any worse than Gabriel next to him, which is perhaps the biggest compliment you could pay him.

Good on the ball, won more duels than any other Arsenal player, and always on hand to sweep up when his side needed him – plays like a defender twice his age.

GABRIEL – 6

Really good on the ball when playing out from the back, he was physically dominant and solid in defence as ever.



PIERO HINCAPIE – 6

Impressive on the ball at left back, but could have done more in terms of supporting Martinelli going forwards.

Solid though at left back with a number of good tackles, interceptions and recoveries.

MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 8

After a week full of rumours linking him with a move away from the Emirates, he formed a heart with his hands when he was gifted a goal by Como keeper Jean Butez.

If Manchester United or Chelsea were watching this one, they might be a little more interested now after a good all-round midfield showing.



EBERECHI EZE – 7

Played a slightly deeper midfield role than usual, but was still very involved going forwards, coming close with a free-kick early on and being at the heart of most good things from Arteta’s side.

That was until he was hooked early on by Arteta and replaced by Fabio Vieira.

MAX DOWMAN – 6

Really exciting to watch on the right side and you could see flashes of his quality and quick feet.

He was well marshalled most of the time by two or three Como defenders, but still managed to impress in glimpses – it’s easy to forget he is so young.

ETHAN NWANERI – 6

Looked really engaged early on with some great tackles and some really tidy footwork, but more often than not that final bit of end product evaded him.



GABRIEL MARTINELLI – 7

Claimed the assist for Myles Lewis-Skelly‘s opening goal, but was good all round in his play today, with some silky dribbles and bursts of pace down the left side.

GABRIEL JESUS – 4

Seemed to have missed a sitter early on, only to have his blushes spared by the offside flag anyway – that was until he too was hooked early on for Viktor Gyokeres.

That was his only real chance, with limited involvement in the game, but he wasn’t overly impressive by any means.

SUBS:

VIKTOR GYOKERES (GABRIEL JESUS, 32) – 5

Didn’t do an awful lot while he was on the pitch, but he wasn’t on it for a very long time.



A few decent bits of hold up play, but not much else to talk about without much support around him.

FABIO VIEIRA (EBERECHI EZE, 32) – 5

Similarly to Gyokeres, he didn’t have an awful lot of time on the pitch to impress.

A few decent passes and glimpses of his dribbling ability on the half turn, but nothing to write home about.

BRUNO GUIMARAES (MAX DOWMAN, HT) – 7

Already a fan favourite at the Emirates after making a few tackles and some nice passes on his debut.

Chants of “Bruno, Bruno, Bruno” could be heard loud and clear for their new dynamic midfield man, who anchored the Gunners midfield nicely with some great defensive play.



Scored his penalty in the shootout too.

DAVID RAYA (KEPA ARRIZABALAGA, HT) – 6

Did exactly what was expected of him, making a simple save in the second half and being good with his feet.

CRISTHIAN MOSQUERA (GABRIEL, HT) – 6

Almost gave Arsenal the lead with an early second half header that was saved by Butez in the Como goal.

Looked quick and sharp at the back, ready to step up in William Saliba‘s absence if called upon.



MARTIN ODEGAARD (ETHAN NWANERI, HT) – 6

Kept things ticking for Arsenal but struggled a little in terms of creating chances for those around him.

Plenty of good passing and a few nice dribbles but nothing in terms of the end product required to win his side the game.

RICCIARDO CALAFIORI (MARLI SALMON, 60) – 6

Not really caused any problems at the back, but dealt with any Como threat nicely, perhaps should have been more involved going forward when his side needed a goal.

KAI HAVERTZ (VIKTOR GYOKERES, 60) – 7

Came close to giving his side the lead in the second half, but no cigar with a left footed shot that fell wide of the post.

Then thought he’d scored a last-gasp winner with a fine finish, only for the linesman to raise his flag and curtail the celebrations.



Still, he was creative and caused more problems for Como than Gyokeres or Jesus.

MIKEL MERINO (PIERO HINCAPIE, 60) – 6

Plenty of touches, with some good passing and defensive contributions, but is another player who has match-winning moments in him who couldn’t find one today.

NONI MADUEKE (FABIO VIEIRA, 60) – 6

Another who came close to finding a winner for Arsenal, but was just missing that end product required of him.

He was more creative than most in this game with the ball at his feet, but played it safe a little too often.



It felt like everyone in the stadium knew he was going to miss in the shootout.

CHRISTOS TZOLIS (GABRIEL MARTINELLI, 60) – 6

Not overly impactful from the left, particularly when Martinelli had been quite exciting to watch in spells – didn’t see an awful lot of the ball.

Gets a bonus point for his emphatic winning penalty.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

BEN WHITE (THEO JULIENNE, 60) – 6

Pretty much identical to Calafiori on the other side, solid defensively, but not showing enough going forward with the scores level.

JOSH OGUNNAIKE (MARLI SALMON, 88) – N/A

Not enough time to make an impact.

Sports.title: Man Utd player ratings: Mbeumo in peak form ahead of new season but Dorgu a huge cause for concern
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED were held to a 1-1 draw in front of a sell-out crowd at Croke Park – before Michael Carrick’s side won the shootout 5-4.

Bryan Mbeumo was the star of the show as the forward set up Joshua Zirkzee‘s cool finish before Brenden Aaronsen equalised in the 29th minute.



The 82,000 spectators wanted more flare but both managers heavily rotated with the Premier League opening weekend fast approaching in just over seven days’ time.

Noussair Mazraoui converted the winning penalty following a rare spot-kick miss from club captain Bruno Fernandes.



Harry Wilson and James Justin also fluffed their lines, making the Red Devils the first side to triumph in a club football match at Dublin’s historic Gaelic football stadium.

Here’s how SunSport’s Manchester United correspondent Samuel Luckhurst rated the Man Utd players who won the Boyle Sports Cup.

Senne Lammens – 7

His first appearance since his World Cup mistake against Spain. Had no chance for Aaronson‘s leveller on his maiden appearance wearing the number one. Made an excellent early second-half save with his foot.

Diogo Dalot – 6

Captained United and looked match-fit in his first pre-season start. Mainly left most of the running to Amad down United’s right-hand side as he got an hour of playing time.

Leny Yoro – 7

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Started at centre back for the first time in pre-season and had little to do amid United’s dominance. Reacted well to deny Dominic Calvert-Lewin from a near-post cross.

Ayden Heaven – 6

A more confident performance after his dozy defending for Paris Saint-Germain‘s goal on Saturday. Looked assured on the ball, particularly when carrying it into the final third.



Harry Amass – 6

An intense performance on a rare start for the teenager amid United’s willingness to cash in. Amass was aggressive in the tackle and seemed keen to demonstrate his credentials as understudy to Luke Shaw.

Andrey Santos – 6

Had a new partner in Tyler Fletcher and the pair underpinned United’s attacks with neat play. Santos was substituted at half-time after what was his fifth start.

Tyler Fletcher – 5

Asserted himself impressively and he sprayed the ball around expertly. Then he got caught out on the ball and committed a cynical foul before another error led to the Leeds leveller.

Amad – 7

Has got better with each of his three starts. Nearly matched Bryan Mbeumo for directness as he give Leeds youngster Rhys Chadwick a grilling. Seems well placed to start the season.



Joshua Zirkzee – 6

His cushioned volley was well saved by James Trafford but Zirkzee was more clinical the second time, scoring for the first time since December. Strangely, he faded after the goal. His peculiar inclusion was maybe a shop window tactic.

Patrick Dorgu -5

One of four players to have started all five friendlies and Dorgu has probably been the least convincing. Did little of note and made way at half-time. Matheus Cunha lacks minutes but should not struggle to get his place back.

Bryan Mbeumo – 8

United’s start of pre-season did all the legwork to brilliantly create Zirkzee’s goal. Mbeumo should have scored himself but Trafford tipped his drilled strike wide and the Cameroonian also hit the crossbar. 8

Subs

Dan Armer -5



Off the pace for an early Leeds chance in the second half.

Toby Collyer – 5

Came on for the second half and struggled to get a foothold.

Tynan Thompson – 6

Had a shot at goal deflect wide.



Matheus Cunha – 6

Played up front on his return and was industrious.

Bruno Fernandes – 7

Tried to make things happen and hit the crossbar.

Jack Fletcher – 6



Entrusted with the odd set piece. 6=

Noussair Mazraoui – 6

Probably trailing Dalot in the battle to start at right back.

Luke Shaw – 6

Largely kept Wilfried Gnonto in check.



Youri Tielemans – 6

Used the ball prudently.

Claimed a cross and made a decent stop.

Sports.title: Man Utd 1 Leeds 1: Zirkzee continues stellar pre-season form with goal but Red Devils fail to beat Whites again
Sports.content:
SENNE LAMMENS will wear Manchester United’s No 1 shirt this season.

And the Belgian, who wore 31 when he arrived at Old Trafford last term, lived up to his new squad number with a fine save to deny Leeds new boy Harry Wilson.



This was Lammens’ first outing since his howler for his country last month, which ended their World Cup bid at the quarter-final stage to eventual winners Spain in Los Angeles.

Michael Carrick will feel that United’s productive pre-season continued at a sold-out Croke Park.



Lammens lived up to his new squad number as the ‘1’ with a fine save, Leny Yoro made a successful return at centre- half and Andrey Santos’ importance could be gauged by his rest for the second half.

Bryan Mbeumo remains United’s standout performer this pre-season, particularly as he has filled in for Benjamin Sesko up front in all five friendlies.



Mbeumo did the bulk of the legwork for Joshua Zirkzee’s goal, drifting wide and deceiving his marker before racing into the final third and craftily slotting in Zirkzee.

The Cameroonian was denied a fourth goal in three games by the agile James Trafford and then the woodwork. With Sesko a mere spectator again, Mbeumo seems certain to start at Hull City on Saturday week and his country’s absence at the World Cup is already benefiting United.

United were the superior side with the stronger XI in the first half. After Leeds introduced their big guns at the interval, they did the majority of the running until Carrick sent on a handful of regulars on the hour.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



In spite of the promotion of some callow academy hopefuls, United’s squad situation is not too dire as they prepare for the start of the new season.

Lammens, on his first start since his World Cup error cost Belgium, was the only senior goalkeeper. Karl Darlow and Tom Heaton are both nursing injuries.

It is unlikely many inside Croke Park had heard of the three United substitute goalies. Dermot Mee, once a Republic of Ireland Under 21 international, was charitably granted a half-hour runout.

Harry Maguire, booed on his last visit to Dublin with United at the Aviva Stadium, was given a breather after four successive starts.

Mason Mount was left out as he recovers from a foot injury while Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford, Lisandro Martinez and Sesko are scheduled to play against AC Milan in Poland on Saturday.



Bruno Fernandes, Youri Tielemans and Matheus Cunha emerged on the hour after their babysitting stint alongside the 15-year-old JJ Gabriel. Fernandes had a goal chalked off for offside and clipped the crossbar.

Segregation was sensibly in place at Croke Park amid a sizeable contingent of Leeds fans. A couple of supporters dared to don half-and-half scarves.

As peculiar as it was of Carrick to include Zirkzee, Harry Amass and Tyler Fletcher, seven of the United starters could feasibly line up at Hull.

A cynic might suggest the selections of Amass at left- back and Zirkzee in attack were shop window tactics.



Amass played with an aggression befitting a competitive game between the two rivals, eager to stake his claim as Luke Shaw’s understudy. Lewis Hall or Myles Lewis-Skelly may dash those aspirations.

Zirkzee, recalled at the expense of the teenager Shea Lacey, nearly capped an incisive attack with a side-footed volley that James Trafford reacted alertly to.

The Dutchman did not have to wait much longer for another chance and he swept the ball clinically past Trafford from Mbeumo’s precise pass.

Ironically, Mbeumo’s potency up front reduced Zirkzee’s playing time in the two friendlies in Sweden. The Dutchman was deployed as the No.10 on his return to the starting XI.



That rare goal for Zirkzee was his first since Ruben Amorim’s penultimate game in charge against Wolves last December. It will count towards his official haul, of course, nor is it likely to increase his chances of remaining at United beyond the transfer window.

When Carrick made a second batch of changes, Cunha played up front. The preference remains to use an auxiliary striker while Sesko builds himself up after a long-term shin injury.

With a Scot wearing the number 39 and a Brazilian number 17 in midfield, United seemed to be summoning the spirit of the Scott McTominay-Fred ‘McFred’ axis.

Tyler Fletcher got away with one mistake but not the second time and Brenden Aaronson’s equaliser has to be a learning curve for the 19-year-old.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

What United lack in their squad they have offset with stability and preparation. Yet the injury to Mason Mount on Saturday and Fletcher’s error in Dublin reaffirm the need for a specialist defensive midfielder.



However inconsequential this game was, there is every chance it trumped the ratings for Coronation Street or Emmerdale.

Sports.title: Man Utd frustrated by Leeds as Bruno Fernandes reminder sent - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Manchester United and Leeds couldn't be separated despite both having chances to win their pre-season clash in Dublin.

In a game that eventually saw the two sides throw on their headline names, neither of them could find the goal that would've given one side bragging rights over the other with just one outing left before the Premier League season begins.

Joshua Zirkzee was on hand to score the game's opener after some impressive work from Bryan Mbeumo, who was among the game's outstanding players. He waltzed past his opposite number and had half of Croke Park to run into, before laying on his team-mate to finish past James Trafford.

Despite United's dominance it was Leeds who were able to claw their way back into the game, thanks to a lapse in concentration, which allowed Dan James to get hold of the ball before laying on Brenden Aaronson to score.

‌



Mbeumo would see a shot hit the bar just before the break and, once the second-half got underway, Senne Lammens needed to produce a reaction save to deny Harry Wilson.

Man Utd ready to open talks over £30m transfer in perfect response to double blow READ MORE :

By the time the hour mark hit 20 of the 22 players on the pitch had appeared from the bench. But even with Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha pulling the strings the Red Devils couldn't find the winner. The Portuguese star did have the ball in the net before the offside flag denied him and hit the bar in the dying stages as his quality showed, but couldn't provide the winning touch.

Determined to give the thousands of fans a winner, the Boyle Sports Cup went to penalties, and Fernandes' failure to hit the target silenced the stadium. The shootout went beyond the five spot kicks and the unlucky man to miss was James Justin - handing those from Manchester the trophy. Here's five talking points from the Irish capital.

Lack of cutting edge frustrates Red Devils

Across the course of the evening those in red will certainly say they had more possession and time in the final third, but it counts for little if you can't make it count. Alex Cairns came on for James Trafford at half-time, but will not have expected to be so rarely called upon.

‌



View 4 Images Joshua Zirkzee's future is still unclear but he scored the game's opener

If anything it was Dermott Mee who needed to make the more notable saves in the second-half. United were minus Benjamin Sesko, who will look to truly establish himself as the team's striker this season, and a No 9 on form may well have seized on some of the half chances that were created. Fernandes, as he has done some many times, tried to win the match with individual bits of quality, but fell just short. The United talisman was able to smile after his penalty miss, which he'll hope is the only blot on his record this season.

Zirkzee hushes talk of exit

The Dutchman hasn't lit up Old Trafford during his two years at the club, so much so that his days could be numbered amid talk of a return to Italy, possibly with Juventus. He's seen forwards arrive and push him down the pecking order but he was tasked with leading the line and needed less than 20 minutes to score the opener.

Zirkzee profited from some impressive play from Mbeumo, but his first time finish was of a player in confidence. This close to the season managers often look to get players who are going to be part of their plans match sharp - and the Dutchman looks that, even if his future remains unclear.

‌



Leeds ring the changes as depth on show

The Whites came out for the second-half, albeit later than they should, with a team featuring 10 news players as Daniel Farke changed all but one individual. If anything Leeds' side looked better than it did in the opening 45 minutes as Anton Stach, Ethan Ampadu, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and new signing Wilson all ran out.

View 4 Images Brenden Aaronson had Leeds level by half-time

It serves to highlight how, after two summer transfer windows, Leeds have created a squad that looks more capable of dealing with life in the top flight. They won the Championship in 2025 but already have been able to attract the likes of Wilson, who was not short of offers this summer. If the feared second season is about to begin, they look more than equipped for it.

Fletcher's timely reminder

In an area where United want to level up, Tyler Fletcher will learn quickly that notable errors could stick in the mind of his bosses. The teenager is set for more involvement this season, but a lapse in contentration in his own third just seconds before Leeds' equaliser will serve as a frustration.

‌



Central midfield is a position which has already seen two new faces arrive, another could follow, and Fletcher will know that taking risks, failing to look over your shoulder, won't fly once the competitive games come round. The 19-year-old has made plenty of forward strides in pre-season, but Aaronson's equaliser will serve as a reminder of how quickly a mistake can be punished.

View 4 Images Both teams will play once more before the Premier League begins in less than a fortnight

Rivalry in full swing

82,000 packed out Croke Park, Europe's third biggest stadium, and further served to highlight how healthy the Yorkshire vs Lancashire rivalry is. When you consider the two teams didn't play each other in the league for 16 years, the passion for the match-up has more than remained.

Leeds secured a landmark victory at Old Trafford last year, one of the few defeats Michael Carrick had to stomach, and the county divide coupled with years of history ensures that this remains one of England's most hotly contest affairs - and that doesn't change when they cross the Irish Sea.

‌

Sports.title: Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem
Sports.content:
Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem

Arsenal were knocked back by Aston Villa as they eyed Ezri Konsa earlier this summer but are ready to ramp up their interest despite the differences in valuation

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa is on Arsenal's radar this summer (Image: Getty)

Arsenal are ready to reignite their interest in Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa despite the two clubs being someway apart in their valuation of the player.

‌



Konsa has just enjoyed his best season to date, helping Villa win the Europa League and playing a key role in England's World Cup journey, which saw them make the semi-finals.

‌



The Gunners, who have wasted no time in bolstering their ranks following their Premier League success, saw a move for Konsa earlier this summer fail to take off. That owed to the fact they only wanted to pay £30m for the 28-year-old - whilst Villa wanted double that.

‌



Arsenal accept they will need to significantly improve their original offer if they are to sign Konsa, reports the BBC, but any move is also contingent on Villa being prepared to let their defender go, especially if their price isn't met.

Arsenal set to finally break record for transfer sale as bid submitted for Gabriel Martinelli READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta's desire to add a centre-half is likely motivated by William Saliba's injury, which he picked up whilst playing for France. His partnership with Gabriel is among Europe's best, but beyond them there is a lack of elite depth. Konsa's versatility is also seen as a major plus.

The England defender remains on holiday having been afforded an extended break due to his World Cup involvement. He was not in the Villa squad that played PSG in the UEFA Super Cup.

‌



Konsa has two years remaining on his contract at Villa Park and the Midlands side are eager to extend his deal. However his transfer value could drop off in the coming months if he does not agree fresh terms.

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa helped England reach the last four of the World Cup (Image: (Photo by Sarah Stier - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

Unai Emery's side have already shown they are prepared to let their first-team stars leave, especially if they feel the price is right. Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea in a British record move whilst Youri Tielemans was allowed to join Manchester United. Lucas Digne has also returned to PSG.

Article continues below

Arsenal have successfully signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle this summer whilst Greek star Christos Tzolis has also been added. No major defensive additions have been made as of yet.

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho hits new low as club reject free transfer for Man Utd flop
Sports.content:
Jadon Sancho hits new low as club reject free transfer for Man Utd flop

Jadon Sancho is still without a club following his Manchester United exit earlier this summer

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho is still a free agent after leaving Manchester United earlier this summer. (Image: (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images))

Serie A side Fiorentina have reportedly turned down the chance to sign former Manchester United winger Jadon Sancho as his search for a new club drags on. The 26-year-old is still without a new club after leaving Old Trafford earlier this summer, with the new season edging closer.

‌



Reports emerging from Italy state that Fiorentina have passed up the opportunity to bring in the ex-United winger, who spent last season on loan at Aston Villa. Sancho featured 39 times for Villa across all competitions, as Unai Emery's side secured fourth place in the league and lifted the Europa League trophy.

‌



Yet despite that triumph at Villa, he hasn't found a new club yet. Alfredo Pedulla claims Sancho was proposed to Fiorentina a fortnight ago, but the Serie A outfit had reservations about signing him given his performances in recent years.

‌



Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

This isn't the first occasion that Sancho has seen a potential move to Italy collapse, with AS Roma showing interest in acquiring the England international during the summer of 2025.

‌



It was claimed his representatives' fees derailed that transfer to the Italian heavyweights, and negotiations this summer have encountered fresh complications.

Non-league outfit Flixton were compelled to issue a statement earlier this summer after Sancho was seen training at the club's ground.

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho was last with Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Club owner Christopher Garcia denied that Sancho had been on trial and clarified: "Over the past few days, we've seen a number of posts and comments circulating regarding Jadon Sancho's visit to Flixton FC.

"To clarify, Jadon was not on trial with the club and was not involved in any transfer discussions. He simply used our facilities for a private training session to maintain his fitness while preparing for the next chapter of his career.

"We're proud that the quality of our pitch and facilities made Flixton a place where a player of his calibre felt comfortable training, and he is welcome to train at Flixton FC whenever he wishes.

‌



"During his visit, Jadon was nothing but professional, humble, and generous with his time. After completing his session, he happily met with young supporters, posed for photos, signed autographs, and left a lasting impression on everyone who had the pleasure of meeting him.

"Jadon is a world-class footballer who has achieved more in the game than most players could ever dream of. He deserves respect for both his accomplishments and the way he conducted himself during his visit, not the unwarranted criticism that has followed.

"We thank Jadon for choosing Flixton FC as a place to train and wish him every success in the next stage of his career, which will undoubtedly be at a level far above where we currently compete. Our doors will always be open to him."

Sports.title: Luis Enrique's daughter tragedy which helped shape PSG manager's new determination
Sports.content:
Luis Enrique's daughter tragedy which helped shape PSG manager's new determination

Luis Enrique has an emotional connection to European competitions as his Paris Saint-Germain side gear up for a Super Cup clash against Aston Villa

View 3 Images PSG manager Luis Enrique's daughter Xana Martinez sadly died in 2019 (Image: Getty)

Luis Enrique will look to add another European trophy to his already glittering cabinet on Wednesday night as PSG take on Aston Villa in the Super Cup. The Spaniard guided his team to their second-ever Champions League success in May and is still inspired by the tragic death of his daughter Xana.

‌



After the Parisian side beat Inter Milan 5-0 in 2025 to win the competition for the first time, they went on to claim consecutive titles, defeating Arsenal on penalties three months ago. Becoming European champions means PSG will once more play in the Super Cup against the Europa League winners, Villa.

‌



They came back in dramatic fashion to secure a shootout win over Tottenham in last year's edition. For this renewal, PSG are favourites to once again lift the trophy. All eyes will be on Enrique as he looks to tactically outwit his compatriot and former PSG manager Unai Emery in the opposition dugout.

‌



Enrique was hugely successful even before taking the reins in Paris, having won the Champions League and Super Cup with Barcelona in 2015. But behind his intense and fiercely competitive demeanour on the touchline lies a tragic story that shook the footballing world several years ago.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Aston Villa linked with bargain Real Madrid transfer to replace Morgan Rogers READ MORE :

In June 2019, Enrique suddenly stepped down from his role as manager of Spain's national team. The Spanish Football Federation cited "urgent personal matters" and Enrique revealed two months later that his youngest daughter, Xana, had tragically passed away at just nine years of age.

‌



View 3 Images Ex-Barcelona coach Enrique was joined by his daughter Xana after the 2015 Champions League final (Image: Getty )

Xana had spent five months fighting osteosarcoma, a rare and highly aggressive form of bone cancer that primarily affects children, teenagers and young adults.

Enrique said at the time: "We will miss you a lot but we will remember you every day of our lives with the hope that one day in the future we will meet again. You will be the star that guides our family. Rest in peace, Xanita."

‌



There was an immediate outpouring of support as Enrique was lauded for his positive and brave outlook despite the tragedy. He went on to share his inspiring perspective on the nine years he spent with Xana in a multi-part documentary about his life and career.

"My daughter came to live with us for nine wonderful years," he said. "We have a thousand memories of her. You may ask whether I consider myself fortunate or unfortunate. I consider myself to have been fortunate. Very fortunate."

Following his first Champions League success as a manager with his beloved Barcelona, Enrique celebrated on the pitch with the youngest of his three children, Xana, who carried and waved a huge flag.

‌



View 3 Images PSG supporters unveiled a tribute to their manager's late daughter (Image: TNT Sports)

He delivered a touching tribute a decade later following his first historic Champions League triumph with PSG, dedicating the victory to his late daughter and stating she was with him "spiritually." After the French side defeated Inter 5-0, PSG fans celebrated their manager by unfurling a huge tifo inside the stadium that also featured Xana.

Enrique was clearly left emotional by the gesture and responded: "I'm very happy. It was very emotional at the end with the banner from the fans for my family. But I always think about my daughter. It means a lot. It's so nice, but I don't need to win the Champions League to remember my daughter. My daughter is always with us."

Sports.title: MI London's Hundred title defence over despite narrow win over Phoenix
Sports.content:
MI London had the lights turned out on their hopes of claiming a fourth straight Hundred title despite beating bottom-placed Birmingham Phoenix in a nip-and-tuck final men's group match.

As the Edgbaston crowd were treated to a solar eclipse, the visitors knew they needed to win by at least 59 runs to take third position from SunRisers Leeds and qualify for the play-off on their home patch after Phoenix won a crucial toss and elected to field.

A total of 157-6 meant they would progress if they could restrict Phoenix to 98, and three wickets in the powerplay put a spring in their step, Sikandar Raza clean bowling Joe Clarke and Richard Gleeson dismissing Mitchell Owen and Laurie Evans with consecutive deliveries to pull clear as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 14 victims.

However, a solid partnership between Jake Weatherley and Sean Dickson steadied the ship and a Tom Curran wide took Phoenix to 99 and ended MI London's slim hopes.

Dickson (23 from 17) fell lbw to Sam Curran, who then had Weatherley (42 from 31) caught in the deep as the hosts lost momentum but Jordan Thompson (23no from 13) and Rehan Ahmed (23 from 11) took them close before Trent Boult held his nerve, nailing his late yorkers to seal a two-run victory.

Earlier, Will Jacks had made a positive start for MI London before falling to Chris Wood after slicing to deep point. James Vince looked in good touch and Nicholas Pooran announced his arrival by dispatching Tom Helm for 10 runs in two deliveries, but Helm came back to bowl Vince (22 off 12) with a back-of-the-hand slowie.

Rehan then put the brakes on by deceiving Sam Curran with a googly and conceded just three runs from his first 10 deliveries, including six consecutive dots.

Thompson took the key wicket of Pooran (36 from 21) when the Trinidadian holed out to long-off before Jason Roy (26 off 21) became Rehan's second victim. Curiously, boasting figures of 2-7 from 15 balls, the leg-spinner was not called upon to complete his quota.

Raza (17 from 13), Ollie Sykes (23no off 14) on debut and Tom Curran (17no off 9) played useful cameos but MI London's total never looked sufficient to produce the miracle they needed.

With the reigning champions eliminated from the competition, SunRisers Leeds will now play Manchester Super Giants on Friday evening at The Kia Oval, with the prize of a Lord's final against Trent Rockets at stake.

Gleeson said: "To win five games and not qualify when two teams have done the same as us is disappointing, but that shows the strength of the competition and you've got to be on top of your game all the way through - 30, 40, 50 runs can make a big difference."

Welsh Fire and London Spirit's men's teams found themselves in similar positions to their female counterparts - unable to qualify for The Hundred eliminator at The Oval on Friday, let alone Sunday's final at Lord's.

Qualification was statistically possible for Fire but it would have meant a record-breaking margin of victory, their four wins having been close affairs and their losses heavy ones.

But that did not mean a lack of competitive spirit in front of a boisterous Cardiff crowd as the Spirit manfully defended 131 to claim a third win of the campaign.

Fire chose to bowl after winning the toss. And that decision paid off initially, Chris Woakes showing his enduring brilliance up front in shackling the powerful pairing of Jonny Bairstow and Lhuan-dre Pretorius, allowing Lockie Ferguson to benefit from the pressure applied by picking up the South African the ball after he had him dropped.

A score of 34-1 from the powerplay with Bairstow on 22 from 11, was an inconclusive start. Twenty-five balls later and it was 59-3, with the Fire in the ascendancy, Woakes having got rid of Bairstow for 34 from 19, Marco Jansen having bowled 10 dot balls in his first 15.

Liam Livingstone and Dewald Brevis, Spirit's leading run-scorers in the tournament with 233 and 212, both went cheaply, and James Coles, belatedly growing into the tournament, flickered for 29 until all 6ft 8in of Jansen leapt at long-off to flick the ball back in for Tom Kohler-Cadmore to complete the catch.

When Fire batted, they lost Matt Short immediately but Phil Salt and Joe Root cruised along, the feeling that wickets in the bank chasing a middling target would be enough.

At 90-2 off 69 balls, with Jordan Cox flexing his muscles, that thinking seemed sound but the glue disappeared with Root (31 from 31) and Cox (44 from 28). Kohler-Cadmore, Ravindra and Jansen disappeared in the last eight balls to leave the Fire just one hit away, losing by six runs.

Sports.title: Rashford absent in Leeds friendly win but still part of Man Utd plans
Sports.content:
Joshua Zirkzee and Brenden Aaronson scored as Manchester United and old foes Leeds played out an entertaining 1-1 friendly draw at the spiritual home of Irish sport in Dublin, before the concluding shoot-out was edged 5-4 by Michael Carrick's side.

On the eve of the new Premier League season, all the talk was about Marcus Rashford and his reintegration under Carrick, but the 82,000-strong crowd at Croke Park were not treated to a first glimpse of the forward in a Man Utd shirt for over 18 months.

Carrick did hint, however, that he intends to keep Rashford around after he returned from his Old Trafford hiatus in "great spirits", adding "he gives us something a bit different".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Marcus Rashford recently returned to Manchester United's training ground ahead of the new season, after a loan spell at Barcelona. Credit: @rachaelandimogenmufc.

The Man Utd boss also kept a number of other high-profile stars in reserve until after the hour mark, instead choosing to give a raft of youngsters a proper run-out. Full-back Harry Amass turned out to be the pick of the rookie pack.

The introduction of Bruno Fernandes and new signing Youri Tielemans improved efficiencies late on, combining effectively to offer Matheus Cunha some pre-season shooting practice, adding to a lively attacking performance from the lesser-seen Zirkzee.

Fernandes himself was played through by Luke Shaw in the second period, much to the delight of the pro-Manchester United fanbase, who chanted 'Bruno, Bruno, Bruno' for large portions of the night, but his strike was flagged offside. He also hammered the crossbar late on.

Image: Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin heads at goal

Of those senior regulars who did start, Bryan Mbeumo caught the eye, showing impressive intensity to tee-up Zirkzee for the game's opener. Dan James and Aaronson were Leeds' conspirators shortly after to turn home their first of five shots on target. Daniel Farke's side have scored a tidy 10 goals in five pre-season outings this summer, albeit they lacked a little composure in the decisive shoot-out.

The key moments from Croke Park

16: GOAL! Joshua Zirkzee sweeps home a smart, low cross from Bryan Mbeumo.

29: GOAL! Dan James latches onto a punt from James Trafford and baits Ayden Heaven before feeding Brenden Aaronson to equalise.

46: SUBS! Leeds change the majority of their starting XI, with Harry Wilson, Dom Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor among those introduced.

60: SUBS! Michael Carrick sends on Bruno Fernandes, Youri Tielemans and Matheus Cunha.

80: RULED OUT! Fernandes' strike is chalked off after the offside flag is raised. He crashes an effort off the crossbar not long after.

PENALTIES! Wilson missed first for Leeds, but was reprieved when Fernandes also spurned his opportunity. James Justin's miss proved decisive as Noussair Mazraoui netted the winner.

Carrick: Rashford gives us point of difference

Michael Carrick on the return of Marcus Rashford:

"He's our player. He's come back great. I've known Marcus a long time, he offers us something a bit different.

"He's trained only two or three days and it's all normal. He's come back in great spirits. We're looking forward to the start of the season."

Farke: Trafford can be world-class

Daniel Farke on new Leeds signing James Trafford:

"He has the potential to be world-class. If he keeps going like this he will rise to the top.

"We have a feeling he can make a big difference, a top-class No 1 is crucial for the club and I pushed very hard for this transfer. I'm very happy. It was a good debut, we're all delighted to have him."

What comes next?

Sports.title: Guimaraes makes bow and Lewis-Skelly scores as Arsenal held by Como
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes made his first appearance and Myles Lewis-Skelly scored amid speculation about his future as Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Como before winning 4-3 on penalties.

Guimaraes, a £75m signing from Newcastle, was introduced at half-time in the pre-season friendly at the Emirates Stadium after Lewis-Skelly's opener had been cancelled out by Martin Baturina.

Lewis-Skelly's goal, stroked home after cutting out a poor pass from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez, came as he is linked with an Arsenal exit. He celebrated by making a heart gesture with his hands.

Guimaraes received a warm welcome with his introduction but Arsenal were unable to find a second-half winner before emerging victorious in the post-match penalty shoot-out in which Guimaraes and fellow new signing Christos Tzolis were among the scorers.

Image: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes came on at half-time

Mikel Arteta left out Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi despite their returns from World Cup duty this week, but there were first cameos of pre-season from their England and Spain team-mates Eberechi Eze, David Raya, Mikel Merino and Noni Madueke.

Arsenal's attention now turns to Sunday's Community Shield against Manchester City at Wembley before their Premier League curtain-raiser against Coventry, live on Sky Sports, on Friday August 21.

The key moments from the Emirates Stadium

7: CHANCE! Gabriel Jesus misses a sitter as his shot hits the post when it appeared easier to score.

Gabriel Jesus misses a sitter as his shot hits the post when it appeared easier to score. 21: SAVE! Martin Baturina cuts inside from the left flank and forces a low save from Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Martin Baturina cuts inside from the left flank and forces a low save from Kepa Arrizabalaga. 33: GOAL! Myles Lewis-Skelly punishes an error from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez as he strokes home the opener

Myles Lewis-Skelly punishes an error from Como goalkeeper Jean Butez as he strokes home the opener 43: GOAL! Como pull level as Baturina dances between Theo Julienne and Max Dowman before firing home an emphatic finish.

Como pull level as Baturina dances between Theo Julienne and Max Dowman before firing home an emphatic finish. 46: WELCOME! Bruno Guimaraes is welcomed by the home fans as he is introduced at half-time for his first Gunners appearance.

Bruno Guimaraes is welcomed by the home fans as he is introduced at half-time for his first Gunners appearance. 53 WASTE! Martin Odegaard puts a chance on a plate for Fabio Vieira but his shot is saved.

Martin Odegaard puts a chance on a plate for Fabio Vieira but his shot is saved. PENALTIES! Arsenal win the shoot-out 4-3 with Guimaraes among the scorers and Noni Madueke the only player to miss.

Analysis: Salmon shows star potential

The debut of a £75m signing and a goal from the player who may have to make way for his arrival took the headlines, but the performance from Marli Salmon provided another talking point.

One of two Arsenal 16-year-olds to start the game along with Max Dowman, the defender was outstanding, his performance a continuation of a strong pre-season.

He lined up at centre-back, with another teenager, the 18-year-old Theo Julienne, as his full-back, but as Arteta made sweeping substitutions and the personnel around him changed, Salmon remained calm and consistent, earning a standing ovation from fans inside the ground when he finally came off in the 88th minute.

Image: Marli Salmon and Mikel Arteta

Salmon departed having won nine of his 13 duels, the most of any player on either side. He had also completed 42 of his 43 passes, which was, again, a game high. The numbers reflected his confidence and quality both in and out of possession.

Como head coach Cesc Fabregas, himself a former Arsenal academy prodigy, marvelled at his impact alongside Dowman. "Amazing. That's what it's all about. Hale End does an amazing job," he said. And there was also praise from Arteta, who appears to have another credible defensive option. "I think he was exceptional," he said.

Arteta: Bruno was pushing to play

Manager Mikel Arteta on Bruno Guimaraes in his press conference: "He only had three training sessions, but he looked good.

"He was really pushing to play some minutes today.

"I think he wanted to get his debut and the feeling of playing in front of our fans immediately.

"And, yeah, you sense immediately, I believe, a strong connection at play that is going to make us better."

Merino: We're ready for 'another final'

Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino speaking to Arsenal's official YouTube channel: "I think we dominated. The team showed what it is capable of.

"Everyone was in a good level. Honestly, I think we deserved to win; we had massive chances to score.

"We take the positives into the next game and hopefully we can dominate every game like we did today."

On the Community Shield: "It's another final and we want to win, we want to give the fans more happiness.

"But especially for us, we want to compete. Wearing this shirt and this badge means a lot and that's about giving everything and playing to our best capacity."

Sports.title: Chelsea set Man City deadline to bid for Fernandez
Sports.content:
Chelsea have told Manchester City they have a deadline of 5pm this Friday to make an offer for Enzo Fernandez.

City are interested in the midfielder, who shared a strong relationship with Enzo Maresca when he was Chelsea boss.

Chelsea value Fernandez at £120m and he has six years left on his contract.

If City do not meet Chelsea's demands, they do not intend to sell Fernandez in this window.

Barcelona's pursuit of Rodri - which saw them have a £40m bid rejected - has raised the prospect of Manchester City making a late move for Fernandez before the window closes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Mark McAdam with the latest on Rodri's potential move to LaLiga side Barcelona

City have targets in mind for any player who departs and they are in ongoing talks with Lille for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi. They have already signed central-midfielder Elliot Anderson for £116m from Nottingham Forest.

Chelsea have a high valuation for Fernandez but they signed him for around £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window. The summer transfer window closes on Tuesday September 1.

Relations between City and Chelsea are strained after the acrimonious manner of Maresca's departure from Chelsea.

City paid Chelsea £17m in compensation to appoint Maresca this summer. He had resigned with three and a half years to run on his contract at the end of 2025 after being sounded out about succeeding Pep Guardiola last autumn.

Chelsea chose to impose this deadline to avoid the distractions that arose when Maresca stood down with his shock exit announced by the club on New Year's Day.

Their view is that interested clubs have had the best part of two months to make an approach for Fernandez. They want new manager Xabi Alonso and his players to be able to focus on the new season ahead.

Fernandez was dropped by Chelsea for two games in April after he admitted he would welcome living in Madrid.

The player and his agent also apologised for his comments. They had been seeking improved terms at Chelsea.

Real Madrid released a statement earlier this summer denying that they would make an attempt to sign Fernandez.

Barcelona expected to raise bid for Rodri

Barcelona are ready to raise their offer for Rodri - which could lead to Man City making their move for Fernandez before Chelsea's deadline.

City want to keep the 30-year-old but he has entered the final year of his contract.

Barcelona are ready to up their offer to City for Rodri to somewhere in the £50m (€60m) to £60m (€70m) bracket.

City are also aware of interest from Nottingham Forest in Tijjani Reijnders.

Sports.title: Atletico agree deal to sign Spurs captain Romero
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid have agreed a deal in principle with Tottenham to sign Cristian Romero.

The package is in the region of £34.2m (€40m) with add-ons. A 15 per cent sell-on clause is included.

Atletico have been long-term admirers of the Argentina international, and there was an expectation that Spurs would allow captain Romero to depart this summer if the right offer arrived.

The central defender was always believed to have preferred a move to Atletico, with Inter Milan and Spurs' north London rivals Arsenal among the other clubs to have been interested.

Romero's Spurs deal is due to run until the summer of 2029.

The 28-year-old was sent off twice last season during Spurs' Premier League relegation battle. He then missed the end of the campaign due to a knee injury.

Romero received criticism from supporters when he appeared to be set to watch his boyhood club Belgrano play River Plate in the Argentina Primera Division Apertura final instead of being at Tottenham's crucial last game against Everton. Romero did, though, attend the final game of the season, in which Spurs secured Premier League survival.

He has made 124 appearances for the club over five seasons, scoring 12 goals and being shown four red cards in the Premier League.

Spurs had appeared to lay the groundwork for Romero's exit this summer following the arrivals of defenders Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi.

'Spurs not getting value for Romero'

Spurs are set to take a lower fee for Romero than what they received for teenage defender Luka Vuskovic, who joined Brighton in a club-record £50m deal earlier this summer.

Speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, which will be available to listen to from midday on Thursday, Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge said of Romero's imminent exit: "Spurs are not going to get the value for a player of his ability.

"Luka Vuskovic, who didn't make any competitive appearances for Spurs, will be sold for more than what the club's captain will go for because he's gone to a Premier League club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Romero's last game for Spurs ended in tears as he suffered a season-ending injury in the loss at Sunderland

"I think it's best for all parties that Romero leaves. I think 99.9 per cent of Spurs fans would agree with that.

"On his day, there aren't many better - he doesn't make any mistakes for Argentina, but in terms of Tottenham it just feels like it's his job.

"He adores Argentina, and there's nothing wrong with that, but it feels as if Tottenham is a bit of a chore for him and it's gone a bit too much that way."

Could Romero have joined Arsenal?

Earlier this month, one source had told Sky Sports News that Arsenal had looked into Romero as an option to bolster their centre-back options.

However, it never progressed beyond interest, with Spurs reluctant to let their captain join a Premier League side, let alone their fiercest rivals Arsenal.

"There was talk that Romero would have happily accepted a move to Arsenal," Bridge told Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast.

"There were no club-to-club talks on this, but when you hear that then that's the final nail for Tottenham supporters."

The north London rivals tend not to do transfer business with one another. The last transfer negotiated between the two clubs came 49 years ago when goalkeeper Pat Jennings joined Arsenal from Spurs in a deal worth a reported £45,000.

O'Hara: Time for Romero to move on

Also speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, ex-Spurs midfielder Jamie O'Hara said of Romero: "He's a bit of a liability. When he plays, he costs us games, points and red cards.

"I just think his attitude towards the board and the way he was, I just think it's, 'All right, thank you, and we're going to move on'.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara called for Tottenham to sell Romero

"We've finished 17th the last two seasons, and he's been involved. He was captain last season, and the way he acted at the end of the season, when he got injured, and we all saw him crying, that wasn't for Tottenham; it was more for Argentina and his World Cup.

"And then he goes to Argentina on the last day of the season, and everyone's like, 'Where's Romero?' So that situation for me needs to be put to bed. I don't think we need any of that bad publicity around us.

"Get as much as we can for him; let him move on. We've got back-up now with Van Hecke and Senesi, so thank you, see you later."

Spurs are set to make a loss on Romero, who joined from Atalanta for around £42m in the summer of 2021.

O'Hara said of Atletico's £34.2m deal for Romero: "The problem is there's a premium for English clubs, who will pay over the odds for people with European clubs inflating the fee.

"The problem is if you're going to go and sell him to Atletico Madrid, they haven't got the money.

"If we were selling him to Man Utd, we could probably get £60m-70m for him. But the problem is if you sell a player to Europe, they just don't have the money that the Premier League clubs have, so you have to accept that it's going to be a lesser fee than what maybe you think you can get for him.

"He wants to go to Atletico Madrid. He just feels like an Atletico Madrid player. I just feel like you've just got to take that one on the chin and move on from it."

Romero's exit signals new era at Spurs

Image: Romero is set to leave Spurs after five years at the club

Speaking on Sky Sports' Tottenham summer special podcast, Sky Sports News senior football news editor Lyall Thomas said:

"Quite a top figure in the football industry said to me, 'Go and watch Romero's role in the second goal in Spurs' 3-0 defeat to Nottingham Forest at home last season'.

"I watched him, and it was arms in the air, not tracking the player back who ended up scoring, which contributed to the goal.

"That was Spurs when they needed their captain the most, and he just wasn't there in that moment, so that says it all.

"It's time to move on from that era of Spurs and into the new era.

"This has been shown by some of the players they've brought in, which is not just to have an impact on the field but to have an impact on the dressing room and sort that area of the club.

"It's a move that suits Romero to go and work with his compatriot [Diego] Simeone. I can imagine they will suit each other down to the ground. It just fits. The planets are aligned on this one."

Sports.title: Doue silences Madjo-mania as PSG beat Villa to win Super Cup
Sports.content:
Desire Doue scored the winner as champions of Europe Paris Saint-Germain beat Aston Villa 2-1 to win the UEFA Super Cup.

The 21-year-old raced in behind the defence and restored the lead for the Ligue 1 side to ensure they retained the trophy but Villa went down swinging in what was a highly-contested fixture at the Red Bull Arena in Salzburg.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia had initially given PSG the lead after cutting inside from the left and wrong-footing Marco Bizot with his well-taken effort (20) but a goal on his professional debut for 17-year-old Brian Madjo sparked Villa into life.

The forward became the youngest player to score in the Super Cup after shrugging off the challenge from Willian Pacho to volley the equaliser home and arguably should have had more to his name, having seen three other chances sail just wide of the target.

Image: Brian Madjo of Aston Villa celebrates scoring against PSG

Villa were without key players Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emiliano Martinez due to their extended post-World Cup breaks but the gaps left by senior players provided the likes of Madjo and 19-year-old George Hemmings with a platform to shine.

The two teenagers looked at home among world-class opposition and the latter came close to responding to Doue's strike seconds after Villa conceded, only for Matvey Safonov to make a fine stop to deny him.

Image: Desire Doue celebrates after scoring what proved the winner for PSG against Aston Villa in the UEFA Super Cup

Luis Enrique's side would hold on to start the 2026/27 campaign with silverware but they were given an almighty scare by Unai Emery and his new-look squad, in a similar fashion to the 5-4 thriller that played out in the Champions League when the sides last met in 2025.

The key moments from Red Bull Arena Salzburg

20: GOAL! Kvaratskhelia opens the scoring for PSG

Kvaratskhelia opens the scoring for PSG 28: CLOSE! Madjo's header curls just wide of the target

Madjo's header curls just wide of the target 35: MADJO MISSES! Another shot from the young striker whistles just wide

Another shot from the young striker whistles just wide 41: MADJO HAS TO SCORE! Madjo's header balloons over the bar from close range

Madjo's header balloons over the bar from close range 45: FINALLY! Madjo makes history and becomes youngest Super Cup goalscorer

Madjo makes history and becomes youngest Super Cup goalscorer 62: GOAL! Doue restores PSG lead

Doue restores PSG lead 64: SAVE! Hemmings has chance to equalise but Safonov saves

Emery: We must feel proud of this performance

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery speaking to TNT Sports:

"With a loss, you can never feel happy but how we compete, how the players respond on the field for 90 minutes. And our chances to score, we must feel really very proud of what we have done today."

On the performances of Brian Madjo and George Hemmings: "Their experiences and having days like today are very important.

"They show how are they are learning after their hard work. This is the way. We decided before the game how we wanted to play this game; we have worked the players in these positions."

Sports.title: Birmingham Phoenix win battle to avoid Hundred wooden spoon vs MI London
Sports.content:
Birmingham Phoenix prevailed in the battle to avoid the wooden spoon in The Hundred women's competition as Ellyse Perry's composed half-century condemned MI London to a sixth defeat of a chastening campaign.

Both teams had managed a solitary victory heading into this fixture but a fifth-wicket stand of 66 between Perry (62no from 39) and Pakistan skipper Fatima Sana (36 from 32) ensured Phoenix halted a three-match losing streak to end with a consolation win and finish seventh in the table.

Set a modest target of 122, the hosts were wobbling at 48-4 after Jemima Spence and Davina Perrin fell in the powerplay and England duo Alice Capsey and Emma Lamb were dismissed cheaply, with Kirstie Gordon (2-20) making early inroads with her left-arm spin.

But Perry found a willing partner in Sana, who eventually fell to Nicola Carey when just seven runs were required, and the Aussie superstar secured the win with six balls to spare.
