Sports.title: Désiré Doué does the business as PSG edge Aston Villa to lift Super Cup
Sports.content:
Luis Enrique says it doesn’t matter what sport he is playing – football, tennis, padel or parchis, a board game – he wants to win every game, all the time. In Paris Saint-Germain, he has built a winning machine, the back-to-back Champions League victors maintaining their habit by conquering Aston Villa in an absorbing Super Cup contest in Salzburg. For PSG, after the joy of Munich and Budapest, three months ago, does a three-peat in Madrid in May beckon? They will surely go close.

Aston Villa more than played their part in an enthralling showpiece, Brian Madjo becoming the competition’s youngest scorer after the 17-year-old cancelled out Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s opener. Villa had chances to gain the lead but Désiré Doué was the match-winner, the forward picking his spot after beating Villa’s offside trap. The goal was initially disallowed but, after a VAR review, Omar Artan, the Somali referee handed the game by Uefa after being denied entry to the US to officiate at the World Cup, awarded it after replays showed Matty Cash played Doué onside.

Before kick-off, the sights and sounds were in effect an extension of Villa’s victory in Istanbul, a party atmosphere raining down from the 6,000-strong Villa following. There were huge cheers when Unai Emery’s face appeared on the big screens in opposite corners after the teams were read aloud and hearty roars for the £38m arrival João Gomes and Madjo, the hulking forward handed his full Villa debut. Madjo’s inclusion felt particularly ominous for Tammy Abraham, the striker signed seven months ago, his £18.3m permanent arrival yet to pay dividends. A claret and blue mosaic formed behind Marco Bizot’s goal as Jeff Beck blared over the speakers. Villa supporters crooned to Erasure and chanted the name of their superb captain, John McGinn.

“We won’t be in our best moment,” Emery said on the eve of the game but his side were almighty fun; some good, some bad, just as he predicted. Only five players from their memorable victory over Freiburg remained in Villa’s XI, though Emi Martínez, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins are still on holiday. Boubacar Kamara made his first start since sustaining a serious knee injury against Tottenham in January.

Emery could also finally unleash Madjo in a competitive game for the first time since his £10m arrival from Metz in January, Villa winning an appeal at the court of arbitration (Cas) to register him after Fifa prohibited him from playing. Only João Pedro, for Chelsea, had scored more goals in pre-season than Madjo but his equaliser here was on the grandest stage yet after goals against Walsall, Real Sociedad and Indonesia All Stars. Here was Madjo against Willian Pacho and Marquinhos, the PSG captain and one of the most decorated defenders in the world.

Kamara drilled wide in search of the opener but PSG seized the lead on 20 minutes through Kvaratskhelia, who had the summer off with Georgia failing to reach the World Cup. Madjo’s clunky control allowed Vitinha to take hold of the ball and pass the baton on to Désiré Doué. Then Kvaratskhelia took charge, jinking inside Matty Cash and blasting his shot into the top left-hand corner at Bizot’s near post. Kvaratskhelia blew a kiss down the lens of the nearest television camera. Six minutes later, it should have been 2-0 after more Kvaratskhelia brilliance, but PSG could not apply the finishing touch. Nuno Mendes galloped on to Kvaratskhelia’s flipped pass down the left flank but the Portugal defender’s cutback evaded four red and blue shirts.

View image in fullscreen Brian Madjo punches the air after scoring for Aston Villa on the stroke of half-time. Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/Reuters

A couple of minutes later came the first of Madjo’s hat-trick of chances from McGinn’s cunning crosses before the teenager levelled. Madjo glanced at a replay after misdirecting a free header and then overcooked a shot when looking for the far corner after George Hemmings got the better of Achraf Hakimi. Another flunked header followed when McGinn twirled clear of Kvaratskhelia. With the half-time whistle looming, Madjo made amends, dispatching a left-footed volley into the roof of Matvey Safonov’s goal after meeting another brilliant cross from McGinn. As McGinn’s flighted ball flew towards the back post, Pacho clung to Madjo for dear life, but Madjo kept him at arm’s length to ripple the net.

Ousmane Dembélé replaced Maghnes Akliouche, a £43m buy from Monaco, at half-time, leaving PSG only shy of Fabián Ruiz from the starting lineup that overcame Arsenal in Budapest in May; the Spanish World Cup winner later replaced João Neves. But it was Villa who registered the first chance of the second half, McGinn working Safonov after Madjo cleverly spread play. A few minutes later, Neves released Dembélé but the France forward ran out of road, allowing Bizot to intervene.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

PSG would regain the lead just after the hour when another pass from Dembélé unlocked Villa’s defence, exposing an imperfect offside line. Dembélé zipped a pass into the right channel and, while Ian Maatsen and Pau Torres raised their hands and Doué’s goal was initially ruled out, semi-automated offside exposed Cash.

Villa still had chances to level. Warren Zaïre-Emery’s extraordinary block prevented Gomes from a near-certain debut goal. Safonov repelled a Hemmings strike and the substitutes Alysson and Abraham almost combined to devastating effect but Abraham did not gamble in the box, much to Emery’s frustration. Perhaps Villa will, as McGinn suggested, prove everybody wrong – again.

Sports.title: Anderson still pained by England defeat but ready to shine at Manchester City
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson has admitted ­England’s World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina still pains him, but is hoping to use the confidence from his performances at the ­tournament to inspire the start of his Manchester City career.

Anderson will probably make his debut when City play ­the Premier League winners, Arsenal, on ­Sunday at the Principality ­Stadium in ­Cardiff for the Community Shield.

“It’s really hard,” Anderson said of England’s loss. “I’m still sort of ­struggling with that. There are highs and lows in football. It’s about how you bounce back.

“I’ve had three weeks to reflect on it, but now is a new season, you have to move forward.

I take huge confidence knowing I can perform on a World Cup stage. I hadn’t played in anything as big as that yet. That was a really good test for me.”

The 23-year-old is likely to become a significant figure in City midfield because of Barcelona’s interest in signing Rodri. A new £51m bid was made by the La Liga side on Wednesday, as they try to seal a deal for the 30-year-old. If the Ballon d’Or ­winner does depart, City’s new No 5 will be expected to be part of the plan to replace him in the middle of the park. Asked if he is similar in style to the Spaniard, Anderson said: “I think so. I can do various things within ­midfield and I’ll see where I get used.

“I’ll play anywhere. Creating things, driving forward or the other role if they ask me to do that.”

Anderson joined from Nottingham Forest for what was briefly a record £116m fee [Morgan Rogers’s £117m move to Chelsea soon eclipsed it] for a British player – City had a ­longstanding interest in him while Pep Guardiola was in charge. Due to his extended World Cup exertions with England, the former ­Newcastle midfielder is yet to feature for City under their new head coach, Enzo Maresca.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Guardiola’s departure, though, did not made him debate his decision. “It’s such a huge club and the players they have are the best. I want to be surrounded by these sorts of ­players, proving myself on a daily basis.

“[Kevin] De Bruyne was always the player I looked up to over the last 10 years. I loved watching him. To be here at the same club and playing where he played is special.”

Sports.title: Manchester United enjoy trip to Dublin with penalty shootout win over Leeds
Sports.content:
With blazing sunshine fading over a hot Dublin day, this penultimate friendly for Manchester United and Leeds United felt like a pre-season game on a far continent, not one staged a few hundred miles from the teams’ home across the Irish Sea.

The phoney-war element is always present whatever the locale, as ­players sharpen technique and fitness, so when Joshua Zirkzee’s instant left-foot shot met Diogo Dalot’s zipped-in cross and James Trafford saved low, all involved could be satisfied.

Even better for Michael Carrick’s men ensued: Bryan Mbeumo raced along the left and served the ball to Zirkzee who, again, hit a first-time effort that this time beat Trafford to his right.

Leeds had been scythed open, their right-side defenders, Jayden Bogle and Sebastiaan Bornauw, rendered awol by a lightning attack straight from the Carrick-Steve Holland ­training ground playbook.

Daniel Farke’s switch to a 3-5-2 at half-time of November’s 3-2 loss at Manchester City is credited, rightly, with saving their top-flight status, and the manager’s job.

Yet it can cause a retroactive-mode if the wingbacks retreat into a five-man rearguard. After Bogle and Rhys Chadwick did so, Mbeumo’s attempt, after one more United foray, underlined the problem.

More proactive, then, were two Ao Tanaka throw-ins that dipped into the area and posed those in red to scramble. When Leeds came straight back at them, a Tyler Fletcher shimmy backfired, and they profited.

The midfielder was robbed by Dan James who flipped the ball into the area where Brenden Aaronson stroked past Senne Lammens, who was helpless. So, too, Trafford when a Mbeumo rocket beat him, the bar saving Leeds, as, along the touchline, replacements prepared to enter for the second period.

Quick Guide Lewis-Skelly scores in Arsenal friendly as transfer speculation continues Show Myles Lewis-Skelly appeared to underline his commitment to Arsenal by setting aside transfer speculation to score in Wednesday’s 1-1 friendly draw with the Italian club Como. The 19-year-old has been linked with Chelsea and Manchester United amid uncertainty over his future. Starting in midfield, he capitalised on an error from the Como goalkeeper, Jean Butez, to put the hosts ahead in the 33rd minute at Emirates Stadium. Lewis-Skelly then made a heart sign to the crowd as he celebrated before tapping the club badge on his shirt on his way back to the centre circle. The England international signed a five-year contract with Arsenal last summer but his long-term future has come under scrutiny since he fell behind Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapié last term to become Mikel Arteta’s third choice left-back. While he started only five Premier League games across the course of the campaign, he enjoyed an end-of-season resurgence in centre midfield. Arsenal, however, are well-stocked in that position after signing Bruno Guimarães to join Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard and the World Cup winners Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Guimarães, who joined from Newcastle in a £75m deal, was introduced at half-time against Como to make his debut, while Lewis-Skelly was replaced in the 62nd minute by Merino. The Premier League champions were pegged back by Champions League-bound Como, who are managed by the former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fàbregas, when Martin Baturina equalised in the 43rd minute. But Arsenal won the penalty shootout 4-3, with Guimarães and his fellow summer signing Christos Tzolis on target. PA Media Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Before the game, Carrick had issued an update on those not involved. “Marcus [Rashford], Licha [Martínez] and Kobbie [Mainoo] aren’t quite ready yet,” he said. “We’re ­preserving them for this weekend [against Milan in Wroclaw].”

Missing, too, were Mason Mount, as a precaution, Tom Heaton, whose problem is being assessed and Harry Maguire, who joined training on Wednesday.

“Tonight is going to be ­historical,” screeched the enthusiastic PA announcer when billing this ­inaugural meeting between two ­English clubs at the cavernous stadium.

View image in fullscreen Brenden Aaronson slots home Leeds’s first-half equaliser. Photograph: Stephen McCarthy/Sportsfile/Getty Images

But Carrick’s three half-time changes were hardly stellar names to please the capacity crowd. Off went Patrick Dorgu, Andrey Santos and Mbeumo for the fringe players, Toby Collyer, Daniel Armer, an 18-year-old debutant, and Tynan Thompson, given a first outing since joining recently.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Farke’s changes ran to 10, with only Bornauw surviving, so now the question was how disjointed the contest might be. Encouragingly, Harry ­Wilson and Alfie Cresswell tested Lammens, then slick Zirkzee footwork took him in on goal.

But further disruption followed when Carrick made six more changes, including the introduction of his captain, Bruno Fernandes, Youri Tielemans, his new £35m midfielder, and Matheus Cunha, who spearheaded the 4-2-3-1.

The result: a long lull before ­Lammens repelled a James Justin rasper, a Fernandes strike was ruled offside and the same player clipped the bar before penalties, to decide the Boyle Sports Cup, arrived.

Before the final whistle five fans rushed on for selfies with Fernandes and Tielemans – youngsters, sure, but a concerning security breach, ­especially as a sixth followed.

View image in fullscreen A capacity crowd of more than 80,000 turned up at Croke Park. Photograph: Stephen McCarthy/Sportsfile/Getty Images

United won the shootout 5-4, Noussair Mazraoui netting the decisive kick, and the teams wandered away offering scant clue how their 2026-27 season will be.

The pre-season results of United now read this victory, 1–1 against Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday, 2–1 (Atlético Madrid), 5–0 (Rosenborg) and the 1–0 loss to Wrexham on 18 July. After this defeat, Leeds’s record is 2-0, against RB Leipzig, 4-2 (Liverpool), 1-0 win (Sunderland), and the 3-2 defeat, also to Wrexham, on 26 July.

Leeds finish their preparation by hosting Augsburg, while United make the trip to Poland. Last term they ended third, 24 points ahead of Leeds in 14th. Given the former’s thus far underwhelming transfer window – only Tielemans and Santos as major signings – they would take the same finish, as would Leeds, surely, as survival will be their priority.

Sports.title: Xavi Hernández appointed head coach of the Netherlands on four-year contract
Sports.content:
The former Barcelona head coach Xavi Hernández has been appointed the new head coach of the Netherlands. The 46-year-old Spaniard has agreed a contract to lead the team through to the 2030 World Cup.

He replaces Ronald Koeman, who stepped down following the Netherlands’ last-32 defeat by Morocco at this summer’s World Cup.

Former Barcelona midfielder Xavi won the World Cup as a player with Spain in 2010 and also lifted the European Championship in 2008 and 2012. He guided Barça to the La Liga title in 2023 after beginning his managerial career with Qatari club Al Sadd.

“I consider it a tremendous honour to become head coach of the Dutch national team,” he said in a statement released by the Dutch Football Association (KNVB).

“As someone who received his training at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, among others, I feel a special connection to Dutch football. You could say that I am a bit of a son of Dutch football.”

Xavi’s appointment marks his first return to management since leaving Barcelona in 2024. He took over the Catalan club in November 2021, also succeeding Koeman, after making 767 appearances for the club.

“The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that also appeals to me enormously: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion, and conviction,” he said. “Of course, the most important goal is and always will be to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy. The potential for this is there, as well as a solid foundation to build upon.”

Former Liverpool head coach Arne Slot walked away from talks about replacing Koeman after saying he wants to remain in club football. His link to the role did not get beyond an initial approach.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“At this stage in my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day, something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team,” Slot told Voetbal International. “And [it is] why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like.

“I have enormous respect for the national team and for the KNVB [Dutch Football Association] and can only be positive about the professional manner in which the talks proceeded that week. For now, I believe club football still has a lot to offer me.”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi has ‘quite a few doubts’ about football future after death of his father
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has hinted that the end of his career may be near after ­admitting to “quite a few doubts” about his football future following the death of his father.

Jorge Messi died last week at the age of 68 in Rosario, Argentina, after a long illness, with his health during this summer’s World Cup appearing to take a toll on Argentina’s 39-year-old captain.

In a tribute on Instagram on Wednesday, Messi wrote: “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you. I don’t know how ​to move forward. I only played football and now I have quite a few doubts about whether I’m going to keep doing it for much longer.

“You were by my side from the beginning; there was so little left until the end. Why couldn’t you hold on just a little longer so we could finish it together?”

Messi ​spent time with his ‌father after the tournament, where Argentina were beaten in the final by Spain, before rejoining his club side, Inter Miami, making his Major League Soccer return against Columbus at the start of this month.

Jorge had been a constant presence during his son’s career from his earliest days at Barcelona, with the World Cup the first time he had been absent from a major tournament. Messi revealed that his father, despite his deteriorating condition, had urged him to play for La Albiceleste in their ultimately unsuccessful attempt to defend their title.

“You always asked me to play in the last World Cup and a few days before it started was when you got worse,” he wrote. “It was the first time you weren’t going to be at a tournament … Every time a match ended, I would ‌wait and hope for your message. That’s when I realised how real the situation was.”

After tearfully celebrating the opening goal of his hat-trick against Algeria in the group stage, Messi had explained he was going through “a few difficult, complicated days” because of “something unrelated to football”. he said he ran out of energy in final.

“My legs couldn’t go on any more,” he wrote. “This time I tried to push myself beyond my ​physical limits, but I couldn’t. ​I never felt well … We weren’t champions, ​but you don’t know how much we enjoyed every match. Once again, you were ​right: I had to ‌be there and play ​it.”

Messi has earned 207 caps for Argentina since making his debut for his country in August 2005. He captained the side to World Cup glory in 2022, matching the achievement of Diego Maradona in 1986, though like Maradona he fell at the final hurdle when attempting to win back-to-back titles.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Messi did, though, break the record for total World Cup goals, with his strike against Egypt in the last 16 his 21st at the tournament and his 125th in all for Argentina. His World Cup tally was later surpassed by France’s Kylian Mbappé in the third-place playoff.

With his future uncertain it remains to be seen whether he will add to his remarkable CV of honours, which includes 10 La Liga titles, four Champions Leagues and eight Ballons d’Or in addition to that World Cup triumph in Qatar.

But he promised to honour his father’s memory through his own children: “I’m going to miss you so much, but you will always be present, especially in the upbringing of my children, because I will teach them and raise them the way you raised me.”

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 6: Chelsea
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 3rd (NB: this is not necessarily Billy Munday’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 10th

Prospects

After a season of struggle and regression, with two head coaches and two spells under a caretaker, there is cautious optimism that this campaign will bring something like stability. Much of that optimism centres around the appointment of Xabi Alonso, an elite manager with something to prove. There is also an expectation that the young players brought in as part of BlueCo’s £1.8bn splurge in recent years are beginning to come into their best years. There is no European football to complicate the schedule and a return to the Champions League by finishing in the top four or five would suffice for now. More importance will be placed on the domestic cups after a season without trophies.

Alonso’s squad is more rounded than what Enzo Maresca or Liam Rosenior had at their disposal. Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers bring quality to positions where Chelsea were lacking it – at centre-back and out wide. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson – the “uncs” as Tosin Adarabioyo has called them – will contribute as much off the pitch as on it. The signing of Marco Palestra, a specialist wing-back, suggests Alonso wants to be tactically flexible. He has used a back four and a back three in pre-season.

What about Cole Palmer? For so much of his time at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea’s form has been tied to his. When he has struggled to be 100% fit, the team have suffered too. After being omitted from England’s World Cup squad, Palmer had a seven-week break and sought advice from a specialist on the groin injury that hampered him last season. “I got bored after six weeks,” Palmer said after returning for pre-season. “I was sat in Marbella thinking: ‘I want to go back in.’” With the prospect of linking up with Rogers and João Pedro, who has also had a good rest, Palmer has plenty of reasons to be excited.

Off-field picture

July ended with Chelsea being fined £10m and receiving a suspended transfer ban over multiple violations of transfer rules under the ownership of Roman Abramovich. An appeal from the club saved them from a six-point deduction. Chelsea were deemed compliant with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules for the three-year period ending in 2025 despite posting an English record £262.4m pre-tax loss for the 2024-25 season. They have not been cowed by failure to qualify for Europe and have spent over £300m on new signings. For the fourth year in a row, Chelsea look likely to start the season without a front-of-shirt sponsor.

Owner-fan relationship

Supporter protests against the ownership of Todd Boehly’s BlueCo have been a frequent sight on matchdays, including before May’s FA Cup final defeat by Manchester City. There have been reservations about the club’s youth-oriented transfer policy from the start and last season’s failings prompted the co-owner Behdad Eghbali to admit the need “to add more ready-made players” to the squad. Whether fans were expecting the arrivals of Welbeck and Henderson is another question. The introduction of a ticket ballot system for home games has also been unpopular with regular match-going supporters.

The manager

It was a bit of a coup for Chelsea to secure Alonso’s services this summer, especially given the Liverpool job was available. The Spaniard has a reputation to rebuild after his dream job at Real Madrid ended in the sack after six months. “I got a scar, now it is healed,” he said. Alonso’s record of developing young players, such as Florian Wirtz, at Bayer Leverkusen while simultaneously delivering silverware is a match made in heaven for the Chelsea hierarchy. One detail to note: Alonso has been appointed as manager, rather than head coach like his predecessors. He has also brought in Austin MacPhee, Aston Villa’s set-piece guru.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Chelsea broke the British transfer record to pry Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Chelsea went one better than Manchester City’s £116m signing of Elliot Anderson by bringing in Rogers, who had been linked with Arsenal, for a new British record fee of £117m. Although he started England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina on the right wing, Rogers has thrived for Aston Villa playing largely off the left and should slot in there nicely at Chelsea. The 24-year-old has proved himself in the Premier League and his best-buddy relationship with his former Manchester City youth teammate Palmer is a major plus. “I can see them linking really well,” Alonso said.

Stat attack

Has anyone checked Chelsea haven’t built a squad of Benjamin Buttons? The average age of their starting XI has decreased over the past three seasons when they were already the youngest team in Premier League history. You can see why they signed Henderson and Welbeck.

Set for a breakthrough

Robert Sánchez is still Chelsea’s No 1 but he may face serious competition this season from the 21-year-old Mike Penders. The goalkeeper, who was third-choice for Belgium at the World Cup, was signed from Genk in 2024 and spent last season on loan at Strasbourg in Ligue 1. The comparisons with Thibaut Courtois, who Chelsea signed from Genk at a similar age, are obvious. Like Courtois, Penders is 6ft 7in and therefore has a massive reach, but he also earns plaudits for his passing. Chances will come in cup competitions, but the clamour for Penders to be first choice might become hard to ignore.

World Cup impact

Enzo Fernández had a rollercoaster of a World Cup. Chelsea’s vice-captain popped up with crucial late goals for Argentina in the knockout stages, including a winning header against Egypt and the equaliser against England. But the abiding memory was his part in Argentina’s unsavoury approach in the final against Spain, where he received one yellow card for dissent and another for sending Pau Cubarsí flying. Real Madrid said in July they had “no intention” of pursuing a move that Fernández seemed to covet earlier this year when he said he would “love” to live in Madrid – comments that earned him a two-game ban under Rosenior. How about living in Manchester? City have been linked.

Sports.title: ‘It’s a nice hobby’: Manchester United’s Janina Leitzig on goalkeeping and gardening
Sports.content:
With some parts of England gearing up for a fifth heatwave of 2026 the new Manchester United goalkeeper Janina Leitzig, a keen gardener, is sympathetic to the precarious health of this reporter’s tomato plants. “You’re not used to so little rain, are you?” she observes. For the time being, after her summer move to Manchester, the former Germany youth international does not have a garden of her own but she reveals that, during her three-and-a-half-year spell at her former club Leicester, homegrown vegetables were her pride and joy.

“I love to do some gardening. Back home, everyone has their own vegetables and it’s just better, it tastes better,” she tells the Guardian. “Being away from home and away from family, of course you have your football friends, but still it can be quite lonely sometimes if you come home from training, so it was really nice to have a garden and to spend time outside. It’s not too much effort, it’s just a nice hobby.”

The 27-year-old got her outdoor fix with a spot of surfing in Cornwall this summer during the off-season, but now the serious business of pre-season is well under way. Her new club Manchester United are heading to La Manga for a training camp between 14 and 19 August, where the focus will have to be less on runner beans and more on running drills.

Leitzig, the former Bayern Munich and Hoffenheim keeper, was sitting down for an interview before it was known that the Spanish coach Eva Olid was to become United’s new manager, but explained why swapping Leicester for United was appealing to her. “It’s such a big club and it’s such a big honour to be here,” Leitzig says.

“I think, for every player, it’s really interesting if you have an offer from Manchester United. First of all, the team is so nice. The characters in here – you can tell it’s a really good and strong team. The training quality is really high. The building and the facilities [at Carrington] are really good; it’s really professional here. [When] the conversations were going on [with United], they just gave me a really good feeling.”

View image in fullscreen Janina Leitzig during a training session at Carrington. Photograph: Poppy Townson/MUFC/Getty Images

Leitzig has signed a contract with United until 2029, after the disappointment of relegation with Leicester last season, but says she has nothing but fond feelings about her former club, who she initially joined on loan in January 2023 before signing permanently that summer.

Looking back at what she learned in the East Midlands, she says: “It was such a special time for me. It was supposed to be only half a year and then it ended up being three-and-a-half. I think that says a lot about how much I liked it there. The people are great and the club is great.

“Obviously we had some tough times and unfortunately the relegation last season was really, really tough and it really hurt, because the club deserves to be in a better position, but I really hope that the girls will do well and I see them soon back in the WSL. It would be great if they could come back up quickly.”

During her time in England, Leitzig has observed an evolution in goalkeeping styles, and she is in a thoughtful mood when discussing what the future might look like for keepers, tactically. On the modern trend of keepers playing out from the back, she says: “To be fair, there was one phase where everyone wanted goalkeepers to play with the feet and I think it’s still really important, but I think there was a phase where it was too much. I think it was a bit overexaggerated at times, so I think it’s coming back now to be more about the basic stuff.

“Obviously you have to switch play and you have to be good with your feet under pressure, but I think the game is going to be more [about] trying to get the ball as quick as possible in the opposite half to then keep the pressure up there and not to try to take such a high risk. It’s going to be interesting.

“I think, because I’m German and Manuel Neuer [her idol] is German, I learned quite early to play with both feet and I was an outfield player initially, so I’m feeling confident about playing with the ball. But saving shots is the best part of goalkeeping.”

The USA keeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce played in 21 of United’s 22 matches in the Women’s Super League last season and Leitzig says they will enjoy working together and helping each other. “They [United] said it’s like a competition [to start in goal]. Obviously it’s really important to have strong goalkeepers, because you never know what happens in the season.

“I will just give my best, I’ll try to bring quality, and then it’s the manager’s decision to decide who’s going to play. But it’s really important that we are a good goalkeeper team, that we support each other and push each other because then everyone can get better.”

United, who finished fourth last season, will get the new WSL season under way on the opening night, at London City Lionesses on 4 September. Leizig concludes by looking ahead to that showdown and says, with fire in her eyes: “To have the first game of the season Friday evening, 7pm, floodlights, it’s just something you’re really excited for. Working in the pre-season you think: ‘When can the [games] finally start,’ so I’m really excited for that game.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s ‘rock star’ plays the hits but will he find it hard to stay in Toon?
Sports.content:
IN A BLACK AND WHITE TOWN

As rallying cries for the dawn of a golden era go, “I am quite optimistic” is not “ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country”. It did not fit the “I think I am a special one” template set 22 years ago by Netflix’s latest documentary subject. Nor did Matthias Jaissle’s unveiling as Newcastle manager meet the pre-match billing of “fire” and “a rock star” that the club’s chief suit had promised the journalists in attendance. Though, considering the summer of tumult on Tyneside, it was a sensible path to take. Expectations among the Toon Army have certainly lowered since Geordies sunk Tin and donned tea-towel headdresses in celebration of Mike Ashley’s departure and the arrival of a consortium underpinned by the petrodollars of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. As it turned out, Lionel Messi neither ended up mowing the pitch nor selling the pies.

Depending on your perspective, that Newcastle have not yet been crowned Premier League and Bigger Cup champions is down to the servile football authorities bowing down to the hated red cartel or that day of wild celebration being one of false hope. The truth lies probably somewhere in between. A number of missteps pockmarked the last season of Eddie Howe’s reign. The “here we go” arrivals were nowhere near up to snuff. It should, though, be readily accepted that Newcastle enjoyed a good run under Howe, including an actual trophy and two rides on the Bigger Cup fun bus.

The Saudi connection has not paved St James’ Park with black gold (or Texas tea as the Beverly Hillbillies once had it). A pitfall of becoming the plaything of a top-level geopolitical operator is that those geopolitics may get in the way. Gulf states have a few things on their plates at the moment, and the interests of that investment fund stretch beyond a football club 3,000 miles from Riyadh. A new phase is entered; Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães are gone. Some might say the Saudis have lost interest, though Jaissle’s arrival from Al-Ahli, another club in the Pif portfolio, suggests hands are still on the tiller.

As for the new manager, the verdict was that he spoke very well at his premiere. “We were looking at each other with smiles and goosebumps,” he cooed, in describing his and his assistants’ first look at the stadium. Realism was offered in admitting a “vacuum” now those assets have been flogged off but there was no preview of the touchline histrionics various profiles have promised. Jaissle also followed the recent but now ingrained tradition of shaking each of his future interrogators’ hands. A classy gesture? A power move? Take your pick. Howe’s departure, and the loss of those big names, has returned Newcastle to the state of flux that was long their usual state of existence. How long can Jaissle’s calm and collected deportment last? How long can measured optimism sustain?

Sports.title: Why the alarm bells should be ringing at Newcastle after defeat by Everton: Squad's lack of depth exposed, the key man who looks out of sorts and midfield puzzle new boss Matthias Jaissle must solve, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
Why the alarm bells should be ringing at Newcastle after defeat by Everton: Squad's lack of depth exposed, the key man who looks out of sorts and midfield puzzle new boss Matthias Jaissle must solve, writes CRAIG HOPE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

In their new change kit, Newcastle United were the ‘shrinking violets’ during a 3-1 defeat by Everton at Murrayfield.

The loss raises serious questions over the squad’s readiness for the Premier League season, with new boss Matthias Jaissle having inherited a group lacking leadership as well as quality in key areas.

David Moyes’ side were the deserved winners after goals from Thierno Barry, Iliman Ndiaye and Tyrique George settled a contest in which the Toffees showed more control and composure. Harvey Barnes fired a late reply for the Magpies.

Here, our chief footballer reporter Craig Hope brings you his four big takeaways for Newcastle to consider…

NEW FACES NEEDED

This was not a ‘reality check’ for Newcastle, because the reality of their situation was already blindingly obvious. They have lost four of their best and most experienced players this summer and head coach Eddie Howe said he could not continue on the eve of pre-season.

Here, it was not just holes in Newcastle’s XI that were exposed, but the depth of their squad looks alarmingly shallow. They need two full-backs, better midfielders and a fresh spark in attack. The danger for Jaissle is that he makes a losing start because he has been left short.

New boss Matthias Jaissle has plenty to think about but the problems were not unexpected

We understand that Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba is among those the manager admires, and the club have him on their list of targets. It is not an active transfer – the 22-year-old currently has an ankle injury – but our sources say it is one to keep an eye on as the window progresses.

Baleba would be an ambitious move, but Newcastle need to be just that if they are to give their new boss a squad that is able to compete in the top-flight this term. For right now, you would forecast a season-long struggle at the wrong end of the table.

On transfers, Jaissle said: ‘I think you all see the matches. You're also smart enough to see the needs in the squad. We handle these things internally. We are aware of what we need. There's still some time.’

He added: ‘For sure, we cannot be on the peak (against Liverpool on the opening day). This is clear. We're just working now for a couple of days.’

SVEN LOOKS SHORT

Sven Botman signed a new four-year contract in January but his performances since have been below the level that earned him that deal. Insiders were concerned that he looked too rigid in his movement towards the end of the season, and that worry has extended into the summer.

The Dutch centre-back is a class act at his best, but he was again at fault for a goal here and his sloppiness on the ball perhaps betrays a lack of confidence. After a series of injuries, the wider concern would be that his best days are behind him. He has a lot to prove this season. For now, Dan Burn would appear a better bet at left-sided centre-back alongside Malick Thiaw.

Sven Botman looked a little off the pace at Murrayfield as Everton outclassed Newcastle

MIDFIELD RIDDLE

For five years under Howe, Newcastle have played with a midfield three. Jaissle, in his first two games, has started with a 4-2-3-1, and an absence of control was all too evident during the first-half period in which Everton scored twice.

Joelinton and new signing Aladji Bamba were the pair in the middle, but the former has always preferred the insurance of two team-mates alongside him, allowing him to charge around and impose his physical superiority.

He is not suited to a more disciplined role in which he needs to take better care of the ball, while Bamba, 20, clearly needs time before he is ready to start in the Premier League. The Frenchman, formerly of Monaco, has made only 25 senior appearances in his career.

If Newcastle going into the season opener against Liverpool with this midfield, you suspect it would not end well.

Harvey Barnes scored a consolation goal for the Geordies, giving their fans something to cheer

STEUR THE POSITIVE (AGAIN)

On a positive note, Jacob Ramsey and Sean Steur were a better combination in the second half. Steur, 18, has been Newcastle’s best player during pre-season and he again showed a maturity beyond his teenage years. His willingness to take the ball in tight areas – and then keep it – is exactly what this team needs in a world without Bruno Guimaraes.

Steur apart, however, ball retention is going to be a problem for Newcastle. And when they have a defence that looks short of pace, the opposition springing quick breaks on the back of turnovers should be a worry for Jaissle.

Sports.title: The encouraging signs emerging under Michael Carrick's coaching, Bryan Mbeumo passes latest No 9 audition - and the young star the club CANNOT afford to let go as Man United beat Leeds on penalties
Sports.content:
The encouraging signs emerging under Michael Carrick's coaching, Bryan Mbeumo passes latest No 9 audition - and the young star the club CANNOT afford to let go as Man United beat Leeds on penalties

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United edged out rivals Leeds United on penalties to win the pre-season Boyle Sports Cup inside a sold-out Croke Park.

While the shootout - which almost didn't happen due to a deluge of young pitch invaders at full-time - ultimately separated the sides, both managers will have taken plenty from this pulsating clash under the lights in Dublin.

Bryan Mbeumo's audition to be Manchester United's starting striker for the opening game of the season was strengthened with another smart display, while Brenden Aaronson finished off a brilliant move to level things up at 1-1 in the first half.

James Justin's costly penalty miss as the fifth taker for Leeds allowed Noussair Mazraoui to win it with the final act as Michael Carrick's side clinched the game 5-4 on spot-kicks.

Daily Mail Sport brings you some of the biggest talking points from an historic night in Dublin…

Joshua Zirkzee (left) and Bryan Mbeumo (right) starred as Manchester United took on Leeds

TRUST COACH CARRICK

One of the things that Ruben Amorim called for was time on the training pitch to imprint his ideas on the United squad.

They fluffed the Europe league final to secure a season without European football and bar a couple of encouraging flashes, tangible signs of style and progress never materialised.

So to see Manchester United playing as well as they have throughout this pre-season - yes, it's pre-season - is a sign of just what good training ground coaches Carrick and his staff are proving to be.

It's a collective effort between Carrick, Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans, Travis Binnion, and many analysts in the background.

Here against Leeds United, much as it was against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg last weekend, you can see tangible signs of progress in the way Carrick wants this team to evolve in its pressing and its play-style.

'He wants to have the ball, he wants to press in certain ways,' summer signing Youri Tielemans explained on Tuesday.

'It might be different than what you are used to, what I have been used to before, but it is logical things in my opinion. It is just smelling football, and that is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht, you know. So for me, nothing changes, but it just needs to gel together.'

United are proving a lot more aggressive in the press and the defensive work of Andrey Santos in midfield, one of the summer signings to the tune of £50million, is pivotal.

The encouraging thing is that while these haven't been perfect performances either, there are more first team stars to come back in.

United lit up Croke Park from the start without captain and talisman Bruno Fernandes, without Tielemans, without Matheus Cunha, without the returning Marcus Rashford, without Benjamin Sesko, and Matthijs de Ligt, and Harry Maguire.

The way Leeds picked United off, capitalising on loose control from Tyler Fletcher, shows that there is still work to do.

But stylistically United, visibly at least, appear to be getting better by the game. For Manchester United fans, that's an incredibly encouraging sign.

Throughout pre-season you can see exactly what Michael Carrick is trying to implement

MBEUMO ON A HEATER

In a summer at Manchester United which has been as much about evolution as it has been revolution, the results of the Bryan Mbeumo striker experiment are yielding some fascinating results.

The Cameroonian is far from a typical No 9 but for Michael Carrick and Manchester United's staff, that is a big part of his appeal.

There are a multitude of factors at play here. United want to platform academy star Shea Lacey for a full-time first team role and he predominantly plays off the right. There's also Amad, who is facing a defining season in that right-side role.

And then you add in that United only have one orthodox No 9 option in Benjamin Sesko, and he hasn't kicked a ball during pre-season due to an ongoing shin injury, although he did travel to Ireland to take part in this week-long training camp.

So Mbeumo as a striker, and a fluid one at that, holds great appeal and perhaps importance, should United not go and add another forward between now and the transfer deadline.

Mbeumo is going to start the season up top, that now looks clear, but expect Carrick to call upon Marcus Rashford, too.

'He's our player,' he said last night. 'He's come back great. He's just like any other player... He gives us something a little bit different.'

Mbeumo hit a real lull in front of goal in the second half of last season and struggled to rediscover momentum that had fans off their seats in the first half leading to question marks about how Carrick may get the best out of him.

But a brace against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm, the equaliser in Gothenburg against PSG, and a brilliant piece of skill, coupled with an assist, for Joshua Zirkzee to open the scoring here in Dublin showed just how much confidence is running through Mbeumo's veins right now.

For the opening goal here - and he should have had his own in the first half when he crashed a shot against the crossbar - he nutmegged two Leeds players as he burst down the left before playing Zirkzee through to score beyond new No 1 James Trafford.

Leeds went on to equalise through Brenden Aaronson in the first half and were good value for it after a rocky start. Despite Carrick's side dominating the ball when their main men came on, it finished 1-1 in front of an 82,000-strong sell-out crowd at Croke Park.

Mbeumo is set to start as centre forward against Hull City to kickstart the Premier League campaign and from there the sky really does feel like the limit for him. This is a formula now, not just an experiment.

TYNAN TIME

While he didn't quite get the loudest cheer of the night - that was reserved for the introduction of Bruno Fernandes off the bench - this was a huge milestone in the career of Tynan Thompson.

The 18-year-old arrived from Tottenham Hotspur this summer as an Emerging Talent Signing that Ineos and United's powers love, look at Ayden Heaven and numerous others.

This was Thompson's first taste of senior football at United and the first time he's been away and part of Carrick's group this pre-season.

Tynan Thompson got his first taste of senior football in a Manchester United shirt in Dublin

Thompson, who arrived in a deal that could eventually total £8m, got a pep talk from his manager moments before the second half restarted and the message, likely, was to be bold, be aggressive and have fun.

What we saw across 45 minutes was a player who looks unafraid to take people on and, in something of a quirk in the modern game, is a winger that likes to take people on on the outside.

A couple of times midway through the second half he managed to get down the left side with a quick burst and then drill a low cross in, only for Leeds to mop it up comfortably.

Sources at United won't pigeonhole Thompson as a first team player or an Under-21 player and he's likely to find himself straddling the two.

But don't underestimate the value of nights like these, in front of 82,000, with the likes of Fernandes and Cunha demanding the ball off you.

This isn't academy football any more…

HARRY'S STYLE

Speaking of rising stars, it should be an impossibility that Harry Amass is allowed to leave unless United go out and get another left back.

Sources have indicated that Amass has been told his best chance of regular minutes will come elsewhere and the club are unlikely to stand in his way for a loan or a permanent, if they get fair value.

That plan needs shelving immediately unless someone like Lewis Hall, who United have made two approaches for but failed on both occasions, walks through the door.

Amass may physically be on the smaller side in stature but he was dynamic in possession and fierce out of it here as Leeds looked to put him under real pressure, particularly early on before they clocked that they may be better off testing Diogo Dalot instead.

Amass has suitors aplenty should he walk out the door but with only Luke Shaw to call on as a bonafide left back right now, Amass should be staying until further notice.

There is no way Harry Amass can be allowed to leave without a new left back coming in

TRAFFORD IS TOP

One thing that Leeds do deserve credit for is the decisiveness they have shown in the goalkeeper department in getting a top talent in James Trafford.

They gave it as long as they could with Illan Meslier, then tried Lucas Perri out, and pivoted to Karl Darlow, now of Manchester United, before paying a club record £40m for him.

Officially Trafford got the Man of the Match here before it went to a penalty shootout and he did make a number of fine saves to keep Manchester United out, not least denying one effort from Zirkzee, and another from Mbeumo.

It cannot be understated just what a difference a truly top goalkeeper can make and if Leeds are to kick on like Brighton and Bournemouth did in getting into Europe, it is moves like Trafford that will go a long way to moving the needle.

MAKE IRELAND A YEARLY TRIP

Lastly, a sold out Croke Park was absolutely incredible, and a trip United should make yearly if the logistics were feasible.

The appetite for Manchester United in these parts is understandably huge and credit as well to the Leeds United contingent who travelled in good numbers.

Naturally the pre-season appeal is wherever the money is for Premier League clubs and the answer for Manchester United is often the United States.

But they could do a lot worse than secure themselves a near-enough home game in Ireland given how many fans turned out for this one.

A cracking trip that should give United's execs pause for thought.

Sports.title: Arsenal's next top prospect shines in absence of key man, Myles Lewis-Skelly makes his case after doubts over his future - and why time is running out for Gabriel Jesus
Sports.content:
Arsenal's next top prospect shines in absence of key man, Myles Lewis-Skelly makes his case after doubts over his future - and why time is running out for Gabriel Jesus

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Myles Lewis-Skelly struck in the first half in Arsenal’s 1-1 draw against Cesc Fabregas’ Como side amid speculation around his future.

Lewis-Skelly's effort was cancelled out by Martin Baturina two minutes before the break in what proved to be a real test for Mikel Arteta's men.

The Gunners went on to win 4-3 on penalties, thanks largely to David Raya. Arsenal are back in action when they face Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday.

Daily Mail Sport's ISAAN KHAN brings you the main talking points from their win over the Italian side.

Marli Salmon stands out

There’s another young gem coming through Arsenal’s Hale End pipeline: enter Marli Salmon.

He stepped up on a night where Mikel Arteta threw down the challenge to his youngsters.

Salmon and Max Dowman, both 16, started, as well as Theo Julienne, 18, who made his first senior team start.

Salmon in particular stood out, for the rarity of a 16-year-old starting in a first-team match at centre back.

The defender last season would typically come on at right back when substituted on in the odd first-team game — once in the Champions League and three times in the FA Cup (he started against Mansfield Town).

Marli Salmon was given a warm embrace from his manager Mikel Arteta when he came off

He coped well and wasn’t deterred by the physical challenge, playing with steel and conviction.

The opposition were wary of taking Salmon on, with the menacing Gabriel alongside him.

His runs and confidence on the ball made the real mark, as he progressed into the opposition half on occasion, evading players with a burst of speed. That takes guts and took the crowd by surprise.

What a baptism of fire such an experience is, and one he will no doubt remember.

Arteta’s confidence in the teenager saw Salmon stay on the pitch until the 88th minute.

He stepped up, alright.

Lewis-Skelly makes his point

A heart-shaped celebration and hands folded in a prayer motion, Myles Lewis-Skelly made his point.

The teenager struck in the first half amid reports suggesting the 19-year-old has been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United by intermediaries, which Arsenal have insisted isn’t the case.

Though Lewis-Skelly brushed the noise aside to enjoy a promising display in a young line-up.

Goalkeeper Jean Butez’s clearance was headed down by Lewis-Skelly to Gabriel Martinelli, who teed up the teenager to strike home on 33 minutes.

The goal was met by chants of ‘Myles Lewis-Skelly, he’s one of our own’, on an evening he used to remind observers of his talents.

Myles Lewis-Skelly delivered a clear message with his celebration amid talk over his future

Yet, it was the midfielder’s actions after the goal which reflected where his intentions lie.

Lewis-Skelly clasped his hands together towards the crowd before making out a heart sign in a clear sign of intent.

He is a fine player, and one who started in last season’s Champions League final.

His ceiling is high — and his future is bright at Arsenal.

Little chance of resurrection for Jesus

The gauntlet had been laid. With Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz on the bench, Gabriel Jesus started as the No 9.

It represented a nudge from Arteta, as if to say ‘show me what you’ve got’.

That didn’t last long, hooked off on 32 minutes for Gyokeres after a limited cameo.

He did try, the Brazilian. The effort was there, trying to pierce the backline with darts forward and active around the goal.

Gabriel Jesus' future looks in doubt and he made way for Viktor Gyokeres

Though his display was marked by a miss on six minutes, the ball falling to him as Eberechi Eze passed on Ethan Nwaneri’s interception.

Jesus had an open goal to aim at with the goalkeeper out of his area — but struck the goalframe.

It dented the forward’s confidence, and he never properly recovered. On 32 minutes, he made way for Gyokeres, a reflection of his underwhelming night.

With just one more friendly remaining — against Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday — time is really running out for the Brazilian, who has been earmarked for the door.

Arteta gets one over ex-Gunners star

From afar, the touchline resemblance of Arteta and Cesc Fabregas was uncanny.

Arms crossed, wearing beige trousers and dark-coloured short-sleeved tops, both men mirrored one another.

The pair played alongside each other at Arsenal once upon a time. And at one stage, rumours suggested Fabregas could one day be Arteta’s successor.

Cesc Fabregas was looking dapper back at the Emirates on the touchline

Though such a prospect is a long way off after Arsenal’s title triumph last season.

Still, Fabregas’ post-match press conference lasted over 10 minutes, with Arteta waiting outside for him to finish.

He clearly had missed the Emirates.

Sports.title: Chelsea set Enzo Fernandez bid deadline: Blues tell Man City and other suitors to offer £120MILLION or forget about signing controversial Argentina star
Sports.content:
Chelsea have told Manchester City they have until 5pm tomorrow to pay £120million to sign Enzo Fernandez — or forget about the transfer.

As Daily Mail Sport has reported previously in this window, City are interested in the Argentina midfielder, who shared a strong relationship with Enzo Maresca when he was Chelsea coach.

Fernandez, who returned to Chelsea training this week after helping his country to the World Cup final, has six years left on his contract.

If City do not meet Chelsea’s demands, the Stamford Bridge club do not intend to sell Fernandez in this window.

City’s interest in the player, 25, has been known to Chelsea since the end of last season which is when their valuation of the midfielder was confirmed to Fernandez’s agent, Javier Pastore.

Fernandez was one of the Argentina players who riled England after the ill-tempered World Cup semi-final in Atlanta, which Argentina won 2-1.

Manchester City have been handed a deadline of Thursday 5pm to bid for Enzo Fernandez

City boss Enzo Maresca is interested in bringing his former player to his new club

The Chelsea man drew Argentina level after 85 minutes and immediately raced over to stand in front of England fans, cupped his hands behind his ears and stuck out his tongue, then blew a kiss.

Chelsea were later forced to delete a post on X which celebrated wantaway star Fernandez’s equaliser after a furious response from fans up and down the country.

Sports.title: Ex-NFL star accused of violating estranged wife's protective order after domestic violence case was dropped
Sports.content:
Marcellus Wiley's estranged wife Annemarie reportedly called the police alleging a potential domestic violence restraining order violation by the ex-NFL star hours after criminal charges against him were dropped.

Court records filed on Monday and obtained by the Daily Mail show Wiley will not face domestic battery charges in Florida following an alleged altercation with his wife that saw him arrested on July 4.

According to the filing in Orange County state court, testimony is 'not corroborated by any physical or other evidence' and therefore the state of Florida is not filing criminal charges as it is 'insufficient to obtain a conviction.'

TMZ now reports that Annemarie contacted police on Tuesday to report a possible violation of his restraining order, with officers responding to their marital home in Los Angeles.

The report claims Marcellus is banned from entering the property under the terms of the restraining order, but no arrests were made after police determined no crime was committed.

An arrest affidavit on July 4 alleged Wiley threatened to kill his wife in an Orlando hotel room and became physical with her in front of their children. Annemarie told police that Wiley stood over her on the morning of July 3 and 'used one finger to sternly and intentionally poke her in the cheek,' before threatening to kill her.

Marcellus Wiley and his wife, Annemarie, who starred on The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills

Marcellus Wiley will not face charges after his arrest over an alleged altercation with his wife

She was spotted in July for the first time since the shocking allegations became public and was not wearing her wedding band on her left ring finger.

The former Real Housewives of Beverly Hills star alleged in the filing seen by the Daily Mail that his abuse started back in 2012, including a number of incidents of physical violence and four alleged rapes. She was also seeking sole legal and physical custody of their three children, and an order denying Wiley visitation.

'Marcellus subjects me to constant criticism, cruel and sarcastic remarks, and intimidation,' Annemarie claims in the application.

'His verbal and emotional abuse is constant, and his physical abuse occurs approximately once a month, and at times more frequently. I am afraid of Marcellus, and I fear for my own safety and for the safety of our children.'

Wiley wrote a lengthy statement defending himself, sent to The California Post, in which he called Annemarie's allegations 'lies' and claimed he can directly contradict her 'baseless claims' with 'videos, photographs, text messages, emails, and other evidence.'

'I love my children with everything I am,' Wiley said in the statement. 'My highest priority has always been protecting them and preserving the relationship they have with both of their parents.

'Because of the public allegations made against me by Annemarie, I have been forced to respond with evidence rather than emotion. More importantly, I owe it to my children to truthfully document what they and I have endured.'

Wiley was arrested in Florida over the July 4 weekend

Wiley, a former ESPN personality, has continued to deny allegations against him

'As you know, I'm usually the first to break down the truth and separate facts from fiction,' he added. 'But because this is now a legal matter – and because my greatest responsibility is protecting my babies, who have already been impacted – I have to handle this differently. When I can speak freely, I absolutely will.'

Wiley is also facing sexual assault allegations from four accusers. The civil claims, filed in New York earlier this year, broaden litigation that began in 2023 when three women accused Wiley of rape during his time at Columbia University. No criminal charges have been filed, and Wiley denies the claims.

One of the new accusers is a former ESPN production assistant who claims she was lured into a hotel room under the guise of a work meeting by Wiley in 2009.

In a graphic written statement in the court filing, the former staffer claimed Wiley emerged from a bathroom naked and physically overpowered her, leaving her 'petrified.'

The woman told the court: 'He pushed me up against the windows of the room so hard I thought they would shatter. I was petrified and believed I was going to be killed.

'I repeatedly pleaded with him to stop and to let me go. He would not. He pushed me face down on the bed and kept me there with my face pressed into the mattress in such a way that I had difficulty breathing, which made me fear for my life.

'Wiley held me down and masturbated over me until he ejaculated. Only then did he allow me to leave the room.

'This assault was devastating to me and I live with the affects (sic) to this day. I will never truly escape from that room,' the former ESPN employee wrote.

Another of the latest accusers claims in the lawsuit that Wiley 'groomed' her from the age of 13 before raping her on her 18th birthday.

Wiley played a decade in the NFL, making the Pro Bowl while with the San Diego Chargers

The unnamed individual alleged in the lawsuit that she was just 13 when Wiley first came into contact with her, after visiting her middle school in Buffalo, New York. The woman further claimed that Wiley, a player for the Buffalo Bills at the time, 'showered her family with free tickets and invitations to his Orchard Park home.'

The accuser alleged that, on her 18th birthday, Wiley flew her to Dallas and 'shouted at her in a frightening manner and coerced her into sex'.

'Marcellus Wiley raped me on my 18th birthday, after grooming me from the age of 13, the alleged victim wrote in her account to the court.

Statements were also submitted to the court by two additional accusers alleging assaults in the late 1990s, including an attack in Culver City and a rape at a USC Hotel.

Wiley has consistently and vehemently denied all allegations, previously using his YouTube channel to dismiss the initial 2023 claims as 'BS' and fabrications.

'For every one of them, I either saw, communicated through email, text, phone, was invited by these individuals after these dates to engage, to be intimate or all the above, after the dates that are in question,' Wiley said on his podcast in May.

'This matters. Why does it matter? Because it directly contradicts the narrative they are trying to present publicly.

'They are attempting to leverage lies for personal gain, as they say, assassination by accusation, that's their goal,' he continued. 'They trying by lying.'

Sports.title: PSG 2-1 Aston Villa: French giants claim UEFA Super Cup triumph but two teen stars show future is bright for Villans - with 17-year-old Brian Madjo bullying Luis Enrique's defence
Sports.content:
PSG 2-1 Aston Villa: French giants claim UEFA Super Cup triumph but two teen stars show future is bright for Villans - with 17-year-old Brian Madjo bullying Luis Enrique's defence

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The UEFA Super Cup belongs to Paris Saint-Germain but Aston Villa left Salzburg with something far more precious than a piece of pre-season silverware.

Between them, teenagers Brian Madjo and George Hemmings have made just six competitive appearances for Villa. Yet both frightened the life out of the back-to-back Champions League winners and on this evidence, they will be given plenty more opportunities by Unai Emery.

They may have sold £150million worth of talent in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne since winning the Europa League and have doubts over the future of other key players. There is nothing quite like teenagers stepping up to the mark, though, and their performances will give Villa plenty of encouragement ahead of their Premier League opener at Brighton on August 23.

Madjo, 17, became the youngest scorer in Super Cup history when he steered home John McGinn’s cross just before half-time. Before that, the 6ft 4ins centre-forward missed two other excellent chances and bullied Willian Pacho, one of the world’s best centre-backs.

Villa signed Madjo for £10m from Metz last January but a registration issue meant he was not cleared to play until this summer.

Either side of Madjo’s strike, goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue ensured PSG retained this trophy, and it is important to say PSG were some way from full fitness and Liverpool target Bradley Barcola did not leave the bench.

Achraf Hakimi lifts the UEFA Super Cup for PSG after their 2-1 win over Aston Villa

Desire Doue beat the offside trap to put PSG 2-1 up against Aston Villa in Salzburg

English 17-year-old Brian Madjo had a number of chances and converted the equaliser

Yet many of Villa’s players were not in peak condition, either. Luckily, Hemmings was one of those determined to make his mark.

The 19-year-old is a product of Villa’s youth system and given the club’s struggles with UEFA’s financial rules, a homegrown player in the first team is a gem. Though Madjo caught the eye for his goal and chances, Hemmings looks the more accomplished player at this stage.

Starting on the left, he was prepared to run fearlessly at Achraf Hakimi, probably the best right-back on the planet. He showed great maturity in possession, too, at one stage winning the ball from Nuno Mendes close to his own-goal line and casually chipping it to Emi Buendia. Expect to see plenty more of this kid in the weeks ahead.

Now Emery’s attention must turn to the market, where he has been fallible during his time at Villa Park. Despite Madjo’s display, another forward will surely arrive while Villa continue to make progress in deals for midfielder Joao Palhinha and left-back Matteo Ruggeri.

Villa have changed a great deal since they won the Europa League less than three months ago. Gone are Rogers and Tielemans, two of their scorers against Freiburg that night, while Digne was sitting on the PSG bench. Three of Emery’s coaching team have also moved on.

That meant only five of the starters in Istanbul featured here, with Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez still on their post-World Cup breaks. With Arsenal offering a £45million package for Konsa earlier in the day, it is unclear how many more times the England centre-back will wear Villa colours.

Emery and skipper John McGinn were bullish about the ‘new Villa’ on Tuesday and in the first half against PSG, we saw why. Though the majority of the PSG group are some way from full speed after the World Cup, they are still some of the world’s best players and it was stirring to watch Villa youngsters Hemmings and Madjo going toe to toe with them.

Hemmings was awarded an early free-kick by referee Omar Artan, the Somalian official who was denied entry to the United States ahead of the World Cup. Though Villa did not create anything from the free-kick, they had laid down a marker.

Even at half pace, PSG are incredibly dangerous when given a chance. After Marco Bizot had scooped away Desire Doue’s deflected shot, Madjo’s loose touch presented the ball to Vitinha. He found Doue and when Kvaratskhelia collected the ball, it was soon flying into the roof of the net from 15 yards.

Madjo's effort beat the goalkeeper for pace after he connected with a John McGinn cross

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia broke the deadlock with a lashed finish for French side

Until then, Madjo had looked very raw and his technique needs refining – though there are few better coaches to do so than Emery. More importantly, he did not allow his head to drop and in the second part of the first half, PSG could not handle him.

Madjo headed two delightful crosses from McGinn over the bar, with the second a particularly bad miss. In between those chances, he had shot wide on an angle after more impressive work by Hemmings and seen another effort blocked following Emi Buendia’s run. Moments later, Madjo hit the outside of the post after holding off Pacho, though this was flagged offside onfield.

When Madjo did score, the opportunity was far tougher than those he had missed. From another McGinn cross, Madjo found his way on to the dangerous side of Pacho and volleyed beyond Matvei Safonov.

It was an uplifting end to the half for Villa, who deserved their equaliser. And soon after the break, they might have taken the lead.

Madjo was involved again, this time taking a pass from Buendia and charging into space behind PSG’s high line. He then fed McGinn, whose shot clipped Pacho and allowed Safonov a split second longer to make the save. Villa were still making the running though and just before the hour, Buendia headed over unmarked.

George Hemmings was another of the young Aston Villa stars lighting up the big stage

Unai Emery congratulates the PSG players after full time in Salzburg on Wednesday night

Against PSG, though, if you lose focus for the briefest moment you will be punished. Doue looked well offside when he took a pass from substitute Ousmane Dembele (not a bad player to be able bring on) and steered beyond Bizot.

The goal was ruled out on field but replays showed Matty Cash, half a yard behind the rest of Villa’s back four, had left Doue onside.

Back came Villa. Now it was Hemmings’ turn to break into the box and draw a save from Safonov.

PSG were looking increasingly dangerous on the break but in the closing 10 minutes, Alysson could not find the return pass to give fellow substitute Tammy Abraham an easy equaliser.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi says 'I don't know how to go on' and hints he will QUIT football as he breaks his silence on dad Jorge's death aged 68
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo paid tribute to the late father of his great rival, Lionel Messi, with a touching message on social media.

Lionel Messi has hinted he will retire from football following the devastating death of his father, Jorge, who was an integral figure in the career of his legendary son.

Jorge died on August 7 following a battle with illness that overshadowed the Argentina captain's mesmerising World Cup campaign in the United States, in which he led his team to the final.

Lionel, who broke down in tears following Argentina's group stage win over Algeria while Jorge's health was deteriorating, shared a heartbreaking letter to his father on Instagram – in which he casts doubt over his playing future.

'Dad, I still can't believe you're gone. It hasn't sunk in yet, or rather, I don't want to accept it. It's very difficult for me to imagine never seeing you again, never talking to you again. I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left too soon. We still had so much to enjoy together.

'I don't know what I'll do without you, I don't know how to go on. I only played football and now I have serious doubts that I'll continue doing that for much longer. You were by my side from the beginning, it was so close to the end. Why couldn't you hold on that little bit longer and we could have finished together?'

Ronaldo replied to the post, saying: 'A huge hug to you and yours in these tough times, Leo. Much strength.'

The Portuguese legend knows of Messi's heartache only too well after losing his father, Jose Dinis Aveiro, in 2005 to an alcoholism-related live condition when he was aged just 20.

'I really don’t know my father 100 per cent,' Ronaldo told Piers Morgan in 2019. 'He was a drunk person. I never spoke with him, like a normal conversation. It was hard.'

Messi revealed that his father was the driving force behind his decision to play at this summer's World Cup, but his ageing legs prevented him from bringing the trophy home – with Spain winning 1-0 in the New York final.

Lionel Messi has thanked fans for their support following the death of his father Jorge (left)

Messi's father and agent died in Rosario, Argentina on Friday August 7

Jorge's death saw an outpouring of emotional tributes from the football world, including from Messi's first team Newell's Old Boys, as well as Barcelona and Argentina.

'You kept asking me to play in the last World Cup, and just a few days before it started, you got worse. It was the first time you wouldn't be in a tournament, but Mom kept telling me you'd get better and be well enough to travel. I told you we were going to reach the final so you could travel.

'Every time a game ended, I waited and missed your message. That's when I realized the situation was really serious. Even so, I couldn't stop thinking about going as far as possible, to give you time and for you to see a game. We reached the final and you couldn't be there. I wanted to win it to bring it to you and show you a new one. I couldn't, my legs couldn't take it anymore. This time I tried to go against my physical limitations, but I couldn't. I never managed to feel well.

'When I arrived, you thought we'd lost the final on penalties. We couldn't talk about anything that happened. You couldn't enjoy any of it. We didn't win the championship, but you don't know how much we enjoyed every game. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play.

'I'm telling you this because it was the only thing we couldn't talk about, because you already know everything else. We used to talk every day and see each other whenever possible, given my commitments.'

Messi missed Inter Miami's defeat by Monterrey on Sunday to return home in the wake of his father's passing, and thanked fans for their well wishes.

He added on his Instagram stories: 'I want to sincerely thank everyone for all the love, respect and enormous consideration you have shown me and my family during this incredibly painful time following the loss of my dad.

'Thank you for being there for us, for every message, every gesture and, above all, for respecting our grief and our privacy.'

Lionel Messi's father Jorge, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, died at the age of 68
