Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Richard Torrez Jr. Faces Bigger Challenge Than Rebuilding Confidence
Sports.content:
“I understand what I did wrong and I can fix it,” Torrez Jr. said via The Ring. “Shoutout to Eddy Reynoso. That dude read me like a book in that second round. I got caught with a shot.”

This was not the first warning. Bakhodir Jalolov stopped him in the amateurs after catching him coming forward. Guido Vianello also found him repeatedly when they fought in April 2025. Torrez Jr. won a wide decision, but his vulnerability was clear.

Top Rank had not matched the Olympic silver medalist particularly tough before Vianello. His power and aggression allowed him to overwhelm early opponents without forcing him to improve defensively.

There are similarities to how Top Rank developed Edgar Berlanga. Berlanga opened his career with 16 consecutive first-round stoppage wins against limited opposition. Those quick finishes built his reputation while offering little chance to develop against fighters who could survive his power.

The American southpaw did not compile the same streak, but his matchmaking created a parallel issue. Quick victories entrenched a style centered on charging forward instead of fixing long-standing technical flaws.

His stocky 6’2″ build means Torrez Jr. is unlikely to become a mobile heavyweight. He can still improve his guard, head movement, entries, and defensive balance.

He wants to return before the end of the year, though Top Rank has not named an opponent. They may choose a safer option after such a heavy stoppage.

One rebuilding fight makes sense. A prolonged return to soft opposition leaves the primary question unanswered. Torrez Jr. needs more than another early night. He must prove that the flaws Sanchez exposed have actually changed.

Sports.title: Top Rank’s Thin DAZN Schedule Tells Half The Story
Sports.content:
Darshan Desai of Uncrowned highlighted the unusual arrangement Wednesday while examining DAZN’s schedule. Raymond Muratalla fought Robson Conceição on a Golden Boy card earlier this month, Top Rank fighters Albert Gonzalez and Samuel Contreras competed on a Matchroom show in July, and Giovani Santillan takes another route when he faces Abass Baraou on September 11 in a ProBoxTV headliner.

Building a full show requires considerably more than placing a fighter on an existing lineup. Opponents require negotiation, purses need settling, and organizers must assemble a complete event around the roster. How costs are divided under Top Rank’s agreement with DAZN has not been made public.

Working alongside Golden Boy or Matchroom gives Top Rank flexible alternatives. Both outfits work extensively with DAZN, reducing the traditional network barriers that historically complicated cross-promotional deals.

Top Rank still has plenty of incentive to stage its own events when a leading fighter can anchor a marquee card. The proposed welterweight title bout between Devin Haney and Keyshawn Davis would have provided another major date before Davis declined the WBO process.

Whatever the reason for Top Rank’s limited number of DAZN dates so far, its fighters are finding work without waiting for the promoter to build an entire show around them.

Sports.title: WBC Threatens Noel Mikaelian’s Title Over Jai Opetaia Fight
Sports.content:
King and Benavidez promoter Sampson Lewkowicz reached an agreement for Mikaelian to defend his WBC cruiserweight title against Benavidez in December in Glendale, Arizona. Zuffa Boxing subsequently announced Mikaelian against Opetaia for September 12 in Las Vegas on the Ryan Garcia-Conor Benn card.

Mikaelian is already training for Opetaia, Pugmire reports, giving the WBC reason to seek an answer in the coming weeks on which fight he intends to take.

Benavidez may already have an alternate route. He teased an announcement Tuesday, and Pugmire reports his next bout will likely be against WBC interim cruiserweight champion Michal Cieslak for the title.

The promotional situation remains unusual. King and Lewkowicz had already struck their agreement when Zuffa announced Mikaelian as Opetaia’s opponent. Mikaelian then began preparing for the September fight despite remaining WBC champion, with Benavidez positioned as his mandatory challenger.

If Mikaelian proceeds with Opetaia, the WBC can remove him and leave Benavidez and Cieslak to fight for the championship. That would give Mikaelian the Zuffa fight he is training for, but without the WBC belt.

Sports.title: Hearn Targets Brandon Moore Next For Teremoana
Sports.content:
“I think we might fight him next, Brandon Moore,” Hearn said after the fight. “We have really got to find someone. It’s so frustrating in Australia because no one wants to fight him.”

A fight with Moore (19-1, 10 KOs) would provide an obvious measuring stick. He defeated Savage by a 10-round unanimous decision last September, dropping him in the seventh. His lone defeat came against Richard Torrez Jr., who knocked him out in five rounds in 2024.

Hearn felt Savage became frightened once he experienced Teremoana’s power.

“I was disappointed Savage didn’t get [further]. I don’t blame him, but it was just the fear. His eyes were popping out of his head as soon as he felt the power.”

Teremoana hardly pressed the accelerator in the opening round, throwing only a handful of punches before hurting Savage with a right hand late. Hearn liked the patience he showed rather than immediately going for the finish.

“I saw a guy that was a little bit more experienced tonight. Sort of took his time. I mean, he could have really done it in 30 seconds.”

Getting meaningful rounds has become increasingly difficult. Hearn conceded that fans will question the quality of Teremoana’s opposition and said Matchroom has reached the point where the competition must increase.

“There’ll be a lot of the public that will say, ‘Well, who’s he fighting?’ And I get that as well. We’ve got to step up,” Hearn said. “We do really, really need rounds.”

Hearn wants Teremoana to fight twice more this year and believes another four or five bouts are needed before he challenges for a world heavyweight title. His target is the back end of 2027, when Teremoana will be 29.

“He needs someone that can take him five or six rounds,” Hearn said. “Sooner or later there’s going to be a 10-round, 12-round war in there, and he’ll be ready.”

Anthony Joshua has also taken notice of Teremoana.

“AJ said to me a few times, ‘What’s this Teremoana?’ I’m like, ‘He’s a fucking monster.’”

Hearn expects a different type of fight once Teremoana encounters heavyweights willing and capable of attacking him rather than simply trying to survive.

Sports.title: Teremoana Teremoana Crushes DeAndre Savage in Two
Sports.content:
Teremoana dictated the opening round, forcing Savage onto the defensive while patiently looking for an opening.

In the co-main event, Michael “Pretty Boy” Zerafa stopped Alejandro “El Venado” Ortiz after nine rounds of their scheduled 10-round middleweight bout.

Zerafa established his jab over the opening two rounds before Ortiz found more success in the third, landing several left hooks to the chin. Zerafa countered effectively and produced a strong fourth round.

Ortiz landed a hard right hand midway through the fifth, but Zerafa regained control in the sixth by increasing his output. The Australian broke through in the ninth, hurting Ortiz and overwhelming him with punches. Ortiz struggled back to his corner after the bell, and his team stopped the fight before the 10th round.

Jasmine Parr defeated Jemma Peart by unanimous decision over eight two-minute rounds in their flyweight bout.

Parr controlled much of the opening three rounds by outlanding Peart, who had greater success with her jab in the fourth. Parr occasionally switched to southpaw in the fifth and sixth while maintaining the higher work rate.

The seventh was the most competitive round before Parr closed strongly in the eighth. All three judges scored the bout 80-72.

At super middleweight, Jack Bowen stopped Dalielibieke at 2:15 of the seventh round.

Bowen used an effective jab early and rocked Dalielibieke with an uppercut in the second. Both connected with hard right hands late in the third before the exchanges became heavier in the fourth.

Another right uppercut from Bowen hurt Dalielibieke midway through the fifth. Dalielibieke responded with one of his better rounds in the sixth, but Bowen regained control in the seventh. A sustained combination prompted referee Paul Tapley to stop the contest.

Lekaysha Woodbridge defeated Sothia Sitthichai over five two-minute rounds in their flyweight bout. Referee Paul Tapley scored the fight 50-45 for Woodbridge.

Light heavyweight Omar El-Abdallah stopped Jordan Towns after three rounds of their scheduled five-round bout. The two were competitive through the opening three rounds, but Towns was unable to answer the bell for the fourth.

In welterweight action, Reube Thornberry stopped Lachlan Harrington at 1:40 of the second round of their scheduled four-round bout.

Sports.title: Jake Paul’s MVP Signs IBF Champion Elif Turhan
Sports.content:
Turhan gives Jake Paul’s promotion another major piece at 135 pounds. Caroline Dubois holds the WBC and WBO championships, while Stephanie Han owns the WBA belt.

That leaves MVP working with fighters who control all four major lightweight titles.

Turhan punched her way into that company last December in Monte Carlo. She broke down Brazilian Olympic gold medalist Beatriz Ferreira and forced a fifth-round stoppage to seize the IBF crown, registering the defining victory of her professional career.

She has since strengthened her position with wins over Taylah Gentzen in January and Gabriella Tellez in June.

Turhan brings pressure and finishing instinct to a division loaded with potential championship fights. She likes to close the distance, force exchanges and punish opponents once her combinations begin finding the target.

The Istanbul fighter becomes the first Turkish boxer to join MVP and follows Nicolson as the second addition produced by the promotion’s agreement with Matchroom.

Turhan believes the partnership can push her toward more championship opportunities.

“I am incredibly excited to be part of this powerful collaboration. This marks a major signal of the exciting initiatives we will undertake for women’s boxing globally, and I am deeply honored to be involved in this journey with all my strength and energy.”

Her next opponent has yet to be confirmed, but her ambitions reach beyond defending the IBF belt.

“I am excited for the opportunities that will come my way as I look to win more major World Titles.”

That pursuit creates an obvious pressure point at lightweight. Dubois controls two belts, Han holds another and Turhan carries the IBF championship.

If MVP eventually matches its lightweight champions, Turhan will have to establish her pressure against fighters capable of controlling distance, countering her entries and punishing her on the way inside.

Sports.title: Teremoana vs. DeAndre Savage Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Teremoana Teremoana improved to 12-0 with a second-round knockout of DeAndre Savage after another destructive heavyweight finish. Savage survived the opening round despite absorbing several heavy shots as Teremoana began finding his distance and opening up. That resistance ended quickly in the second. Teremoana cracked Savage with a big punch that buckled the American’s legs but left him standing. The Australian kept hunting the finish, dropped Savage moments later, and watched as he failed to beat the referee’s count. Savage became only the third opponent to take Teremoana beyond the opening round, but the extra three minutes merely delayed another knockout for the Australian heavyweight.

Michael Zerafa broke down Alejandro Ortiz for a stoppage victory on the Gold Coast after taking command in the later rounds. Zerafa began forcing Ortiz onto the back foot, then cracked him with a heavy shot in the seventh as the pressure increased. His corner demanded he keep letting his hands go while staying smart, telling him Ortiz was hurt whenever he opened up. Zerafa responded by pressing harder and keeping Ortiz under fire. The breakthrough came when Zerafa dropped Ortiz and immediately looked to close the show. Ortiz climbed off the canvas but remained hurt, and the fight was stopped soon afterward when he had taken enough. The victory gave Zerafa the result he needed after entering the fight under pressure and facing questions over his recent form.

Sports.title: Jack Dempsey’s Harry Wills Problem Never Went Away
Sports.content:
Following Jack Johnson’s 1910 victory over Jim Jeffries, racial violence erupted across the United States. The possibility of another Black heavyweight challenging a white champion encountered resistance from promoters, regulators, and others concerned about another interracial title fight.

Wills paid heavily for that environment.

A Dempsey-Wills fight nearly materialized in 1922 when promoter Tex Rickard selected a date and had tickets printed for a proposed bout in New Jersey. The promotion collapsed when the financing needed to meet Dempsey’s guarantee failed.

Another attempt ran into opposition in New York, where athletic commission chairman William Muldoon resisted an interracial heavyweight championship fight over concerns about racial unrest.

Dempsey also gave his critics ammunition. He drew the color line early in his championship reign before later changing his public position. His long stretches of inactivity intensified criticism that Wills was being denied an opportunity he had earned. Yet Wills himself resisted blaming Dempsey.

“My only regret in life is that I never got a shot at Dempsey, [and] I’m sure I could have beaten him,” Wills later said. “It wasn’t Jack’s fault. He wasn’t scared of anyone. He was a great fighter.”

Dempsey lost the heavyweight championship to Gene Tunney in 1926. Wills never fought for the world title.

The missing fight should count when Dempsey’s championship reign is evaluated. Wills was precisely the type of challenger a champion needed to defeat to remove questions about his dominance.

Placing the entire responsibility on Dempsey, however, ignores the racial barriers, regulators, promoters and failed financing that repeatedly interfered with the fight.

More than a century later, nobody knows what would have happened if Jack Dempsey and Harry Wills had finally met. That unanswered question is why Wills remains an unavoidable part of Dempsey’s legacy.

Ghana News.title: Luv FM High School Debate: St. Hubert and Adutwum SHS seal their round of sixteen spots
Ghana News.content:
The third day of the Luv FM Kel-Charcoal Toothpaste High School Debate lived up to expectations, producing two engaging and competitive contests as St. Hubert Seminary and Osei Adutwum Senior High School secured impressive victories to book their places in the 1/16 round of the competition.

Wednesday's contest at the Christian Service University featured strong performances from all four participating schools, with debaters demonstrating confidence, research, critical thinking and persuasive speaking skills.

For Anglican Senior High School and Tepa SHS, however, the day's contests marked the end of their journey in this year's competition.

The first contest of the day brought together St. Hubert Seminary (SAHUSS) and Anglican Senior High School, Kumasi, in what turned out to be a nail-biting clash.

The two schools were tasked with debating the constructive motion: “Community service judgment will serve a purpose than custodial sentence.”

St. Hubert Seminary argued in support of the motion, while Anglican Senior High School took the opposing side. From the opening presentations, both teams demonstrated a clear understanding of the subject and sought to convince the judges with carefully constructed arguments.

St. Hubert Seminary placed strong emphasis on the restorative nature of community service, arguing that it can allow offenders to contribute positively to society while also serving as a form of punishment.

The school presented community service as an alternative that could help rehabilitate offenders rather than relying solely on custodial sentences.

Anglican Senior High School, on the other hand, mounted a strong challenge to the proposition, presenting counter-arguments aimed at defending the relevance and effectiveness of custodial sentences.

As the contest progressed, the exchanges became increasingly intense, with both sides using their rebuttals to challenge weaknesses in their opponents' arguments.

One of the standout moments came from the supporting speaker for St. Hubert Seminary, who delivered a particularly convincing argument and helped strengthen the school's case before the judges.

After the final rebuttals, St. Hubert Seminary emerged victorious by a majority decision, recording 237 points against Anglican SHS's 225 points.

The result sent St. Hubert Seminary through to the next stage while bringing Anglican SHS's campaign to an end.

The victorious debaters were visibly delighted with the result and expressed confidence in their performance.

Their comments suggested that they had entered the contest with belief in their preparation and ability to progress.

The second contest of the day featured Tepa SHS and Osei Adutwum SHS, with both schools battling not only for victory but also for a place in the next round of the competition.

The motion for the contest was: “Democracy has outlived its usefulness.” Tepa SHS argued for the motion, while Osei Adutwum SHS argued against it.

The debate generated strong arguments from both sides, as the schools explored the relevance of democracy and its place in modern society.

Tepa SHS sought to convince the judges that democracy had lost some of its usefulness, presenting arguments to support the motion.

Osei Adutwum SHS, however, challenged the proposition and defended the continued relevance of democratic governance.

As the contest unfolded, Osei Adutwum SHS gradually established greater control over the debate. Its speakers delivered arguments and rebuttals that resonated strongly with the judges, ultimately giving the school a commanding advantage.

At the end of the contest, Osei Adutwum SHS secured a unanimous decision, defeating Tepa SHS by 234 points to 191.

The convincing victory sparked excitement among the school's supporters, who celebrated as their team secured qualification to the 1/16 round.

Students from Adutwum SHS captured the mood after the contest, saying: “It’s a great feeling. We prepared and we have conquered.”

The result means Osei Adutwum SHS moves forward in the competition with renewed confidence, while Tepa SHS exits after a determined campaign.

The remaining schools will now look to build on their performances as they battle for places in the subsequent rounds and ultimately for the title of champions of the 8th edition of the LUV FM Kel-Charcoal Toothpaste High School Debate.

More exciting contests are expected in the coming days as the participating schools continue their quest for debate supremacy.

The 8th edition of the LUV FM Kel-Charcoal Toothpaste High School Debate is sponsored by Kelcharcoal Toothpaste, Didi Shito, Bigoo, The Seed Travelz, Serpo Mystical Pen, Verna Mineral Water, Jackson University College, Tamak, St. Ben Jewelry, Otuasekan Community Bank, and New Generation Investment Services

Ghana News.title: La Liga to inspect Celta Vigo’s pitch after fungus outbreak
Ghana News.content:
La Liga officials are set to carry out a pitch inspection at Celta Vigo's Estadio de Balaidos following a suspected fungus outbreak.

Celta are due to host Osasuna on Sunday night in their opening match of the 2026-27 season, kicking off at 20:30 BST.

Following reports in Spain of the outbreak, sources close to La Liga have told BBC Sport that the league are due to visit the 24,870-capacity stadium in Vigo in the next 24 hours to assess if the match can be played as scheduled.

The pitch is said to have been hit by a fungus infection that has damaged the playing surface, with Celta Vigo believed to have requested that the match is postponed.

Meanwhile, opponents Osasuna are said to be open to playing the fixture as scheduled.

Spain's national team played a friendly against Iraq at the Esadio de Balaidos in June ahead of their successful 2026 World Cup-winning campaign over the summer.

The stadium has been undergoing renovation works for more than a decade, with it planned to be among the 11 Spanish stadia used to co-host the 2030 World Cup alongside Portugal and Morocco.

Once renovation works are completed, the arena is set to increase its capacity to between 40,000 and 44,000.

Celta originally had the option to postpone the match due to striker Borja Iglesias reaching the World Cup final with Spain, but opted not too.

Three La Liga matches that were due to be played on the opening weekend, Valencia v Real Betis, Real Madrid v Real Sociedad and Barcelona v Athletic Club, have all been rescheduled for later in the month due to clubs having players involved in the World Cup final.

Ghana News.title: Rotten waste chokes Accra CBD as Tudu refuse lingers
Ghana News.content:
A growing heap of uncollected refuse at the Tudu trotro bus stop has turned into a public health hazard, with traders and commuters in the Accra Central Business District demanding urgent action.

The pile of waste, which has been left uncleared since Monday, has swelled over the past three days and now emits a strong stench that is making trading unbearable for shop owners in the area.

Tudu is one of the busiest commercial hubs in the CBD, with thousands of traders, passengers and pedestrians passing through daily. But the stench and flies from the refuse have forced some businesses to operate under difficult conditions. “We can no longer stand it. The smell is too much, especially in the afternoon. Customers also complain, and some don’t even want to stay,” a shop owner told Global Information Centre. As of 3:00 pm on Wednesday, the waste was still sitting at the bus stop with no sign of city authorities clearing it. Flies and stray dogs were seen around the dump, raising fears of cholera, malaria and other sanitation-related diseases.

The situation has sparked frustration among residents who question the effectiveness of the current sanitation drive in the capital. “If we cannot even clear one heap at Tudu in the heart of Accra, then are we really winning the sanitation battle?_” another trader asked.

Environmental health experts have repeatedly warned that uncleared waste in crowded areas like Tudu creates breeding grounds for disease and undermines government efforts to make Accra the cleanest city in Africa.

Traders are now appealing to the Accra Metropolitan Assembly and waste management companies to move in immediately and clear the refuse before the situation worsens.

Ghana News.title: Ghana receives final work plan for AU Champion on Gender and Development
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has received the final Work Plan for the African Union Champion on Gender and Development for 2026–2028, marking a major step towards translating the Champion’s mandate into concrete actions to advance gender equality and development across Africa.



The work plan was formally presented by the Director of the African Union Commission’s Women, Gender and Youth Directorate (WGYD), Ms Prudence Nonkululeko Ngwenya, at the close of a three-day Strategy Co-Creation and Validation Workshop held in Accra.



Presenting the outcomes of the workshop, Ms Ngwenya said participants had been deliberate in defining an innovative and impactful role for the Champion, particularly as Ghana prepares to assume leadership of the African Union.

She noted that gender equality remains central to AU Agenda 2063, economic growth and social development, with the Champion expected to mobilise political support and advocate for gender equality and women’s empowerment at the highest level.



Receiving the work plan on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama, the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, said the document should not be viewed as an end in itself but as a roadmap for action.



She said its value would ultimately be measured by its translation into concrete interventions, strengthened policies, mobilised resources and measurable improvements in the lives of women and girls across Africa.



Dr Lartey reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to supporting the AU Champion and highlighted recent strides in advancing gender equality, including the passage of the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Act, 2024 (Act 1121), the National Gender Policy (2025–2034), and Parliament’s approval of the African Union Convention on Ending Violence Against Women and Girls.



The three-day engagement focused on the Champion’s comparative advantage, vision and theory of change, strategic priorities, Presidential initiatives, implementation and partnerships, investment, monitoring and accountability.



The validated work plan is expected to provide a clear framework for coordinated action as Ghana works with the African Union Commission to advance gender equality and development across the continent.

Ghana News.title: Torres misses Barcelona training to finalise PSG move
Ghana News.content:
Spain's World Cup hero Ferran Torres has been given permission to miss Barcelona training to finalise a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

Torres, 26, scored an extra-time winner against Argentina to help Spain claim their second World Cup this summer.

He was due to return to training with the Catalan giants on Wednesday but will not, as a move to PSG gets closer.

The deal with PSG, who play Aston Villa in the Super Cup final on Wednesday night in Salzburg, is likely to be worth more than £40m.

Torres only has one year left on his contract at Barcelona, and some fans have been frustrated that the forward has spoken openly about the possibility of leaving the club.

Speaking on a media tour of the United States following Spain's World Cup win, he said: "I have a contract with Barcelona but, in football, you never know."

Asked directly about links with PSG, he added: "Every time these teams want you it's a good thing.

"You never know because in football everything can change in one minute, so I have to be ready for everything."

PSG have won the Champions League in the past two seasons and are managed by former Barcelona coach and player Luis Enrique.

The Parisians could lose Bradley Barcola this summer, with the forward wanted by Liverpool.

Torres has been at Barcelona since 2022 having previously spent two years at Manchester City. He has scored 25 goals in 65 appearances for Spain.

Ghana News.title: Xavi becomes first non-Dutch Netherlands coach since 1978
Ghana News.content:
Former Barcelona manager Xavi Hernández has been appointed the new head coach of the Netherlands on a four-year deal.

The 46-year-old, who played for Barcelona and Spain, will become the first non-Dutch coach to take charge of the Netherlands since Austrian coach Ernst Happel stepped down in 1978.

Ronald Koeman resigned as Netherlands manager following a last-32 defeat by Morocco at this summer's World Cup.

"I consider it a tremendous honour to become head coach of the Dutch national team," Xavi said.

"As someone who received his training at Barca's academy, with strong influences from Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, among others, I feel a special connection to Dutch football.

"You could say that I am partly a son of Dutch football. Other great coaches, especially Louis van Gaal, under whom I made my debut at Barca, and Frank Rijkaard, also played an important role in shaping me as a player and coach."

Former Liverpool head coach Arne Slot confirmed he held talks over the job but withdrew because he wants his next role to be in club football.

Xavi, who won three international trophies, was part of the Spain team that beat the Netherlands in the 2010 World Cup final.

He retired in 2019 and went into management with Al-Sadd before taking over at Barca in November 2021, where he won a La Liga title in his first full season in charge.

It will be Xavi's first managerial job since he stepped down from Barcelona in 2024.

Ghana News.title: Office of the Registrar of Companies fined GH¢240k for engaging unlicensed cybersecurity provider
Ghana News.content:
The Cyber Security Authority (CSA) has sanctioned the Office of the Registrar of Companies (ORC) and Purpleline Solutions Limited for breaches of Ghana’s cybersecurity requirements.

The ORC was fined GH¢240,000 for failing to comply with two directives requiring it, as a designated Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) institution, to engage only appropriately licensed Cybersecurity Service Providers (CSPs).

In a statement, the CSA said the ORC engaged Purpleline Solutions Limited, which was not licensed by the Authority to provide cybersecurity services, despite being specifically directed to engage a Tier 1 licensed CSP.

The Authority said it directed the ORC on June 15, 2026, to engage Tier 1 licensed CSPs to strengthen the security and resilience of its critical information infrastructure.

The ORC was subsequently required to provide details of its cybersecurity service providers, the Terms of Reference for its proposed Security Operations Centre (SOC), and relevant Public Procurement Authority approvals.

According to the CSA, the ORC nevertheless proceeded to engage Purpleline Solutions Limited, constituting a violation of Section 92 of the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038).

The Authority said the ORC was fined 10,000 penalty units for each of the two instances of non-compliance, amounting to GH¢240,000, and directed to comply with the outstanding directives within one month of receiving the sanction letter.

“The Authority determined that the ORC failed to comply with two separate directives issued by the CSA. Consequently, pursuant to Section 92(2) of Act 1038, the ORC has been fined Ten Thousand (10,000) penalty units for each instance of non-compliance, standing at GH₵ 240,000.00, and directed to comply with the outstanding directives within one month of receiving the CSA’s sanction letter,” part of the statement read.

The CSA also sanctioned Purpleline Solutions Limited for providing cybersecurity services without the required licence.

The company was fined 10,000 penalty units, equivalent to GH¢120,000, after the Authority determined that it had provided cybersecurity services without first obtaining the necessary licence.

The CSA noted that Purpleline applied for a cybersecurity service provider licence on July 15, 2026, after the Authority had established that the company had already been engaged by the ORC.

It stressed that an application for a licence does not authorise a company to operate as a Cybersecurity Service Provider.

“Entities are required to obtain the requisite license before commencing the provision of regulated cybersecurity services,” the statement read.

The Authority has warned institutions against engaging unlicensed cybersecurity service providers while cautioning companies against providing regulated cybersecurity services without the appropriate licence.

The CSA said organisations cannot engage an unlicensed provider and subsequently expect the provider to regularise its status.

“An application for a license is not the same as holding a license and does not authorise an entity to commence regulated cybersecurity operations,” the Authority emphasised in the statement.

The Authority has therefore directed designated Critical Information Infrastructure institutions, public-sector organisations and other entities covered by the Cybersecurity Act to verify both the licensing status and appropriate licence tier of cybersecurity service providers before awarding contracts or allowing them to commence work.

The CSA said it will continue to monitor compliance and take enforcement action against institutions that engage unlicensed providers, as well as companies that provide cybersecurity services without the requisite licence.

“Cybersecurity licensing is a legal requirement, not an administrative formality,” the Authority said, adding that it will use its regulatory powers to ensure organisations entrusted with critical systems and sensitive information meet their cybersecurity obligations.

Ghana News.title: Ghana–TradeMark Africa partnership renewal to boost trade and exports — Trade Minister
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry (MoTAI) and TradeMark Africa (TMA) have renewed their partnership through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at strengthening trade facilitation, boosting exports and supporting sustainable economic growth.



The renewed agreement reinforces the commitment of both institutions to deepen collaboration in implementing Ghana’s obligations under key trade frameworks, including the World Trade Organization (WTO) Trade Facilitation Agreement, the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) trade agenda.



The MoU was signed by the Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, and the Deputy Chief Executive Officer of TradeMark Africa, Allen Sophia Asiimwe.

It builds on an earlier partnership established in January 2023, which provided a strategic framework for advancing Ghana’s trade and economic development priorities.



Under the renewed partnership, TradeMark Africa and the Ministry will continue implementing the Ghana Country Programme Strategy, which focuses on impactful interventions in trade facilitation, regional integration, private sector competitiveness and improved market access.



The agreement will further support efforts to modernise Ghana’s border management systems, strengthen digital trade infrastructure, improve logistics networks and reduce the time and cost of moving goods along the Abidjan–Lagos Corridor.



It will also promote stronger standards and quality systems to enhance the competitiveness of Ghanaian exports, particularly agricultural and manufactured products.



A key focus of the partnership is to expand opportunities for women, young people and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to participate in regional and AfCFTA trade through inclusive trade interventions and improved access to trade finance. The agreement will also support Ghana’s preparedness for emerging green trade requirements.



Speaking on the impact of the partnership so far, Ms Ofosu-Adjare highlighted significant achievements, including the recent commissioning of improved border management systems at the Akanu–Noepe Joint Border Post.



She noted that the integrated digital customs systems, modern infrastructure and solar energy solutions introduced at the border had enabled 24-hour operations and helped reduce delays in the movement of goods.



In her remarks, Ms Asiimwe commended the Government, particularly the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, for its continued collaboration with TradeMark Africa and expressed optimism that the renewed partnership would further deepen cooperation and deliver greater results.



Beyond infrastructure and technology, the collaboration has supported traders and businesses by strengthening institutional capacity, training border officials and providing export-readiness support to SMEs.

More than 1,250 women and small-scale cross-border traders have benefited from support on AfCFTA procedures, simplified trade processes and safer trading environments.



The renewed MoU is expected to provide a platform for scaling up investments, increasing exports and advancing Ghana’s ambition of becoming a leading regional trade and investment hub. It also aligns with national priorities centred on private sector-led growth, industrialisation, job creation and the development of a resilient, export-driven economy.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
