World.title: Tartu University Hospital cutting back departments seeing fewer patients
World.content:
Some employees at the hospital fear layoffs, but the hospital's management says staff will initially be offered the opportunity to take up other positions.

Several employees at Tartu University Hospital say there is anxiety and uncertainty among staff over how work will be organized in the future, amid fears of layoffs. Some employees have even taken out legal expenses insurance out of concern that they could lose their jobs. Although no official notices have yet reached the maternity ward, staff there are prepared for the possibility that 14 people could be laid off. One daytime midwife position was already eliminated in the spring.

Saima Hinno, a member of the hospital's management board, confirmed that work arrangements are being reviewed and positions will be eliminated if necessary, but said she could not say whether layoffs would take place or how many people they might affect.

"I can't give a specific number at the moment because, on the one hand, some reviews are still underway, while in some cases people have already moved to other positions. Whether the number ends up being that high, lower or higher, time will tell, as will the funding model we have been given. We also can't keep more people in positions than we have the funding or volume of treatment to support," Hinno said.

Hinno did not specify which other positions and departments could be affected by the restructuring. She said, however, that demand for staff has increased in the mental health field. The hospital is therefore also offering employees the opportunity to move into positions where there is a greater shortage of workers.

"We can talk about specialist nurses and whether they need additional training, more experience or further studies, because that would allow them to provide services for which there is greater demand. Layoffs are always subject to discussions between both sides and must be justified, because presumably there was a need for a position before and now that need no longer exists. Employees are always offered work they can do within the scope of their qualifications or with additional training, and we will certainly offer that," Hinno said.

So far, maternity ward employees have been offered the opportunity to work as operating room nurses or move to the hospital pharmacy. Many, however, would prefer to continue working in the profession for which they trained and maintain their professional qualifications.

According to a board member of the Estonian Midwives Association (EÄÜ), the decline in the number of births has not actually reduced midwives' workloads, as the profile of the average person giving birth has changed over the years, making deliveries more complicated.

"A midwife's work in a maternity ward certainly can't be assessed solely by how many births they actually attend. You also have to consider how much midwifery care each person giving birth may need overall. If we eliminate one position, regardless of where maternity care is provided, the workload of the colleagues who remain will certainly increase significantly. It may also be that some issues only become apparent once the changes are actually implemented. If staffing is reduced and there is a very large amount of work within a very short period of time — maternity care is an emergency healthcare service — unfortunately, not all of the consequences can be foreseen," EÄÜ board member Käthlin Vahtel said.

Neither North Estonia Medical Center nor the Women's Clinic at East Tallinn Central Hospital is planning similar changes to positions or layoffs.

World.title: Experts warn Estonia must act soon to fix health fund deficit or face higher patient costs
World.content:
Experts say the current government cannot postpone solving the Health Insurance Fund's financial troubles for future administrations. Delaying decisions may lead to a situation where people will have to pay more out of pocket for medical care.

Estonia has a solidarity‑based healthcare system, meaning wage earners cover the treatment costs of children and the elderly. In a rapidly aging society, social tax revenue is no longer sufficient to fund healthcare, and the Health Insurance Fund has been running a deficit of nearly €100 million for several years.

Last week, Minister of Social Affairs Karmen Joller said this government will not change healthcare financing. The fund's reserves should last until 2029, and only then will it be time to decide.

"From my perspective, these decisions were unavoidable already today, because the expectation that using reserves will preserve access to care at the current level is actually an illusion," said healthcare analyst Kaija Kasekamp.

According to her, Estonia must now decide whether to continue with solidarity‑based health insurance or whether people will have to start paying more themselves.

"International experience and research show that systems based on solidarity and equal access have better health outcomes and, in fact, lower total healthcare costs," Kasekamp said.

President Alar Karise kohtumine haiglajuhtidega Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi /ERR

Priit Perens, head of Tartu University Hospital, said hospitals will manage for the next couple of years, but problems are expected later.

"The issue is that healthcare services are becoming more expensive. Patients' and the entire population's expectations for service quality are rising. Both lead to additional cost growth," Perens said.

He added that while more efficient solutions can always be found, savings alone are not enough to fill the €100 million gap in the Health Insurance Fund's budget. Finding additional funding is, in his view, a matter of societal agreement — and if society does not consider it necessary, access to medical care may increasingly depend on a patient's ability to pay.

"The upper end of healthcare services requires such large investments that if only three people in Estonia can afford a specific service and others cannot, they will likely go abroad to buy that service. We simply cannot — and neither can the private sector — make such investments," Perens said.

Triinu-Mari Ots Autor/allikas: PIret Kooli/ERR

Family doctor Triinu‑Mari Ots said it is the responsibility of the state and healthcare organizers to explain to people what kind of care can realistically be provided. Currently, this burden has been shifted onto family doctors.

"Unfortunately, at the primary‑care level, a lot of time is spent in one‑on‑one conversations with patients explaining what we are currently unable to provide, because it is not needs‑based nor affordable for the state," Ots said.

World.title: Senior Iraqi security delegation heads to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A high-level Iraqi security delegation will travel to Riyadh on Thursday, August 13, 2026, to conduct talks regarding recent cross-border drone strikes targeting petroleum infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, according to a senior government source.

The delegation will be led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari, Director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, alongside Iraqi National Intelligence Service (INIS) Chief Hamid Al-Shatri. The trip follows a reciprocal visit to Baghdad days earlier by Saudi Intelligence Chief Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan.

Key Security & Diplomatic Developments

High-Level Delegation: Led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari and Intelligence Chief Hamid Al-Shatri to establish joint intelligence-sharing protocols with Riyadh.

Incident Background: Late last month, the Saudi Ministry of Defense reported intercepting several drones originating from Iraqi territory targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

Domestic Investigation: Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Falih al-Zaidi ordered a formal military investigation into the launch origins following the Saudi allegations.

Diplomatic Mediation: The visit comes after international and regional mediation restored diplomatic channels following the cancellation of Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s planned trip to Riyadh late last month amid joint U.S.-Saudi strikes inside Iraq.

Regional Position: During a recent bilateral meeting in Amman between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Riyadh reaffirmed support for Iraq while stressing the necessity that Iraqi territory not be utilized as a platform for aggression against neighboring states.

The bilateral security summit aims to reinforce radar tracking, anti-drone intelligence sharing, and border surveillance between Baghdad and Riyadh.

While the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” denied responsibility for the Saudi oil facility strikes, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s administration is taking direct steps to prevent unauthorized non-state launches, safeguard Iraqi sovereignty, and protect diplomatic and economic ties with Riyadh.

World.title: Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — President of the Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Faiq Zidan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Syria on Thursday, August 13, 2026, marking a landmark first-of-its-kind judicial mission to Damascus, according to a senior official source.

The high-level visit aims to hold structured talks with Syrian judicial authorities to address shared legal frameworks, cross-border judicial coordination, counter-terrorism extradition agreements, and legal mechanisms regulating bilateral trade corridors.

World.title: Iraq Transport Ministry reports 95% completion of Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani met with the Parliamentary Transport and Communications Committee on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to review execution milestones across strategic infrastructure projects, including the Development Road, the Grand Fao Port, and national rail modernization.

During the executive session, Al-Hasani presented technical updates on the 1,200-kilometer Development Road Project, confirming that primary design phases are near completion, with railway engineering blueprints reaching 95% and highway transit designs at 85%.

Key Operational Metrics & Project Milestones

Development Road Project: Designs for the 1,200 km transit corridor are nearly complete (95% for railway tracks, 85% for highways). The MOU executed with Turkey serves as a preliminary framework with no current financial or legal obligations.

Grand Fao Port: Submerged tunnel construction reached 86% completion, alongside advanced structural work across five main container berths.

Rail Network Modernization: Ministry teams are actively pursuing the rehabilitation of the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia railway corridor extending toward the Syrian border.

Maritime Fleet Mobilization: State maritime companies confirmed readiness to deploy Iraqi vessels to transport crude oil and refined petroleum products to support alternative national export strategies.

Administrative & Executive Actions: Al-Hasani confirmed the suspension of Iraqi Airways’ former Director-General and two deputies following an internal investigative audit.

Legislative Alignment: Agreement reached to draft amendments to Transport Law No. 80 of 1983 and establish a joint parliamentary-executive committee holding weekly meetings to update transport regulations.

The meeting highlights Iraq’s strategy to transform into a central logistics bridge connecting the Gulf to Europe, bypassing maritime transit chokepoints.

By pairing the Grand Fao Port’s advancing infrastructure with overland rail links extending north to Turkey and west through the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia line toward Syria, the Ministry of Transport is laying the groundwork for integrated commercial supply chains across Eurasia.

World.title: MP Abdul Jabbar proposes 145 km pipeline to boost Basra crude to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Independent MP and Secretary-General of the Fao–Zakho Coalition, Amer Abdul-Jabbar, proposed a plan on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to construct a 145-kilometer oil pipeline link to transport Basra crude north toward Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal.

Abdul-Jabbar stated via social media that the proposed missing link would instantly increase Iraq’s northern export capacity by 150,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd). To avoid drawing on the federal budget during the ongoing liquidity crisis, he advocated launching a “National Volunteer Effort,” utilizing surplus piping from state-owned enterprises alongside logistical backing from private contractors operating under Ministry of Oil contracts.

Key Technical & Strategy Highlights

Proposed Pipeline Link: A 145 km strategic bypass connecting southern oilfields in Basra directly to northern export routes toward the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Capacity Increase: Designed to boost crude export flows by 150,000 to 300,000 bpd, mitigating bottlenecks caused by Persian Gulf shipping disruptions.

Zero-Cost Volunteer Framework: Proposed execution via a “National Volunteer Effort” using inventory audits of unused piping across state firms and private sector contractor support.

Existing Ministry Export Strategy: Complements Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair’s August 9 plan to export 750,000 bpd to Ceyhan via: 450,000 bpd pumped through the Strategic Pipeline after rehabilitating the PS3 pump station in Najaf and K3 in Haditha. 300,000 bpd transported via road tankers (including 200,000 bpd through KAR Group and 100,000 bpd under a secondary contract).

Long-Term Iraqi-Turkish Energy Framework: Ministry of Oil is finalizing a 1-year interim agreement with Ankara, paving the way for a 10- to 20-year strategic partnership involving Turkish BOTAŞ and BP in developing Kirkuk oilfields.

Abdul-Jabbar’s proposal comes as the Ministry of Oil accelerates alternative land-based export channels to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Minister Khudair previously confirmed that Iraq’s State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) and Turkey’s BOTAŞ are actively inspecting and rehabilitating the northern export system to handle between 500,000 and 750,000 bpd. Implementing the 145 km bypass link could offer Baghdad an immediate, low-cost mechanism to restore crude cash flows while long-term pipeline infrastructure is constructed toward Syria and Jordan.

World.title: Meta meets its own ‘tobacco’ moment in court
World.content:
Oakland – With billions of users around the world, Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media’s big tobacco moment.

After a coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps, four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.

Top prosecutors of those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.

Meta “strongly disagrees with these allegations” and is “confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people,” a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has “listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement.”

Although it’s not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.

“It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s,” Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley’s Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.

While these cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, just like when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.

By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.

– ‘Protecting teens’ –

Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with s featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as “Joe Camel.”

Jury selection begins today in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco and opening statements are expected to begin August 18.

Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach $1 billion.

In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta’s apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as $1.4 trillion, close to Meta’s entire market value which hovers around $1.5 trillion.

Despite the eye-popping number, money isn’t Meta’s biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.

“The huge issue here is reputational harm” and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.

“Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning,” as well, he said.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.

The case could be “the beginning of a broader reckoning” for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.

It will be important to see the “gap” between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.

Meta is “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” Meta told AFP last week.

With so many plaintiffs suing Meta and other social media companies, these lawsuits could potentially “go on for decades,” Joralemon said.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.

World.title: Colombia rescuers find woman alive as quake death toll passes 240
World.content:
Pereira – Colombian rescuers pulled a 32-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building Tuesday, sparking cheers and applause as exhausted crews raced to find more survivors from the country’s strongest earthquake in a century.

Daniela Largo was carried from the wreckage wrapped in a blue blanket as rescuers embraced and relatives shouted out with joy.

The rescue came as soldiers, firefighters and volunteers searched collapsed buildings across western Colombia after a 7.4-magnitude quake killed at least 241 people and injured more than 1,600.

“We were losing hope and then we received a call,” said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.

Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

“Thanks to him, today we’re happy,” she said. “At home her 12-year-old son is waiting for her.”

In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.

As darkness fell, families prepared to sleep in parks as aftershocks rattled damaged neighborhoods where entire blocks had been reduced to rubble.

The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia’s largest disaster responses in years.

“The house came down on top of us. I wasn’t able to get out,” said Beatriz Arcos, who was trapped with her husband and mother beneath their collapsed condominium.

“It took about an hour to get us out.” Arcos said she was hospitalized after a concrete block fell on her back. Her husband and mother were also injured.

In Cali, residents armed with picks, shovels and their bare hands joined firefighters in digging through collapsed buildings.

Rescuers stopped every few minutes to call into the rubble and listen for any response.

“We’re doing this with our hands, with gloves” said volunteer Pablo Cesar Ruiz “It’s sad to see time slipping away.”

In Pereira, army units and sniffer dogs combed through twisted concrete and exposed steel.

At one site, a rescue squad leader abruptly raised his fist, stopping workers so they could listen for signs of life.

Volunteers formed human chains, passing bricks and chunks of masonry hand-to-hand to clear paths into collapsed structures.

– ‘So much effort’ –

For many families, the desperate search was becoming a vigil.

“My aunt lived there. She’s under the rubble,” said Jorge Gonzalez, standing beside a collapsed building in Pereira.

“I arrived yesterday and I haven’t left, and until they find her body I don’t intend to leave here.”

While some families waited for news of missing relatives, others were grappling with the loss of homes, possessions and livelihoods.

“We lost everything,” said Stella Galvis, fighting back tears after escaping the collapse of her home.

“We survived by a miracle, since I managed to get my little boy out and my partner managed to get out too.”

From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.

Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.

On one mound of debris, a young couple climbed over broken masonry searching for belongings.

They recovered a box from inside a child’s bright red bedside table.

Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.

One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.

“We lost everything, but we’re alive,” said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.

“We’ve never had to do this before, to depend on someone else to help us. It’s amazing how life can change.”

Others struggled to come to terms with losing homes built over decades.

“You buy a little house with so much effort, spending 40, 50 years struggling to get yourself that house, you finally get it and in just a few days it all goes down the drain,” said 79-year-old Jaime Alzate.

In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.

Yet amid the destruction, many Colombians mobilized to help.

Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.

“It’s about wanting to help your community, your city and your country,” said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.

President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.

As aftershocks continued to rattle damaged cities, rescue crews pressed on through the ruins, hoping more voices, taps or whistles might still emerge.

World.title: Passengers rescued as second ferry in days catches fire in Indonesia
World.content:
Mataram – A navy vessel and other ships rushed in Wednesday to rescue over 100 people from a ferry on fire off the tourist island of Bali, officials said, in the second such incident in days.

There were no immediate reports of casualties among the passengers and crew, with at least 114 people on board, according to the manifest.

The passenger ferry had been sailing from Bali to the next-door island of Lombok when it caught fire in the early morning hours.

Muhamad Hariyadi, head of the search and rescue agency at Mataram on Lombok island, said the total number of passengers on board was being verified.

He said passengers were evacuated on at least three different vessels, including a navy ship and another ferry.

Search and rescue vessels were at the scene and a helicopter was conducting surveillance from the air.

“As of now, we have not received any report of casualties,” Hariyadi told Metro TV.

“We have approached the ship and confirmed that all passengers are no longer on board,” he added. “We visually see no passengers on the ship.”

Last week, five people died when a ferry caught fire off Java island.

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia — an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that rely heavily on boat connections.

Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi, last month.

Four bodies were recovered, but the search operation ended with 14 others still officially missing.

World.title: Charges dropped against Bondi Beach attack hero
World.content:
Sydney – Australian police dropped assault charges on Wednesday against a man lauded for his bravery during last year’s mass shooting at Bondi Beach.

Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed was hailed as a hero after footage showed him disarming a gunman during the December 14 attack, which killed 15 people at a Jewish festival.

Ahmed was earlier this year accused of stalking and assaulting his father, charges he denied.

Both charges were withdrawn after a brief hearing on Wednesday, court documents showed.

Ahmed ducked between parked cars as the Bondi shooting unfolded, grabbing one of the two gunmen and wresting away his weapon in an effort to stop the killing.

He sustained gunshot wounds in the attack.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese would later meet Ahmed in person, describing him as a “true Australian hero” and an inspiration to all.

World.title: Amid tariff fear, Swadeshi Jagaran Manch says shun US brands
World.content:
RSS-affiliated Swadeshi Jagran Manch has called for a boycott of American products

NEW DELHI: From beverages to social media, Swadeshi Jagaran Manch has sought to turn the latest US tariff threat into a wider "swadeshi" campaign, calling on Indians to boycott American products and platforms.The RSS-affiliated economic body reacted to the US Senate legislation which, according to SJM, would empower the US President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries making significant purchases of Russian oil. It said the move amounted to an attempt to dictate India's energy choices. It also urged the govt to reconsider two recent policy moves which it claimed favoured US companies - allowing FDI e-commerce entities greater flexibility over export inventory and merchant discount rates on certain UPI transactions.

World.title: SC orders CBI probe into Chhattisgarh custodial death
World.content:
It also directed the state govt to pay Rs 25 lakh as interim compensation to the family of the deceased

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Accusing top administrative and police officials of Chhattisgarh of trying to "cover up" a custodial death case, Supreme Court on Wednesday expressed lack of confidence in the state administration's catching the errant officials and handed over the case to CBI. It also directed the state govt to pay Rs 25 lakh as interim compensation to the family of the deceased.A bench said that the case warranted immediate registration of an FIR and a thorough investigation into the circumstances leading to the death of Shravan Suryavanshi, which the state authorities had "conveniently and deliberately tried to cover up".It said that state authorities were adopting a "dilatory approach" and could not be trusted to conduct an impartial probe. Shravan was arrested on Jan 18, 2024, after he was found in possession of raw Mahua liquor and lodged at Central Jail, Bilaspur, from where he was referred to hospital on Jan 21.He died a day later.Referring to the high court order, bench said the death of the deceased was on account of violence perpetrated on him in custody. In compliance with the court's directive, the DGP, director general (Prisons) and principal secretary (Home), virtually appeared before the court, which found their explanation "perfunctory and pedantic"."In this backdrop, the stance of blissful ignorance taken by the senior officers of the State of Chhattisgarh, including the Principal Secretary (Home), the DGP and the DG (Prisons), is sacrilegious and reflects a disturbing disregard for the statutory procedure governing custodial deaths. The explanation offered that neither any police action nor any disciplinary action was taken against the persons responsible because the judicial inquiry report had not been served upon the police officials is a cover-up story and an attempt to pull the wool over the Court's eyes," bench said."We have seen the medical reports of the deceased Shravan and find that a clear attempt was made to mislead the inquiry because, in the medical report prepared at jail at the time of his death, the cause of death was recorded as cardiopulmonary arrest with aspiration pneumonitis, with the diagnosis being alcoholic withdrawal and delirium tremens," it said.The court thereafter asked CBI director to ensure immediate registration of a regular case over Shravan's custodial death, ordering that the investigation be entrusted to a senior officer and conducted expeditiously. The report of the investigating officer is to be placed before the court on the next date of hearing. It further said that the conduct of state officials concerned in failing to take appropriate steps pursuant to submission of the judicial inquiry report should also be examined and made a part of the investigation.

World.title: PIL seeks policy to balance right to protest & commute
World.content:
SC to consider identifying protest sites that wonât affect daily commute of people

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: If citizens have a fundamental right to assemble and protest peacefully, should it interfere with fundamental rights of those who are not part of the protest to commute safely to their offices or go about their daily lives?This conflict of fundamental rights of protesters and other citizens was highlighted by advocate V Elanchezian, who appeared for PIL petitioner Aalok Mohan, and requested a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant to direct govt to frame a model national framework for providing facilities and guidelines for regulating protests so that they don't interfere with the rights of others.Citing population growth and urbanisation, the petitioner said, "Despite these developments, there exists no comprehensive national framework prescribing minimum planning standards for infrastructure relating to peaceful public assemblies. Consequently, public authorities across the country adopt differing administrative practices, often leading to avoidable conflict between the constitutional rights of demonstrators and those of commuters, patients, school children, emergency services and the public. ""The issue is not whether citizens have the right to assemble peacefully, for that right is protected by the Constitution. The issue is whether constitutional governance now requires govt to examine and formulate a comprehensive national policy providing minimum standards for planning and developing civic infrastructure that facilitates peaceful public assemblies while ensuring harmonious protection of all Fundamental Rights," the petition said.The bench said it would consider the issue flagged by the petitioner along with other pending petitions seeking identification of proper protest sites with basic amenities, including water, washroom, food and medical assistance, so as not to inconvenience or impede daily commuters from reaching their workplaces or destinations on time.

World.title: Govt asks Air India to ‘take responsibility’, tells DGCA to improve dope checks
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Govt has warned Air India to improve its oversight on operations and âtake responsibilityâ for ensuring safety. The aviation ministry has also ordered DGCA to quickly revise its drug-testing rules and increase the percentage of personnel who must undergo mandatory testing.

The govt has also directed the aviation regulator to enforce tougher penalties against those testing positive for ârealâ drugs, while giving additional chances to those whose positive results stem from medicines.

The pilot-in-command of Air Indiaâs badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight with 145 people onboard is learnt to have told investigators he had been prescribed sleeping pills due to personal problems which, he claims, led to the positive dope tests.

His onboard behaviour is also underthe scanner after the cabin crew complained against him.

âThe final report of AIâs last June Ahmedabad crash in which 260 people lost their lives is not yet out and then something like this happens with Air India. Govt has taken a very serious view of what happened on AI 2379 and heads will roll. Aviation secretary Samir Sinha has told the AI brass in clear terms that the airline needs to take responsibility and that people found guilty by the probe will not be spared,â said a person familiar with the discussions.





The anger stems from the fact that AI 2379 may have narrowly avoided a disaster. While cruising near Odisha, the aircraft reportedly got a series of warnings â many in quick succession â related to the three hydraulics systems, doors and elevator (which makes an aircraft ascend and descend). Autopilot had also tripped off. It had suffered a loss of altitude during cruise, injuring many on board.

An Airbus team is in India to examine the reported issues along with officials of the French aviation regulator, with Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau probing whether these warnings were real or spurious and what had caused them.

Pilots want Airbus to give a detailed explanation of the same.

âTaking pilot-in-commandâs alleged state and the multiple warnings, we compliment the co-pilot for ensuring the aircraft landed safely. This incident will lead to multiple changes to strengthen safety,â said a senior govt official.

Many pilots feel the warnings âshould have beenâ false as there was no way an aircraft suffering multiple whammies could have flown uneventfully for about two hours to land safely at its destination instead of the crew opting to land at the nearest airport.

Dope test changes

Senior pilots say there is a problem with the DGCAâs civil aviation requirement on the subject titled âprocedure for examination of the aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substancesâ as it treats crew members testing positive due to taking some medicines the same as those who are addicted to ârealâ drugs or take them recreationally.

World.title: J&K SIA reopens probe into 1990 killings of Kashmiri Pandit poet, nurse
World.content:
On June 29, SIA filed a chargesheet in the abduction, torture and killing of Bhat

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Sarvanand Kaul Premi was a poet. Sarla Bhat was a nurse. Both were Kashmiri Pandits who stayed behind when militancy erupted and were killed in 1990. More than three decades later, J&K policeâs SIA revived unresolved cases from the Valleyâs darkest years. The agency searched Wednesday nine locations in its probe into the abduction-murder of Premi and his younger son, weeks after filing a chargesheet in Bhatâs killing.Premi, 66, a poet, teacher and Gandhian, and Verinder were abducted from their village, Soaf Shali near Kokernag, on Apr 30, 1990. They were shot dead the next day. Five days later, the grief-stricken Kaul family left Kashmir, never to return.State Investigation Agencyâs searches were linked to FIR No. 45/1990 registered at Dooru police station in Anantnag. SIA is pursuing militancy-era cases that had lain cold for decades.On June 29, SIA filed a chargesheet in the abduction, torture and killing of Bhat, 27, a staff nurse in the neonatology ward at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences in Srinagar. She was allegedly abducted by JKLF from SKIMS Habba Khatoon Hostel on Apr 18, 1990, and taken to Illahibagh-Lal Bazar, tortured and shot dead.Her bullet-riddled body was found the next day at Omer Colony Malabagh in downtown Srinagar.Born in Soaf Shali in 1924, Premi joined Khadi Bhandar after completing his education and became associated with Mahatma Gandhiâs Swadeshi movement. His association with Kashmiri poet Ghulam Ahmad Mahjoor inspired his literary career. He translated Rabindranath Tagoreâs âGitanjaliâ into Kashmiri and the Bhagavad Gita and Ramayana into Kashmiri and Urdu, and advocated secularism and interfaith harmony.J&K govt under then-CM Farooq Abdullah posthumously awarded Premi a gold medal in 1997 for his contribution to Kashmiri literature and communal harmony.The killings from Kashmirâs violent spring of 1990 were part of a wider wave of hostility against Kashmiri Pandits after militancy erupted, driving a mass exodus of the community from the Valley. In 2010, J&K govt under then-CM Omar Abdullah told the assembly that 209 Kashmiri Pandits had been murdered since 1990.

World.title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann meets Governor; seeks 10-day parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara on "humanitarian grounds"
World.content:
Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Wednesday met with the Governor to recommend a 10-day parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara on humanitarian grounds, citing the deteriorating health of the prisoner's mother.

Jagtar Singh Hawara is currently serving a life sentence for his involvement in the 1995 assassination of the then Punjab chief minister Beant Singh.

Speaking to the media after the meeting, the chief minister stated that the recommendation was made to allow Hawara to meet his mother, who has not seen him in over three decades.

"A recommendation was made recently regarding the matter of granting parole to Jagtar Singh Hawara so that, on humanitarian grounds, he could be given parole as his mother's health is not well.

His mother has a desire to meet him after 31 years," CM Mann said.

The chief minister explained that since the case is being heard in the Union Territory, the Governor's role is pivotal in forwarding the request to the Central Government.

"I met the Governor today because as the case is being heard in the UT, the Governor will have an important role and the matter will be sent to the Centre. The final decision rests with the Centre, but we have requested a 10-day parole," he added.





Addressing potential concerns regarding security and public order, CM Mann informed that he has provided a formal assurance to the administration.

"In this regard, we have assured the Governor that we will not allow the atmosphere to be spoiled in any way and the situation will remain under control," the CM asserted.

According to the chief minister, the Governor has responded positively to the request and promised to expedite the administrative formalities.

"The Governor has assured that he will speak with the Home Secretary of the Government of India today itself to complete the formalities, and Hawara will receive relief soon. The Punjab government will send whatever necessary documents are required from their side," Mann stated.

Earlier on August 9, CM Mann wrote to Governor Gulab Chand Kataria regarding the same.

"It has been brought to my notice that Mr Jagtar Singh Hawara's mother is not in good health due to age-related health problems. Mr Jagtar Singh Hawara has also filed CRWP No. 3868/2026 in the Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court, Chandigarh, seeking direction to release him on parole. The Hon'ble Court has also directed to consider his parole application. Therefore, on the basis of human compassion, I would like to request you to grant 10-day parole as soon as possible," the letter read.

World.title: Assam floods: Toll rises to 103; 87,000 remain affected in four districts
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The flood situation in

showed signs of improvement on Wednesday, with the number of people affected falling to around 87,000 across four districts. However, the death toll from this year's floods rose to 103 after two more people died in the past 24 hours.

The latest figures from the Assam State Disaster Management Authority showed that one person drowned in Sivasagar and another in Karbi Anglong.

Around 86,800 people are still affected by the floods in Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon and Sivasagar. Golaghat remains the worst-hit district, with more than 42,000 people affected. Nagaon has around 20,000 affected residents, while Sivasagar has about 15,000.

The situation has nevertheless improved compared with Tuesday, when nearly 1.13 lakh people were affected across the four districts.

Authorities are continuing relief operations in the affected areas. A total of 79 relief camps and distribution centres are currently operating across five districts, providing assistance to 13,011 people.

Over the past 24 hours, relief agencies distributed nearly 96.55 quintals of rice, 18.26 quintals of dal, 5.41 quintals of salt and more than 204 litres of mustard oil among flood-affected families.

Despite the improvement, the floods continue to damage homes, farmland and infrastructure.





According to ASDMA, 433 villages remain underwater, while more than 10,884 hectares of crop land have been damaged across the state.

Floodwaters have also damaged embankments, roads, bridges and other infrastructure in several districts.

The Dhansiri River at Numaligarh continues to flow above the danger mark, adding to concerns in the affected areas.

The floods have also affected livestock. More than 32,900 domestic animals and poultry have been impacted across Assam.

While the overall number of people affected has declined, the rising death toll and continuing damage to villages, farmland and infrastructure show that the flood crisis is far from over.

World.title: China says India border 'generally stable' amid tensions in Arunachal
World.content:
China said Wednesday that the situation along the India-China border was âgenerally stable at the momentâ, while declining to confirm reports of increased Chinese military activity in disputed areas near Arunachal Pradesh.

Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks at a regular press briefing in Beijing in response to questions about videos circulating on Indian social media that purportedly showed heightened Chinese military activity along the border.

Guo said China and India had held the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on Border Affairs the previous week. He said both sides had agreed to maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels and work together to preserve peace and tranquillity along the border.

The comments came a day after India reiterated that its border with China remained a matter of serious concern and that maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control was essential to the broader relationship between the two countries.

The Chinese response also came amid reports of heightened military activity by Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradeshâs Upper Subansiri region. Beijing claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of what it calls âSouth Tibetâ, a claim consistently rejected by New Delhi.





India had separately pushed back against Chinaâs objections to New Delhi formally identifying 27 locations and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard Indian names. The Ministry of External Affairs said the state was an âinalienable and integralâ part of India and that nothing could change that reality.

The latest exchanges come as India and China continue efforts to stabilise ties that deteriorated sharply after the 2020 Galwan Valley clashes and a prolonged military standoff along the border.

The two countries reached a disengagement agreement covering the remaining friction points at Depsang and Demchok in October 2024.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping subsequently held talks in Kazan, followed by further diplomatic efforts aimed at improving bilateral relations.

World.title: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, youngest person to hold role, to leave at month’s end
World.content:
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, the youngest person to hold the role, will leave at month’s end, U.S. President Donald Trump announced on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).

Ms. Leavitt, 28, just recently returned to the White House after taking a brief leave for the birth of her second child in May.

Ms. Leavitt has been one of the most visible advocates of Mr. Trump’s “Make America Great Again” movement. The Republican president described her as one of his “most trusted aides” in a social media post announcing her departure.

He said Ms. Leavitt “will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family, a decision I totally understand and respect! Karoline will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party, as we work to defy History, and conclusively win the Midterm Elections.”

Ms. Leavitt recently returned to work after taking leave following the birth of her second child, a daughter, in May. She also has a two-year-old son.

“The truth is since returning to the White House after the birth of my daughter, I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary — and that is why I have ultimately made the bittersweet decision to depart the White House and embark on a new chapter in my life,” Ms. Leavitt said in a social media post.

Mr. Trump did not outline plans for who might replace her in the high-profile role.

She worked as a spokesperson for MAGA Inc., a super PAC supporting Mr. Trump, before joining his 2024 campaign. In 2022, she ran for Congress in New Hampshire, winning a 10-way Republican primary before losing to incumbent Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas.

During Mr. Trump’s first term in office, Leavitt worked as a press aide in the White House press office. She then became communications director for New York Republican Rep. Elise Stefanik.

Ms. Leavitt briefed from the White House press room less frequently than some of her recent predecessors. Mr. Trump, who regularly engages with reporters during White House events and during his travels, primarily deployed Ms. Leavitt to Fox News and other conservative news outlets to trumpet his agenda and take shots at Democrats and the mainstream media.

Mr. Trump’s first-term press secretaries were Sean Spicer and Sarah Huckabee Sanders, who were known for quarrelling with reporters. Another, Stephanie Grisham, never held a briefing. Her successor, Kayleigh McEnany, often lectured the news media during her appearances in the press briefing room.

World.title: Delhi High Court seeks clarity over Meta’s policy on access to Rights Manager
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) sought clarity from Meta over its policy governing access to its Rights Manager tool, after concerns were raised that fraudulent actors have allegedly exploited the platform’s copyright-protection mechanism to target original content.

Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani directed Meta to place on record its norms and eligibility criteria for granting access to Rights Manager, along with the grounds on which applications for the tool may be rejected.

The directions came during the hearing of a suit filed by content creator and business coach Mohit Kumar, who operates the social media handle Rise With Mohit.

Mr. Kumar, represented by advocates Himanshu Goyal and Muskaan Garg, alleged that scammers first copied and uploaded his original videos to Meta’s Rights Manager, falsely presenting themselves as the rights holders, and then relied on those registrations to have copyright strikes issued against Mr. Kumar’s accounts.

Applied thrice

The counsel submitted that his client had applied for access to Rights Manager on three occasions but was rejected without being given any specific reason. They pointed out that creators with relatively smaller audiences had been granted access to the tool, while established creators with substantial viewership, engagement and commercial collaborations were allegedly being denied it.

The counsel further submitted that, in Mr. Kumar’s case, the consequences of the alleged fraudulent content removals extended beyond the restoration of the content, affecting his audience engagement, commercial collaborations and ability to sell his courses.

Meta’s counsel informed the court that the copyright strikes in dispute had been reversed after technical verification and that content removed pursuant to those strikes had been restored. Meta also stated that Mr. Kumar’s accounts had not been suspended and continued to remain accessible.

Justice Bhambhani observed that concerns surrounding the misuse of copyright enforcement mechanisms appeared to be recurring across cases involving content creators and warranted closer examination. The court noted that the issue was contributing to an increasing number of disputes and litigation. The matter has been listed for September 24, when similar cases are also listed.

World.title: For Independence Day Reception (At Home), Rashtrapati Bhavan to showcase country’s cultural heritage
World.content:
Rashtrapati Bhavan, the official residence and office of the President of India, will host the Independence Day Reception (At Home) on August 15 as a celebration of the country’s cultural diversity and traditions of environmental stewardship.

The Hindu Independence Day Edition

“Under President Droupadi Murmu, Rashtrapati Bhavan has increasingly served as a national platform for showcasing India’s artistic traditions through State Receptions, banquets for foreign dignitaries and programmes such as the Artists-in-Residence initiative. The 2026 reception will focus on the living cultural traditions of Chhattisgarh, Goa, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, highlighting the relationship between communities, culture and nature,” said a release issued by the President’s House.

Folk dances, music

Around 35 artists from the four States will present folk dances and musical traditions, including Maharashtra’s Lavani and Songhi Mukhawate, Chhattisgarh’s Gedi and Gaur Madiya, Madhya Pradesh’s Bhagoria and Baiga Karma, and Goa’s Samai and Ghode Modni.

The performances reflect diverse community traditions. Gedi, performed on bamboo stilts during Chhattisgarh’s Hareli festival, showcases agility and balance, while Gaur Madiya of Bastar reflects tribal valour. Bhagoria and Baiga Karma embody social, agricultural and nature-linked traditions. Samai features performers balancing brass lamps, while Ghode Modni recalls the bravery of Goan warriors.

The musical programme will unfold as a cultural journey through forests, villages, temples and coastal landscapes, culminating in a shared performance by musicians from all four States. It has been curated by Chhattisgarh folk artist Rakesh Kumar Tiwari, a Sangeet Natak Akademi Award recipient.

The theme will extend to décor and cuisine. Table runners will feature Bagh Print, Khunn, Kunbi textiles and Soura traditions. The menu will include regional specialities such as Indori Poha, Patoleo, Mini Farra, Bafauri, Khamang Kakdi, Dodol and Kodo Millet Kheer.

The reception seeks to demonstrate how India’s cultural heritage and environmental traditions continue to reinforce one another.

World.title: Seven dead, many injured in Mumbai landslip
World.content:
At least seven people died, and several others were injured after a landslip struck Mumbai’s Ghatkopar area in the early hours of Wednesday (August 12, 2026) following heavy rains. Rescue operations are underway to trace one person believed to be trapped under debris.

Mumbai’s civic body, Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), reported it as a Level-II incident — a serious incident requiring additional resources and coordination beyond the immediate ward — that occurred at 3:48 a.m. at Gaushiya Chawl in Chirag Nagar of Ghatkopar West. The soil and debris from the hillside collapsed onto two to three houses nearby, according to BMC Mayor Ritu Tawde, who visited the site to inspect operations.

Locals described being jolted awake by a loud noise from the collapse and running from their homes. One of the residents, Shaira Bhanu, was also affected by the landslip. A tree fell on her house, with her child getting trapped under the water tank installed on her house. “As the portion of the house collapsed, we quickly removed the water tank and then ran out of the house to safety. If they had worked a bit faster, more lives would have been saved,” she added.

“As we heard the noise, we did not think about anything; we just ran out of the house. A tree fell on top of a house in an adjacent lane to where the landslip hit. We were awake the entire night and couldn’t sleep because of the shock,” said Mohammed Aman, who lived near the site of the landslip.

Ms. Tawde on Wednesday (August 12) inspected the rescue operations, announcing ₹4 lakh for the next of kin of each deceased person and ₹50,000 assistance for each injured person. “The authorities had made every possible effort to rescue people trapped under the debris,” the mayor said.

Rescue operation

Police reached the spot at 4 a.m. and asked residents in the vicinity to move out, a resident of Gaushiya chawl who also helped authorities in rescue operations, informed The Hindu.

On the ground, two divisional fire officers (DFO), an assistant divisional fire officer (ADFO), two senior station officers (SrSO), four station officers, four fire engines, two fire tenders, two rescue vehicles, two mobile water tankers, and one water quick response vehicle have joined the rescue operation.

One person remained trapped under the debris, Deputy Chief Fire Brigade officer K.R. Yadav said, as the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), along with around 50 BMC personnel, continued rescue efforts.

“The site of the incident and the route leading to it are extremely narrow, allowing only one person to pass at a time. BMC officers, employees and workers, along with the Mumbai Fire Brigade, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), and Mumbai Police, are making every possible effort to rescue people trapped under the debris,” Ms. Tawde said.

Seven dead

All the deceased were taken to Rajawadi hospital, where Chief Medical Officer Vishal declared seven people were brought dead and three others were injured. The four injured people were taken to Kurla Bhabha Hospital.

The deceased are identified as Mohamad Samir Ansari (14), Sahil Husen Abdul Kazi (19), an unidentified person (45), Aban Arif Shaikh (2), Manat Arif Shaikh (4), Marjina Arif Shaikh (27) and Viket Ramesh Yadav (27).

The injured at Rajawadi Hospital are identified as Farana Dilber Khan (28), Dilber Amnulla Khan (38), and Shamin Muslim Khan (26).

Kurla Bhabha Hospital received four injured persons — Sohel Ansari (18), who sustained a head injury; Mohamad Ansari (14), Naimuddhin Eqbal Khan (28) and Sajid Ansari (16).

A family of four members, who died in the landslip, had just shifted to the chawl from Uttar Pradesh a few days ago, Mumbai Police said.

Notice sent

BMC had alerted residents and advised them not to stay in areas that are at risk of landslips or rockfalls and to evacuate from such locations. In particular, a notice was also issued as part of pre-monsoon precautionary measures. At Hill No. 3, Ashok Nagar, Kurla, the municipal administration had warned residents about the risks and conducted awareness campaigns in this regard.

“The BMC had already given notice, warning them to clear the area within 15 days. The owners of the house should be responsible for warning their tenants and heeding our warning. Our priority is to make the path clear for the rescue and relief work,” Sandhya Doshi, BMC corporator from Shiv Sena, said.

Guru Prasad Gupta, who stood for election in Ward 160 from Narayannagar, said: “I don’t know whether a notice was sent or not, but I have one request to the government. If people are living on a hill and there are chances of landslips, the government should take steps to move them out. Otherwise, this situation will repeat every year. The government should conduct a survey, find this out, and shift them out via the Slum Rehabilitation Authority, or put a blockade there to avoid such incidents in Mumbai again because they have lived there for the last 30-40 years.”

More houses on the verge of collapse

Some of the residents, including Sheikh Shahid, moved out of the house, grabbing important documents with them. “The houses are now tilted at an angle that they can fall at any moment. Even now, our doors are locked, and we can’t take anything out of the house. Five houses in this lane are broken down. They won’t cut down the tree now, or there will be more damage,” said Shahid.

Rashid Shah, who lives in the chawl, said: “I live in the first house in the chawl. If it keeps raining like this, I will have to also consider moving out before another landslip reaches my house.”

Sion slab collapse incident

In another incident during the day, a structure had collapsed in Mumbai’s Sion East area, where five persons were trapped but rescued after an hour-long operation.

The incident occurred at 4:48 p.m. at Mala Garden in Pratiksha Nagar of Sion, where a gazebo (seating arrangement structure) with a cement slab roof fell, injuring five persons. The injured were taken to Sion Hospital for treatment after they were rescued.

World.title: Babulal Marandi slams visit by police officers to Jharkhand protest site
World.content:
Leader of Opposition in Jharkhand Assembly Babulal Marandi on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) condemned the late night visit by two top officials at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where the agitation by job aspirants over alleged irregularities in the State recruitment examinations entered its 19th day

Ranchi’s Deputy Commissioner (DC) Manjunath Bhajantri and the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Rakesh Ranjan reached the protest site late at night, Mr. Marandi said.

Sharing a post on X he wrote: “This morning, as soon as I checked my mobile, I learned from the tweet posted by Amit Malviya ji, the party’s central social media coordinator, at 1:30 AM, and ANI’s social media post that late at night, Ranchi’s DC and SSP reached the protest site at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium and attempted to forcibly remove the students by cutting off the electricity.”

He strongly condemned the “undemocratic and reprehensible attitude” of the Ranchi district adminstration and the Hemant Soren-led governement.

“The officials stated that the government has cancelled the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) exam, so the protest should now be ended. As soon as the students received the information, BJP leaders arrived at the protest site late at night. Upon seeing the BJP leaders arriving there, the administrative officials left the spot,” he added.

The senior BJP leader, who also visited the site on Wednesday morning (August 12, 2026), asserted that the government can no longer tolerate even the peaceful struggle of students fighting for their rights and future. He added that the students’ demand is absolutely clear: there should be a fair CBI investigation into the selling of jobs and irregularities in the JPSC and JSSC exams.

“The students have already trusted the government’s assurances in the name of a CID investigation, and now they no longer have faith in that investigation. Simply cancelling the JPSC exam will not resolve the entire matter. The government should immediately order a CBI investigation and take concrete action on all the legitimate demands of the students,” Mr. Marandi said.

The former Chief Minister alleged that instead of suppressing the students’ voice by force of the police and administration, the government should resolve their demands.

“I warn the Hemant government not to make the mistake of challenging the power of the students. If an attempt is made to suppress this voice that has arisen in Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, its spark will reach every village in Jharkhand,” Mr. Marandi said.

He also demanded that the Ranchi district administration should ensure proper arrangements for electricity, water, sanitation, and other basic facilities at the protest site, rather than attempting to disrupt the peaceful movement at the government’s behest.

Ranchi DC, SSP on purpose of visit

On the purpose of the visit, DC Bhajantri said they had come to check on the protesters. “We have come here to ask whether the protesters are not facing any difficulties. Three students are on hunger strike over here, so we requested them to eat something so that their health does not deteriorate,” he said.

“We also have a request from the students to think about a practical and implementable next step, and accordingly we will cooperate,” the DC added.

Mr. Bhajantri was also found asking students whether they had appeared for the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission-Combined Graduate Level (JSSC-CGL) exam.

Ranchi SSP Mr. Ranjan appealed to the students not to allow any outsiders or anti-social elements to become part of their movement. He also urged the students to verify the identities and origins of all individuals at least once at night.

Reacting to the visit of the officials, student leader Kunal Singh said that it was humanly not possible to identify the outsiders and that it was the job of the special branch. He also alleged that during their visit, the officials tried to separate the JPSC and JSSC students.

World.title: 31-member parliamentary panel to review FCRA Bill
World.content:
The Lok Sabha on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) adopted a motion referring the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to a Joint Parliament Committee (JPC), amid a huge uproar by the Opposition which demanded that the Bill be withdrawn completely as it was intended to target minority institutions.

The motion to refer the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 to a 31-member JPC was added into the List of Business of the Lok Sabha through a supplementary list just before the House was supposed to reconvene at 2 p.m., after being adjourned within minutes at 11 a.m. Though Union Home Minister Amit Shah was listed to move the motion, it was Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai who actually placed it before the House.

Also read: Parliament monsoon session LIVE updates

The Opposition has been demanding that Mr. Shah should be present in the House and make a statement on last month’s police action against protesting students in Delhi.

JPC report by Winter Session

The FCRA JPC will have 21 members from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha. While the Lok Sabha MPs will be nominated by Speaker Om Birla, those from the Rajya Sabha will be nominated by Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan.

The committee has to submit its report to the Lok Sabha by the last day of the first week of the Winter Session of Parliament this year.

‘Targeting minorities’

Before the motion was adopted, senior Congress MP K.C. Venugopal said that the proposed legislation is clearly targeting NGOs, especially those run by minority communities, and demanded that the Bill be withdrawn.

“On the one hand, the RSS is collecting donations from foreign countries, and on the other the government is targeting NGOs. The government should withdraw the Bill,” he said.

Samajwadi Party MP Akhilesh Yadav also demanded the withdrawal of the Bill, saying the entire Opposition was against it. “[Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren] Rijiju-ji should clarify which Bill they brought till date that was not against minorities,” he said. The DMK’s T.R. Baalu also demanded that the Bill be withdrawn.

Amidst the Opposition uproar, Mr. Rijiju dared them to show a single clause in the Bill that was against minorities. “If Venugopal or any MPs have reservations about the Bill, they can raise it in the JPC. They will get enough time. This is not targeted at any minority community. I thought they would welcome sending it to a joint committee instead of opposing it,” he said. “I challenge Akhilesh ji to show one provision which is against minorities. Lies are being spread in the country. There should be rules,” the Union Minister added.

‘Country wants House to function’

The FCRA Amendment Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25, but was not taken up for passage during the Budget Session. The Bill proposes to create a designated authority to manage and dispose of assets if an organisation loses its FCRA licence, which the Opposition claimed could affect legitimate foreign funding for Christian NGOs and other minority-run social welfare and educational institutions.

After a brief adjournment following the adoption of the motion, was adopted, the Lok Sabha again re-assembled at 3 p.m. and passed the Mines and Minerals Bill without any discussion.

Earlier, in the morning, the Lok Sabha Speaker appealed to the Opposition to allow the House to function, stressing that it was not right for them to tarnish the image of the House by holding protests and shouting slogans. Mr. Birla told protesting MPs that even if their approach and thoughts differ from the ruling front, the country wants the House to function.

World.title: Troubling bill: On the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026
World.content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party-led government’s relentless zeal in over-regulating civil society organisations is on display again in the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which it had sought to push through Parliament. After strong protests, it has now been referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC). In 2020, the government got amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, or FCRA, passed that barred a registered body from passing funds to another, even one registered under the same Act, and cut the share of foreign funds that could be spent on administration from half to a fifth, among other restrictions. It now proposes to go further still by taking over the assets that the money built, even on the mere lapse of a certificate. Under the Bill, a donee organisation can lose its registration not only when the government cancels it, but when renewal is refused, not applied for, or not granted before the old certificate runs out. As soon as this happens, the organisation’s foreign funds and what was built with them will pass to a government-designated authority automatically. The property returns only if the organisation re-registers within a period the government has yet to specify, failing which it is lost for good. According to the Bill, a building put up only partly with foreign money will be taken over in full. The organisation must then apply to get back the share not paid for with foreign money. The Bill does allow for an appeal to a district judge, but only against what the authority does with the property later. The refusal to renew cannot be appealed against, and the organisation will not be entitled to be heard before the refusal is made. In essence, because the authority acts on the Centre’s instructions, the Centre can use opaque reasons to withdraw a licence, take over the property, and then direct the body now holding it.

It is not surprising that minority religious institutions have been the most alarmed. This is true of Christian organisations, which run thousands of schools, colleges and hospitals built and sustained with money from churches and congregations abroad. Hundreds marched in Aizawl, Mizoram, under a newly formed council of churches; organisations in Kerala have objected to the Bill; Nagaland’s Chief Minister wrote to the Home Minister seeking a parliamentary review; and the Tamil Nadu Assembly has also unanimously resolved that the Centre should withdraw the Bill. The Home Minister has assured church leaders that the Bill will not apply retrospectively, but the text of his own Bill says otherwise. A hospital built decades ago can still be taken over today because a certificate has been allowed to lapse. The JPC, to which the Bill has been sent, should redraft it to provide organisations with an opportunity to be heard before renewal is refused, as well as a right to appeal against such a refusal, among other changes that would make the regulation fair and transparent.

World.title: Singappen Special Force helps 11-year-old boy from Coimbatore continue schooling
World.content:
The Singappen Special Force (SSF) attached to the Coimbatore District (Rural) Police helped a Class 6 student continue his schooling after his mother was unable to support his studies.

The force extended a helping hand to the boy who was left helpless and unable to continue his school education due to family circumstances.

According to the police, the boy from Kuniyamuthur area of Coimbatore was living with his parents and studying in Class 6 at a government school. The boy’s father forced his wife and son out of the house, allegedly due to a family dispute. The mother faced hardship as she could not take proper care his son and send him to school while she went out to work.

The mother approached SSF, seeking help for her son’s education and safety. Upon receiving her request, the SSF team inquired about the boy’s situation. The team helped the woman enrol her son in a residential school at Valparai. The mother expressed her gratitude to the force.

In July, the SSF team enrolled two children in the tribal residential school at Valparai on July 20 after their mother struggled to support their studies following the death of her husband. The force also arranged clothes and study materials for the siblings.

World.title: 'We aspire for it to grow': Turkiye's Erdogan eyes expansion of Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
World.content:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Wednesday that he hoped more countries would join a defence agreement signed last week between Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, aimed at stabilising a region wracked by conflict.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed on Friday as the Middle East grapples with fallout from the US-Iran war, which has dragged in regional players and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

“Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries,” the Turkish leader told the London-based Asharq Al-Awsat daily. “Rather we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella.”

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way.

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thursday and Friday.

Cairo has robust military cooperation with Ankara, but has given no indication it intends to sign up to the new security alliance, which contains a Nato-style clause saying any attack on one would be seen as an attack on all.

The five-month US-Iran war has upended the security architecture in the region and forced a rethink of decades of conventional wisdom rooted in US military supremacy.

Erdogan said the pact emerged out of the “new circumstances” in the Middle East with regional players seeking to assume greater responsibility for their own security and stability.

“Regional issues should be resolved by regional actors, and with this action, we consider that we have taken a first step toward achieving that goal,” he told the Saudi-owned newspaper.

“Resolving regional issues must be carried out away from formulas imposed from the outside. We know very well that solutions imported from abroad only bring disasters.”

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has been hailed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as an “important strategic step”.

Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

On Monday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif affirmed that the defence pact was “entirely for defensive purposes”, and not for any aggression.

Addressing the federal cabinet on Monday, PM Shehbaz stressed that the objective of the pact is to “promote peace, progress, and prosperity in the region”.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza.

Israel ‘removing Palestine’ from world agenda

Erdogan also accused the Israeli government of Benjamin Netanyahu of seeking to “remove Palestine” from the world’s agenda.

“The aim of the Netanyahu government is to remove Palestine from the common agenda of humanity by profiting from chaos and new conflicts in the region,” Erdogan said at a joint news conference with his Palestinian counterpart, Mahmoud Abbas.

“No matter what they do, they will not succeed. The Palestinian cause will continue to grow in people’s hearts as they try to destroy it,” he stressed, vowing Turkiye would fight for the establishment of a Palestinian state.

A strong advocate of the Palestinian cause, Erdogan has repeatedly lambasted Netanyahu’s government, accusing the Israeli prime minister of committing “genocide” in Gaza and of pursuing expansionist policies in the West Bank, Lebanon, Syria and beyond.

Abbas arrived in Ankara on Tuesday accompanied by his diplomatic adviser Majdi Khalidi, intelligence chief Majed Faraj and senior Palestinian official Ziad Abu Amr.

He met Erdogan on Wednesday with the pair discussing developments in the region in talks the Palestinian leader described as “important and fruitful”.

“I hope the decision to hold legislative and presidential elections in Palestine after a long time will bring good fortune … [and] will advance the reconciliation process,” Erdogan said, in a nod to the historic rivalry between Abbas’ Fatah movement and Gaza’s Hamas rulers.

Abbas also hailed the defence pact between Ankara, Riyadh and Islamabad, saying it was “of utmost importance” and expressing hope it would help enhance security and stability in the region.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Re0.94, raises high-speed diesel by Re0.54
World.content:
The government on Wednesday reduced the price of petrol by Re0.94 and increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.54 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs324.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs382.79 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for August 13 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: After death of 3 Pakistani sailors, FO says Islamabad will implement maritime coalition 'in full earnest'
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday that Pakistan, as a signatory to the recently announced multinational maritime defence coalition, would implement its commitments “in full earnest”.

The statement comes following the deaths of three Pakistani sailors in Houthi strikes on a Saudi cargo ship on Tuesday.

Last month, Riyadh unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea region. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, Turkiye and Egypt, backed the coalition in a joint statement.

Answering questions at a weekly press briefing, FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi elaborated that Pakistan was a signatory of the recent joint statement supporting a multinational maritime defence coalition, led by Saudi Arabia, to protect shipping and energy supply routes.

“Pakistan is a signatory to this maritime coalition communique and we will implement it with full earnest,” Andrabi said, adding that the country was engaged with the Saudi authorities in this regard.

Andrabi further said that on the directions of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Pakistan was ascertaining the details of the agreement.
