World.title: Irakli Kobakhidze: “‘Deep state’ is trying to artificially fuel Russophobia in Georgia”
World.content:
“Radical anti-Russian sentiment in the country is being artificially fuelled and is part of a new campaign against Georgia,” Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze said at a briefing. He said attempts to intensify Russophobia in Georgia were part of a plan carried out by agents of the “deep state”.

Kobakhidze recalled that the Georgian government had repeatedly said that, after Russia launched its full-scale war against Ukraine in 2022, the so-called “global war party” had tried to draw Georgia into the conflict and open a “second front” in the country.

The prime minister said this “window of opportunity” created an “existential threat” to Georgia and its population. He said calls for Georgia to join international sanctions against Russia soon followed. According to the government, complying with those demands would have had serious consequences for the country’s economy.

“Because the Georgian government refused to comply with these demands, pursued a sovereign policy and acted in the interests of the state, our country became a target for the European bureaucracy and Western leaders working in tandem with informal oligarchic forces,” Kobakhidze said.

He also addressed the sanctions imposed by Western countries on the Georgian government. According to Kobakhidze, pressure mechanisms, including sanctions, were already being used when the previous US administration under Joe Biden was in power.

Kobakhidze said the sanctions had targeted senior Georgian government officials, ruling party honorary chairman Bidzina Ivanishvili, judges, senior police officers and others.

He said the West had also used Georgia’s EU membership prospects as a tool to pressure the government.

“They failed to break the ruling party, which enjoys the support of the Georgian people, so now they are trying to use their agents to drag Georgia into a new provocation,” he added.

Kobakhidze said a “new stage of the attack” on Georgia, its people and its sovereignty had begun:

“This is a qualitatively new stage of the attack on Georgia, the Georgian people and the country’s sovereignty, unfolding simultaneously on several fronts.”

Background

Several days before the anniversary of the August 2008 war, Irakli Kobakhidze published a lengthy letter addressing the issue of “Russophobia”.

In the letter, Kobakhidze discussed the links between Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Georgia’s domestic political situation and the opposition’s position. He said the “global war party” benefited from the ongoing conflict in Ukraine because it wanted to “fuel Russophobia at the highest level among its agents around the world, including in Georgia”.

Kobakhidze accused the opposition and civil society of changing their attitude towards Russia. He described their current tough stance towards Moscow as “Russophobia”.

The letter reignited political disputes over the events of the 2008 war. This time, however, the debate focused not only on the circumstances that led to the war and Russia’s responsibility. The prime minister shifted the focus from Russia’s actions to the position of his Georgian opponents.

Georgian PM on “Russophobia”

World.title: Ilham Aliyev’s AzTV interview during Nakhchivan visit: industrial park, energy projects and Zangezur Corridor
World.content:
Ilham Aliyev’s visit to Nakhchivan

On 11 August, Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev and First Vice-President Mehriban Aliyeva visited the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic. It was Aliyev’s 17th visit to Nakhchivan since he became president.

During the visit, officials held foundation-laying ceremonies and opened several facilities. Aliyev also visited historical sites and presented battle flags to military units.

The visit ended with an interview with Azerbaijan Television (AzTV), in which Aliyev outlined his plans for Nakhchivan’s development.

The interview focused on the autonomous republic’s economic and social development, energy security and transport infrastructure. Aliyev also discussed Nakhchivan’s place in Azerbaijan’s broader strategy, particularly its future development in conjunction with Karabakh and Eastern Zangezur, territories that came under Baku’s control after the Second Karabakh War.

Key events during the visit

During the visit to Nakhchivan, President Ilham Aliyev and First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva inspected work at the Shams-1 and Garbi Ufug solar power plants, which have a combined capacity of 50 MW.

One of the key events was the laying of the foundation stone for the Nakhchivan Industrial Park. It will be Azerbaijan’s second-largest industrial park by area, after the Sumgayit Industrial Park. A 300 MW thermal power plant is also planned for the site.

Nakhchivan’s total generating capacity currently stands at around 200 MW. Once the new plant comes online, this will increase by roughly half.

The visit programme also included:

the opening of the Nakhchivan Regional DOST Centre;

the presentation of new electric buses and an inspection of railway infrastructure reconstruction works;

the laying of the foundation stone for the Nakhchivan hotel complex, which is expected to be completed by around 2028;

the laying of the foundation stone for a social housing complex;

an inspection of restoration work at the Momine Khatun Mausoleum and the unveiling of a monument to architect Ajami Nakhchivani;

the presentation of Nakhchivan’s General Development Plan through 2044, which envisages expanding the city and increasing its population;

the presentation of battle flags to new commando units of the Separate Combined Arms Army.

Key points from the AzTV interview

Aliyev described his visit to Nakhchivan as a “sign of the autonomous republic’s comprehensive development”. He said every visit should produce concrete results. He highlighted strengthening defence capabilities, energy security, job creation, preserving historical and cultural heritage, and developing transport links as key priorities.

Defence and governance

Aliyev said Nakhchivan’s geographical position – particularly its lack of a direct land connection with mainland Azerbaijan – requires special attention to the region’s defence. He highlighted the creation of the Separate Combined Arms Army and new commando units as key steps.

According to the president, “Azerbaijan’s Armed Forces carry weight in the region”. He also said Nakhchivan had introduced a system of special presidential representatives, similar to the model used in Karabakh and Eastern Zangezur. Aliyev said the benefits of this system of governance were already becoming apparent.

Energy

Nakhchivan has been fully supplied with gas for around 15 years, Aliyev said, thanks to a gas swap agreement with Iran.

The president also placed particular emphasis on the region’s solar energy potential. He said Nakhchivan was Azerbaijan’s most favourable region for solar power generation. More than 600 hectares of land have already been allocated for the development of this sector. The potential is estimated at at least 500 MW and could reach 1 GW in the future.

Aliyev also highlighted the growing role of the private sector. Projects to build solar power plants with a combined capacity of 50 MW are already under way.

The president described electricity exports as a strategic priority. Iran and Turkey are currently the main destinations, but Azerbaijan ultimately hopes to export electricity from Nakhchivan to the European market as well.

Zangezur Corridor – TRIPP

Aliyev said that “the creation of the Zangezur Corridor was our initiative”, recalling that connecting mainland Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan, an integral part of the country, had remained one of Baku’s strategic goals for many years.

He said he had insisted that a provision on the corridor be included in the trilateral statement signed by Azerbaijan, Russia and Armenia on 10 November 2020. Aliyev claims the Armenian side did not want to agree to this, but had no other alternative because continuing the war was not in its interests.

Noting that there had been no practical progress on the issue for five years, Aliyev said a solution emerged after the Washington summit on 8 August 2025, when the TRIPP project (Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity) was launched.

Speaking about the current state of the work, the president said the Horadiz-Aghband highway was almost complete, with only minor technical issues remaining. He said construction of the railway was also progressing rapidly.

Aliyev added that a project for power transmission lines linking mainland Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan through Armenia had already been prepared, and locations for the pylons had been identified.

Aliyev predicted that these projects would eventually turn Nakhchivan into one of the region’s key transport and energy hubs.

A unified development concept

The president stressed that Nakhchivan, Eastern Zangezur and Karabakh should develop under a unified concept. He said the geographical proximity of the three regions requires a common approach to their development.

Aliyev noted that master plans for cities in the territories that came under Azerbaijan’s control after the Second Karabakh War had already been approved. He also said he had ordered the preparation of a similar document for Nakhchivan. The “Nakhchivan City Development Master Plan through 2044” was presented to the president during the current visit.

Speaking about the region’s tourism potential, Aliyev said Nakhchivan had significant opportunities thanks to its rich historical heritage, scenic landscapes and clean air. At the same time, he acknowledged that the hotel infrastructure remained underdeveloped and that the existing hotels were generally of a low standard, hindering the growth of tourism.

He said that to address the problem, construction had begun on a new five-star hotel complex in the city centre. The project is expected to be completed around 2028.

Ilham Aliyev’s visit to Nakhchivan

World.content:
New road safety rules in Georgia

Georgia plans to tighten road safety rules under the National Road Safety Strategy for 2026–2030, approved by the government on 5 August 2026. The strategy includes changes in several areas.

At this stage, the measures remain proposals, and some will require further legislative amendments before they can take effect.

What is changing:

Child seats will become mandatory for pre-school children. This means that when transporting a child of the relevant age, it will no longer be enough simply to seat them in the car or secure them with a standard seat belt.

Georgia plans to establish a standard for alcohol-based ignition interlock systems. Under the strategy, authorities intend to take alcohol interlock technology into account when setting requirements for vehicles entering the Georgian market. The government strategy says seat-belt use is one of the key ways to reduce deaths and serious injuries in road accidents. It pays particular attention to rear-seat seat belts because unrestrained passengers in the back can endanger not only themselves but also people sitting in the front of the vehicle.

World.title: Lasha Bugadze becomes first modern Georgian writer whose book was barred from being sent to prison
World.content:
Precedent for literary censorship in Georgia

The administration of Rustavi Prison refused to allow Lasha Bugadze’s new novel, The Observer, to be delivered to the prison. The book was intended for Nana Sander, who was convicted over her participation in a protest on 4 October 2025.

Notably, the penitentiary code contains no provision explicitly banning fiction from being brought into prisons.

The book’s synopsis describes a fictional political reality involving the long rule of a “despot”, the “division of the country into zones” and a “cult of the leader”. It also mentions the scheduling of elections and a decision by the country’s population on whether they should take place.

According to Bugadze, a prison official refused to allow the book in, saying the novel contained “political content”.

The writer says it is unclear to him who determined that the book contained political content and what criteria they used. He suspects the decision may have been prompted by words and phrases in the novel, such as “despot” and “cult of the leader”.

“The employee told me directly that the book could not be delivered because it was political in nature. I don’t think he sat down and read the book. I doubt he even read the synopsis,” Bugadze said.

In his view, someone appears to have judged the work to be political without giving any clear reason.

“Who put this label on the text? [Who decided] whether it was political or not? What does that even mean? And, excuse me, even if the content is political, why should a citizen – whether a prisoner or anyone else – not have the right to read such a book?” the writer said.

Bugadze sees the incident as a potential precedent for censoring literary works:

“It can be described as the first significant example of literary censorship in modern Georgian history. This is an extremely dangerous precedent, and under no circumstances should it be considered normal. The situation requires a response. No one has the right to stop someone from reading.”

The head of the human rights organisation Sapari, Baia Pataraia, announced that legal proceedings would begin over the incident:

“We are taking legal steps. <…> First, we will demand a written and reasoned refusal.”

The organisation PEN Georgia also responded to the case. It described the incident as an alarming precedent for censorship of a literary work, linked not only to the novel’s content but also to the author’s political and civic stance. The organisation stressed that censoring fiction and restricting freedom of expression are unacceptable in a democratic society.

Lasha Bugadze’s The Observer

Precedent for literary censorship in Georgia

World.title: Armenia seeks alternatives amid concerns over possible Russian gas price hike
World.content:
Russian gas pressure on Armenia

If the issue of raising gas tariffs arises, the Armenian authorities will discuss it with their Russian counterparts in a friendly atmosphere, Sargis Khandanyan, an MP from the ruling Civil Contract faction, told journalists.

Khandanyan added that he had no information about any negotiations with Russia over gas tariffs. However, he expressed confidence that, if necessary, Armenia would be able to find alternatives to Russian gas. These could include supplies from Iran, although this is not the only option.

Yerevan and Tehran have already discussed the issue. Following talks held with Iranian partners by Armenia’s Minister of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure, Davit Khudatyan, it emerged that the volume of Iranian gas supplies could potentially be doubled.

“This decision has nothing to do with any other country, Russia in particular. It is a profitable economic activity that both countries are interested in expanding,” the Armenian minister said.

Political analyst Robert Ghevondyan notes that there has recently been increasingly frequent talk of a possible revision of Russian gas prices. He views the issue in the context of the levers of pressure being used against Armenia. In his view, Moscow has already exhausted much of its arsenal and is now resorting to economic leverage, including in the energy sector.

“Political, cultural and terrorist levers, as well as the influence of the criminal subculture, are no longer working for various reasons. And Russia, in order to prevent Armenia from strengthening its independence, has decided to make full use of its last remaining lever,” Ghevondyan said.

‘This scenario cannot be ruled out’: On gas imports from Azerbaijan

Journalists asked MP Sargis Khandanyan how likely it was that the tariff on gas imports from Russia could change by the end of the year.

“I am not aware of when this issue was last discussed with Russia. Nor am I aware of any information that would give grounds to believe that the gas tariff could change,” he replied.

At the same time, the MP noted that the government attaches great importance to diversifying supplies. He recalled the agreements reached during the visit of Armenia’s Minister of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure to Iran. According to him, the “Trump Route” could also be considered as one such opportunity:

“As part of the transit route that will connect Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan through Armenian territory, a gas pipeline will be built. This could provide another opportunity. We could consider this pipeline as an additional source. Of course, this is a very theoretical idea, but it would not be difficult to implement.”

Asked about the possibility of importing gas from Azerbaijan, Khandanyan said that Yerevan and Baku were discussing a broad range of issues:

“I do not know how far we have progressed on the issue of gas supplies, but this scenario cannot be ruled out.”

In late October 2025, Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev announced that all restrictions on transit to Armenia would be lifted. Since then, Armenia has been receiving petroleum products from the neighbouring country by rail. According to official figures, Azerbaijan has already supplied Armenia with 20,000 tonnes of petroleum products.

Yerevan and Tehran agree to increase gas supplies. Can Moscow stand in the way?

Minister of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure Davit Khudatyan paid a three-day visit to Iran. Upon returning from Tehran, he said that the volume of Iranian gas supplied under the “Gas for Electricity” programme could be at least doubled. He explained that the pipeline’s capacity exceeds the volume of gas currently being supplied.

Under the programme, Armenia has been receiving gas from Iran since 2009, converting it into electricity which is then supplied back to Iran.

To increase gas imports and export a corresponding volume of electricity to Iran, construction of the Iran-Armenia high-voltage power transmission line needs to be completed. The Armenian government hopes that the long-delayed project will be completed by the end of the year.

Meanwhile, since 2015, the Armenian section of the pipeline carrying gas from Iran has been controlled by Russian company Gazprom.

As a result, some experts doubt whether Iranian gas supplies can be increased without Moscow’s consent. The Armenian government, however, has assured that there will be no obstacles to expanding supplies under the “Gas for Electricity” programme.

Expert commentaty

Political commentator Artem Yerkanyan says:

“Russian Security Council Deputy Secretary Alexei Shevtsov threatened that unless Armenia revises its foreign policy course, it will have to pay $800 for Russian gas instead of the current $177. Compensating for that difference would cost at least $1bn. That is more than the €50m the European Union has promised Armenia as compensation for the impact of strained relations with Russia.

It is worth explaining what the figures of $177 and $800 actually mean. Russia’s Gazprom sells gas for $177 to Gazprom Armenia, which is owned by Gazprom itself. In other words, it also earns revenue from the distribution of the gas, and that revenue also goes to Gazprom. Therefore, I think it would be incorrect to say that Armenia buys gas for $177.

It is also unclear where the figure of $800 comes from, considering the following:

China buys Russian gas for $258;

Turkey for $280;

Hungary, Serbia and Slovakia for $400;

Spain, France and Belgium for $450.

Moreover, according to a forecast by Russia’s Ministry of Economic Development, by the end of this year the average price at which Russia will sell gas to countries outside the EAEU [an economic bloc led by Russia] will be $290.

If the average price is $290, why are they planning to sell it to Armenia for $800? That is unclear.”

Political analyst Robert Ghevondyan argues:

“Following the elections, the Armenian authorities have continued to pursue a multi-vector foreign policy. Dependence on Russia is steadily declining, with the economic dimension playing an increasingly important role in this process.

While Russia is trying to exert economic pressure, Armenia is opening up new markets that Armenian businesses previously ‘failed to notice’ because of their excessive focus on the Russian market. Although problems remain with some goods, economic diversification is advancing rapidly.

In the energy sector, Armenia has alternatives when it comes to building a new nuclear reactor, which in itself is a headache for Russia.

It is no coincidence that, alongside economic blackmail, Rosatom executives periodically make Armenia ‘attractive’ offers to build a new Russian nuclear reactor. However, the Armenian authorities are likely to opt for a different proposal.

A rise in gas prices could initially cause problems. But Armenia has alternatives here as well: Iranian, Turkmen and now Azerbaijani gas.

Consequently, in the near future, Russian gas may find itself merely competing on the market. This would limit the Kremlin’s ability to use gas prices to blackmail Armenia.

In conclusion, it should be noted that increased pressure from Russia is having the opposite effect. Armenia is steadily ‘freeing itself’ from excessive Russian influence and diversifying its economy. The Kremlin does not appear to recognise this yet, but that is its problem.”

World.title: Kobakhidze: Georgia does not publicly declare Russia an enemy because this would require follow-up steps
World.content:
Georgian prime minister on Russia

Georgian Dream Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze told journalists that the Georgian government does not publicly call Russia an “enemy” because such a political statement would require corresponding action.

A journalist asked Kobakhidze whether the Georgian government considers Russia an enemy. The prime minister replied:

“Your questions are shameful, you look ridiculous. Let me explain in simple terms why this question is shameful: you want to get a sensational headline, even in the Russian media, saying that I have declared the Russian Federation an enemy. This is a specific political statement that would have to be followed by specific steps – roughly the same, or exactly the same, as those your party” (referring to the United National Movement – JAMnews) “took in 2008 and before.”

The journalist asked whether this was precisely why the government was reluctant to openly call Russia an enemy.

“Of course. What, should I repeat it again?!” Kobakhidze replied.

Kobakhidze also addressed Russia’s occupation of Georgian territories and reiterated that the Russian Federation occupies 20% of Georgia’s territory.

“Of course, the Russian Federation is the only state and party that has occupied Georgian territories. This is an absolutely clear fact. Numerous statements have been made about this, and there is no doubt about it,” Kobakhidze stressed.

He said Russia’s occupation of Georgian territory was a “crime against the Georgian state and the Georgian people”:

“This is an egregious crime: first the occupation, and then the so-called recognition.”

Georgian prime minister on Russia

World.title: Remote school bus axed leaving students and families stranded
World.content:
Hailed as a remote success story, Queensland's longest school bus service has been axed, leaving six primary students stranded from their school.

For the last six years up to 18 students in the remote towns of Bidunggu and Gregory, about 300 kilometres north of Mount Isa, have made the three-hour daily return trip to Burketown State School to learn alongside peers in the classroom.

But during the last school holidays, Bidunggu resident and parent Natalie King said families were told the bus service would not resume in term three, leaving boarding school or School of the Air as the only educational options.

The next nearest primary school from Gregory is 165km away at Doomadgee, but there is no school bus.

"This bus gave them a chance to be with teachers in person … for students to have that kind of normal school experience," Ms King said.

"These kids need an education."

The wheels are coming off

The bus service was established in 2021 after Burketown State School approached the community to create a regular bus service and boost enrolments, which, according to the Department of Education, currently sit around 27 students.

Ms King said the 240km round trip each day was not ideal but resulted in far better outcomes than remote schooling.

"I sent my young fellow away to boarding school in Cairns after he graduated from Burketown. The teachers down there couldn't believe how well educated he was," she said.

"That's the sort of education we were getting."

The lengthy bus ride is 120km long, or roughly 90 minutes. (ABC North West Qld: Emily Dobson)

The service was funded by the Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) and was operated by Burketown State School until last term.

Burketown State School declined to comment.

A Queensland Department of Education spokesperson said the state school had worked hard to try and find a replacement operator.

"The Department of Education is working closely with the principal to identify any eligible drivers within the school community; however, the very limited availability of suitably qualified drivers and staff absences have impacted the continuity of the bus service," the spokesperson said.

"The Mount Isa School of the Air is liaising with the three families and six students to engage in further education.

"We will continue to liaise with TMR, who are investigating if there are any options for the bus to be run by the council or other community-based groups."

A TMR spokesperson confirmed funding was available for the service, but no replacement had been found so far.

Calls for a school

Monique Mckerrell's family fell in love with the area on a cross-country road trip. (Supplied: Monique Mckerrell)

Gregory resident Monique Mckerrell moved to the region with her two children after being amazed by the area's natural beauty.

"We were planning on travelling Australia … we found Gregory and fell in love," she said.

"The spring that runs all year round to swim in, fish in, there's lots of hunting that we enjoy doing too, it was just prime."

Monique Mckerrell fears that as her children get older they will miss out on the same schooling and social experience other kids receive. (Supplied: Monique Mckerrell)

But the bus service's closure has raised questions about what future is possible in a town without access to face-to-face schooling.

"Going to school is an important life experience, learning how to be part of the world, communicating, listening, thinking, and trying new things, and then gaining that confidence away from home," she said.

"If you had a school [in Gregory], it would bring more people in the community … in the long run I would prefer a physical school in town."

Gregory previously had a primary school — a campus of Doomadgee State School — between 2003 and 2012, which closed after enrolments dwindled to four students.

But the community has grown.

According to the most recent census data, Gregory has a population of 122 people, about 60 per cent more than the 2016 census.

Meanwhile, Burketown, where the region's only school remains, recorded a population of 204 people in 2021, down 34 residents from 2016

Ms King agreed a school at Gregory was needed as raising children without access to face-to-face learning was "too hard".

"It's just so sad because a lot of families, they want to come home, they want to come back … but now that we've got no school it's too hard."

A Department of Education spokesperson said little evidence supported the construction of a new school in the Gregory area.

Natalie King said the school bus service gave students a chance to play, socialise and learn face-to-face. (ABC North West Qld: Emily Dobson)

"When planning for new schools, the department considers a broad range of factors to establish a service need to provide a new school," the spokesperson said.

"For most new schools in Queensland, the service need is underpinned by an analysis of the local school network and its ability to meet projected population growth."

World.title: P-plater who ploughed car into herd of cattle recounts 'terrifying' ordeal
World.content:
A P-plate driver who ploughed through a herd of cows at 110 kilometres an hour on a country highway in the dark, killing several, has described his "terrifying" experience.

WARNING: This story contains descriptions and photographs of dying animals that may be distressing.

Police say Hervic Declarador, 19, was lucky to escape with his life after the "intense and harrowing" incident.

The accident happened about 10pm on Sunday as Mr Declarador was driving his brand-new ute on South Coast Highway near Marbelup, about 420km south of Perth.

He had bought the car just two weeks earlier.

Mr Declarador said he had little time to brake before hitting the herd. (Supplied: Hervic Declarador)

"I was just driving normally and then everything exploded in my face ... I had ringing in my ears, and everything went black, and there were airbags all over me," he said.

" It was terrifying, it just happened too fast. "

Hidden danger

The accident happened on an unlit stretch of the highway connecting the city of Albany to the tourist town of Denmark on WA's south coast.

Mr Declarador said he had been blinded by the lights of a car parked on the side of the road as he rounded a corner.

The car's driver had apparently been trying to alert other motorists to the cows, but Mr Declarador said the high beam had instead obscured the danger ahead.

Several cows were killed or injured in the crash. (Supplied: Hervic Declarador)

"I was thinking 'oh, what a dickhead' and as I got closer, I tried to flash them to try and turn them off, but when I flashed my own high beams, that's when I saw the cows," he said.

" I was only 15 metres away from the cows, give or take, and I didn't have time to brake ... I just smashed right into them. "

Car 'unrecognisable'

The 19-year-old said he initially thought the damage was relatively minor because of the car's safety features, but that relief was short-lived.

"I didn't really feel the impact because the airbags just caught me so well that I thought it was just going to be a big dent," he said.

The brand new car was unrecognisable after the crash. (Supplied: Hervic Declarador)

But once outside, he saw the full extent of the carnage.

"There was a cow on the ground, still alive, couldn't move, looking at me with tears in its eyes," he said.

"And then I saw my car … the whole bonnet was caved in, dented in and just unrecognisable."

Fallen tree freed cows

Great Southern Police Superintendent John Munday said about 50 cows had wandered onto the road after a tree felled by strong winds landed on a fence.

Officers who attended found four dead cows on the road and euthanised a further three injured cows at the scene.

Mr Declarador had purchased the vehicle two weeks earlier. (Supplied: Hervic Declarador)

He said police had not spoken to the driver who tried to warn Mr Declarador of the cows, but believed they were acting in the interests of other drivers.

"I think they were probably trying to do the best thing they could at the time, but equally, I can put myself in the shoes of that driver to be really unsure as to what's going on," he said.

Mr Declarador said he had been blinded by the high beams of a parked vehicle. (Supplied: Hervic Declarador)

He described the incident as "intense and harrowing", with Mr Declarador lucky to walk away without serious injury,

"These incidents, they're extremely dangerous, and there have been multiple occurrences where there are fatalities and serious injuries where cars have hit any sort of livestock, native animal on the road," he said.

" It's just fortunate nobody was hurt, and the car stayed on its wheels. "

Superintendent Munday said no charges had been laid, and responsibility for the investigation had been handed to the City of Albany.

There have been several recent reports of livestock wandering onto public roads across the Great Southern, with some residents saying it was only a matter of time until they caused a serious incident.

A livestock warning remains in place for the stretch of highway where the accident happened, with motorists advised to exercise extreme caution.

World.title: Aussie man charged with fraud, child indecency in US
World.content:
A convicted fraudster notorious for his dating app antics in regional New South Wales has been hit with fresh charges on the other side of the world.

Brett Joseph, 39, made claims of immense wealth to a woman he met on dating apps, when in reality he had a humble upbringing in Mudgee, in the state's Central West.

He was eventually convicted of several counts of fraud in Mudgee Local Court in 2016, before moving to Texas in the United States — where he is again alleged to have fallen on the wrong side of the law.

Do you know more about this or have a similar story? Email turner-cohen.alex@abc.net.au

Brett Joseph made the rounds on dating apps across regional NSW. (Supplied: Daisy Armstrong)

Texas police charged Mr Joseph with the fraudulent use or possession of identifying information last Wednesday.

He has not yet been indicted, the Wharton District Court confirmed.

Arresting officers from the Throckmorton Sheriff's Department told the ABC they served Mr Joseph with papers relating to a civil case, but after running his drivers licence discovered there was an outstanding arrest warrant for fraud.

A mugshot taken in October last year, when Joseph was charged with child indecency. (Supplied: Throckmorton County Sheriff's Office)

"We confirmed the warrant and placed him under arrest and transported [him] to the Stephens County Jail," Sheriff Glen Whitfield said.

A booking sheet and accompanying mugshot shows Mr Joseph spent two days behind bars before posting a $US10,000 ($14,200) bond.

Decade-old fraud conviction

The ABC can reveal this is not Mr Joseph's first brush with the law in Texas.

In October last year, he was charged with indecency with a child by exposure, and spent a night in a Texas jail cell with a $US25,000 ($35,400) bond.

"I have not been indicted on either charge," Mr Joseph told the ABC.

"Anyone can be arrested on anything, doesn't mean they're guilty."

He said the charges were the result of an "ugly" break-up with a former romantic partner, and that "people get charged every day".

Brett Joseph told the ABC he was innocent and denied ever being convicted of fraud. (Supplied: Daisy Armstrong)

Brett Joseph has used multiple aliases. (Supplied: Daisy Armstrong)

Mr Joseph also denied he was a convicted fraudster here in Australia.

He was charged with eight offences relating to theft at the Griffith Local Court nearly a decade ago, but these were dismissed.

Four charges of receiving or disposing of stolen property were dismissed in 2017, while four charges of disposing of property were dismissed the following year.

But Mudgee Local Court records show Mr Joseph has been tried and convicted on three occasions for fraud-related crimes.

In 2016, he pleaded guilty to three counts of dishonestly obtaining property by deception.

He was fined $1,500 and also sentenced to 12 months' imprisonment, though this was suspended and he was put on a good behaviour bond.

Brett Joseph and Daisy Armstrong at the races 10 years ago while they briefly dated. (Supplied: Daisy Armstrong)

Brett Joseph and Daisy Armstrong briefly dated in 2016. (Supplied: Daisy Armstrong)

Mr Joseph said the public scrutiny he has been receiving for the past decade is the result of his "crazy b****" ex-girlfriend Daisy Armstrong, who has been running a public awareness campaign against him.

Speaking to the ABC, Ms Armstrong, also 39, said she has indeed unashamedly continued to publish information on Mr Joseph's whereabouts in a bid to warn others.

"Nothing has changed," she said in relation to the new charge.

"It's been 10 years since I first started blowing the whistle on him, and if he had learnt from his mistakes and become a better person, then of course we wouldn't still be on this train.

"I wish I could say that he might have learned his lesson, turned over a new leaf.

"At least people have a fighting chance to know who they're dealing with, which I didn't have," she added.

Daisy Armstrong, now, says she has moved on with her life but is happy to keep her website on Brett Joseph updated in a bid to warn others. (Supplied: Daisy Armstrong)

Ms Armstrong, from Griffith in NSW, dated Mr Joseph for six months in 2016 after meeting him on Tinder, but soon grew suspicious of some of his claims.

He had been living for free on her family's property, and she discovered a new dating profile where he had been misrepresenting himself as a wealthy farmer to attract other women while they were still together.

After starting a public website about Mr Joseph, she learned he went by multiple aliases, she said, including Brett Goodman, Hunter Ballieu, Brett Jones, Brett Inglis, Brett James and Brett Jay.

Brett Joseph has previously been previously convicted of fraud. (Supplied: Daisy Armstrong)

Another woman the ABC spoke to, Alanna O'Donnell, from Wollondilly Shire in NSW, said precious jewellery went missing after she lived with and dated Mr Joseph for several weeks back in 2009.

She was able to recover her antique ring years later, when she found the website about Mr Joseph and was shocked to discover Ms Armstrong had been gifted her ring.

This led to the theft charges against Mr Joseph in Griffith Court in 2017, but they were ultimately dismissed.

"I feel very let down by the Australian court system, that's for sure," Ms O'Donnell said.

"I feel very frustrated that the alarms were raised so early in Australia, but it's taken America to come in and hopefully put him away and stop that behaviour," she said of the new charges.

"I think it's just disgraceful that he's still going."

Ms O'Donnell recalled her six-week romance with him as a "whirlwind".

"It's like he consumes you in his personality," she said.

"[He] takes you on this whirlwind adventure, and you just don't even know you're in this cyclone until you start getting glimpses of things that don't necessarily add up.

"It's very trance-like. It feels so surreal: 'Somebody [who] finally loves me for who I am.'"

Brett Joseph has misrepresented himself in regional NSW. (Supplied: Daisy Armstrong)

Brett Joseph at an event in NSW several years ago. (Supplied: Daisy Armstrong)

Fraud detectives warning

Michael Gerondis, a retired fraud squad detective inspector and family friend of the Armstrongs, said he had been keeping tabs on Mr Joseph for years.

"He was saying that he was an agronomist," Mr Gerondis recalled, describing when he first met the fraudster.

"He couldn't even spell agronomist, but he came up with all these stories."

Mr Gerondis said like many fraudsters, Mr Joseph got away with some of his lies because they had "an element of truth to them".

"He told people that he had a huge cattle ranch in Australia. It did exist, it was a huge property, it just wasn't his," the ex-cop said.

Mr Gerondis said he was not surprised to see Mr Joseph has landed in hot water in the US.

"He's going to continue to do it [conduct himself fraudulently]. He can't help himself … I was surprised that it took so long," he said.

World.title: Nick Reiner could face death penalty if convicted of murdering parents
World.content:
A Los Angeles County grand jury has indicted Nick Reiner on murder charges in the killings of his parents, director Rob Reiner and Michele Singer Reiner, and added the allegation that he was lying in wait before attacking them.

Jake Reiner describes 'living nightmare' after parents' deaths Jake Reiner, the older son of Rob and Michele Reiner, says learning his parents were killed — and the aftermath of that — has been “too devastating to comprehend”.

The grand jury, which had been meeting in secret, returned the indictment on July 20.

It was unsealed on August 12 when Nick Reiner, 32, entered a not guilty plea.

The director, actor and Hollywood luminary Rob Reiner and his wife, photographer and producer Michele Singer Reiner, were stabbed to death in their home in the upscale Brentwood section of Los Angeles on December 14 last year.

Nick Reiner was arrested hours later and charged two days later.

Major step towards trial

The grand jury indictment is a major step toward trial and allows prosecutors to skip California's preliminary hearing process, where evidence is publicly aired.

Rob Reiner, Michele Singer, Romy Reiner, Nick Reiner, Maria Gilfillan and Jake Reiner on the red carpet in September 2025. (Reuters: Aude Guerrucci)

"This was a profound betrayal by someone who was loved and trusted by the very people he is accused of killing," Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said in a statement.

"We hope that by having a grand jury return an indictment in this case it will bring us one step closer to a trial and achieving justice."

The unsealed indictment reveals few new details in a case that has been shrouded in secrecy.

But the lying in wait allegation along with other circumstances mean Nick Reiner is eligible for the death penalty.

Prosecutors say they have not decided whether to seek it.

The indictment did not say how or why Nick Reiner was lying in wait.

It also included an allegation that he used a knife in the killing.

Authorities previously said the couple was stabbed.

Nick Reiner pleads not guilty to murder Nick Reiner has pleaded not guilty to two counts of first-degree murder in the fatal stabbing of his parents in December last year.

Many of the most basic questions about the killing remain publicly unanswered.

Prosecutors have said nothing about possible motives and leaks in the case have been virtually nonexistent on both sides.

The Los Angeles County chief medical examiner said he would like to make their autopsy reports public, but a court order has prevented him from doing so.

The LA County Public Defender's Office, which is representing Nick Reiner, declined to comment on the indictment.

World.title: Moves to axe character references after Western Power rape case
World.content:
There are growing calls for the WA government to ban positive character evidence after three Western Power staff were stood down for offering references for a former colleague convicted of rape.

Warning: This story contains details some readers may find distressing.

As the law stands, judges sentencing offenders can consider references provided to the court which illustrate parts of a person's character.

In the case of former Western Power employee Jeffrey David Spinner, the judge determining the 59-year-old's sentence received eight positive character references which he said illustrated the offending was "out of character".

Western Power staff stood down after backing manager in rape trial Western Australia's energy minister lashes out at Western Power employees who provided references for a senior manager who was jailed for raping a female colleague.

Judge Massey summarised one Western Power operations manager's statement as saying Spinner had a "strong moral compass", while another colleague described him as always acting "respectfully and appropriately" towards her and others.

A third described him as a "supportive mentor" and a "loyal and dependable friend".

"There's a fairly consistent theme running through those references of you being a very good employee, a dedicated family person and dedicated to your friends as well," Judge Massey summarised.

"So I do give you the benefit of being a person of prior good character."

It contributed to Spinner receiving a five-year jail term.

Offending 'disturbing'

Those statements stood in stark contrast to the judge's assessment of Spinner's offending against his subordinate — a woman he was mentoring — which was described as "disturbing".

"You essentially did what you wanted with her at a time when you must have thought she was either passed out or asleep," the judge said.

Judge Massey had found the offending happened after the victim felt pressured into going out to dinner with Spinner, which ended with him bringing her to his hotel room, showering her in her clothes and helping her into bed before assaulting her.

Jeffrey David Spinner (right) was sentenced to five years in jail for the rape of a colleague. (Facebook: Jeff Spinner)

In her victim impact statement, which also factored into Spinner's sentence, the woman said she "no longer feels safe in the way she once did and consequently assesses whether she can trust the people round her".

"She speaks of feeling scared, vulnerable and uncertain about her future. She no longer sleeps well and is in a near constant state of hyper-vigilance."

'Terrible' lapse in judgement

The three current Western Power staff who gave Spinner positive character references were all stood down on Tuesday, after the case was brought to the agency's attention by a journalist the afternoon before.

Energy Minister Amber-Jade Sanderson said the aim was: "To send a message to the organisation and to the community that this behaviour is unacceptable, that this has been a terrible lapse in judgement of those individuals."

Amber-Jade Sanderson at a press conference with Western Power chief Gair Landsborough. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

Recently appointed CEO, Gair Landsborough, said he had been unaware of the character references because an oversight meant Western Power staff were not in court when the sentence was handed down and the character references referred to.

"For over two years, we've been supporting our employee," he said.

"She remains part of Western Power's workforce, a real valued contributor, and we want to make sure we continue to support her."

The organisation's handling of the case, communications with the minister and broader culture and safety programs are now all under review.

'An absolute victory': Good character evidence scrapped in NSW A survivor advocate behind the campaign calling for good character references to be abolished in sentencing perpetrators of sexual offences has described the NSW reform as "an absolute victory".

And while the state government has committed to outlawing positive character evidence for child sexual assault cases, it is yet to decide whether to do the same for those involving adults.

"Removing these references protects victims from further trauma, ensuring fairness and focusing sentencing on the gravity of the offence rather than the offender's reputation," Attorney General Tony Buti told the ABC in a statement.

"We are currently considering extending this ban to other types of offending."

Earlier this year New South Wales abolished good character references in sentencing for sexual offences.

However, legal figures had raised concerns it could limit the ability of courts to understand "the offender as a whole person".

Banning references 'critical'

Alison Evans, from the Centre for Women's Safety and Wellbeing, said it was critical the government banned the practical for adult offenders as well.

"As a state, we are letting victim survivors of sexual violence down if we continue to permit the use of good character references in the courtroom to … influence sexual violence sentencing," she said.

Alison Evans says character references are not reliable evidence. (ABC News: Courtney Withers)

The family and sexual violence advocate said the practice caused a "great deal of harm" to victim-survivors and risked "making them feel that somehow they are to blame".

"Good character references by family, friends, co-workers aren't reliable evidence," she said.

Greens women and children's safety spokesperson Jess Beckerling agreed.

"Far too many victims of gendered violence are facing the courts and hearing their perpetrator being described as being of good character," she said.

"That's re-traumatising for those victim-survivors, it's outrageous, and it's time that the Cook Labor government just get on and change it."

Ms Beckerling said with parliament scheduled to sit for just nine more weeks before the end of the year, it should be a priority for the government.

Jess Beckerling criticised the government's legislative agenda. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

"We have a very poor legislative agenda at the moment here in Western Australia," she said.

She said that instead of dealing with "unnecessary administrative bills, we should be dealing with the important things".

"We need to be dealing with this," she said.

World.title: Jonas Brothers confirmed as half-time entertainment for historic MCG clash
World.content:
The Jonas Brothers will perform at half-time of the NFL's season opener between the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams at the MCG.

The NFL announced the headliners for the half-time show overnight. The game will air on Netflix in Australia on the morning of Friday, September 11. The Jonas Brothers will be part of the entertainment line-up for the league's international schedule this season involving seven countries and four continents.

"We couldn't be more excited to perform at half-time during the NFL's first-ever regular season game in Australia," the Jonas Brothers said in a statement.

"Playing at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground in front of such passionate Australian fans is an incredible honour."

The Jonas Brothers — featuring Nick, Joe and Kevin — have sold more than 20 million albums and recently landed a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

Tim Tubito, the NFL's senior director of global game presentation and entertainment, said the league's first regular season game in Australia is a landmark for the NFL.

NFL confirms historic MCG game to be played on AFL semifinal weekend The first-ever regular-season NFL game played in Australia has had its date confirmed, with the Melbourne Cricket Ground to host the historic match in the middle of the AFL finals series.

"The Jonas Brothers are global entertainers whose music connects across generations, making them the ideal artists to help us celebrate this historic game in Melbourne," Tubito said.

"We look forward to delivering a memorable half-time performance for our fans in Australia and those watching around the world."

The NFL game is set to clash with the AFL's semifinal weekend when the two losing teams of the qualifying finals will host matches.

That could cause headaches for the AFL if those two teams are Victorian clubs, with Hawthorn likely to finish top four and Melbourne and Geelong still in the hunt.

World.title: Europe's first solar eclipse in 27 years in pictures
World.content:
Crowds have gathered around Europe to see the skies fall dark in a rare total solar eclipse.

The moon completely covered the sun as seen from the Javalambre Astrophysical Observatory in Arcos de las Salinas, near Teruel, Spain. (Reuters: Christian Hartmann)

Artists use self-made artefacts to observe the solar eclipse near the small village of Castell de Cabres, Spain. (Reuters: Eva Manez)

From Spain to Iceland, people gathered to witness the Sun's light be fully blocked by the Moon in the continent's first solar eclipse in 27 years.

Totality — when the Moon completely covers the Sun's light — was expected to last less than 2 and a half minutes, reaching its maximum duration off Iceland's west coast.

Reykjavik, Iceland was covered by darkness. (Reuters: Denis Balibouse )

By the time it got to a small patch of Portugal and then to Spain, just before sunset, totality dwindled to a minute or so. The total eclipse then ended over the Mediterranean.

Beachgoers watched the solar eclipse along the coast of Fregene, near Rome. (Reuters: Guglielmo Mangiapane)

Masks and glasses are essential when viewing the eclipse. (Reuters: Denis Balibouse)

One woman used a welder's mask to view the eclipse. (Reuters: Kacper Pempel)

Before the spectacular celestial event, long queues were seen outside shops selling special eclipse glasses.

The glasses are essential for safe viewing, even if only a sliver of the sun remains visible. They are made with special filters that block solar radiation that can damage the eyes.

Spain was a popular viewing point of the eclipse. (Reuters: Christian Hartmann)

Navarrete, northern Spain. (Reuters: Vincent West)

Watch parties were held, with crowds heard cheering as the sky went dark in Iceland's capital, Reykjavik.

Authorities were expecting up to 6 million visitors in mostly rural areas within the eclipse's path across the north of Spain and the Balearic Islands, said Juan Cruz Cigudosa García, Spain's secretary of State for science.

"I hope that tonight will see the emergence of a wonderful generation of astrophysicists," he said.

A single camera captured the different stages of the eclipse. (Reuters: Borja Suarez)

" It's such a special moment. "

The eclipse was followed by a sunset in Spain, making the event particularly alluring.

The eclipse was visible from Berlin. (Reuters: Fabrizio Bensch)

The Molecule Men, a 30-metre-high metal sculpture in Berlin's Spree river, stood out. (Reuters: Joachim Herrmann)

The eclipse reflected over the Vistula river in Warsaw, Poland. (Reuters: Kuba Stezycki)

Millions of others across Europe enjoyed a total view of the celestial spectacle.

Thousands gathered in town squares and on beaches to see the show.

Some of the best views were in rural parts of Spain. (Reuters: Ana Beltran)

The Eiffel Tower silhouetted while the moon partially covered the sun. (Reuters: Sarah Meyssonnier)

Landmarks from Paris to Saint Petersburg shone through bright red and yellow skies.

The Prague Castle stood out in the light. (Reuters: Eva Korinkova)

Parts of central and eastern Europe like Belgrade in Serbia saw the skies go dark. (Reuters: Djordje Kojadinovic)

Across Britain, where the sun was more than 90 per cent obscured, people flocked to hilltop parks and anywhere with an open view of the sky to see the best eclipse since 1999.

Grey clouds did not deter viewers in Glastonbury. (Reuters: Toby Melville)

In Greenwich Park, with views of the River Thames and central London, the sky turned an eerie grey as a sliver of light sat atop the moon like a hat.

Beaches in Italy were a popular viewpoint. (Reuters: Guglielmo Mangiapane)

In the east, Saint Petersburg, Russia turned red in the eclipse. (Reuters: Marina Lystseva)

According to NASA, the next total solar eclipse is expected in August 2027 to be visible across northern Africa.

In July 2028, Australia and New Zealand will also have a chance to experience the skies go dark in a total solar eclipse.

The "diamond ring" effect appeared as the moon moved across the sun. (Reuters: Borja Suarez)

The eclipse was the most significant since 1999. (Reuters: Fabrizio Bensch)

World.title: China's rejection of Australian mung beans prompts chemical rethink
World.content:
China has rejected 10 containers of Australian mung beans after testing found the shipment exceeded allowed chemical levels.

Australian mung bean Association and Pulse Australia agronomist Paul McIntosh said tests found residue levels of glyphosate from Queensland were five times the allowed limit.

"[It's] very disappointing for the industry as a whole because we all get hammered with the same brush about that sort of stuff," he said.

The Grains Research and Development Corporation estimates glyphosate is used to dry out about 95 per cent of Australia's mung bean crop prior to harvest, known as desiccating.

If applied too early, the agency warns higher chemical residues can remain on the seeds during harvest, which risks exceeding acceptable export levels.

Mr McIntosh said this meant there was a chance growers could exceed chemical levels even if they were using the chemical correctly.

"You could be doing everything right for 90 per cent of the paddock, and 10 per cent of the paddock could be fairly green and suck up a lot of glyphosate," he said.

"And hey, presto, before you know where you are, you've got an MRL (maximum residue limit) issue."

Maximum residue limits are the highest amount of chemical residue that is legally allowed in a food, set well below safe eating levels.

They are set by the importing country as part of trade access agreements, and influence the timing and rate of application farmers can use.

Bumper crop

The rejected shipment was part of a bumper crop for Australian growers, who will produce 100,000 to 120,000 tonnes in 2026, almost all of it exported.

Most were destined for China, which also sets some of the toughest maximum residue limit (MRL) restrictions.

Grower and exporter Clint Allenden said recently Chinese authorities had become stricter on enforcement.

"China's our main market … they've always had these regulations, they just haven't enforced them," he said.

Clint Allenden has focused on making sure his clients are following label instructions. (ABC Capricornia: Jessica D'Souza)

He said the tougher compliance had prompted him to investigate and alternative to glyphosate for desiccation.

"When we were made aware of the testing being done in China for beans, we looked into swathing and we contacted a swathing contractor," he said.

Slow uptake

Swathing is a mechanical process that involves cutting and laying crops in rows to dry them out, before using equipment called a swather to harvest them.

Stewart Johnston was one of the first mung bean growers in central Queensland to swath his crop.

He experimented on part of his crop during the most recent growing season on his farm at Banana, about 600km north of Brisbane, sourcing the equipment from Western Australia.

"It definitely sped the process up, like anywhere from three to five days after swathing, we were ready to go [harvest]," he said.

Stuart and Helen Johnston started swathing their crop this year. (ABC Capricornia: Jessica D'Souza)

But Darren Jensen, who grows mung beans near Biloela, about 50km east of Mr Johnston's farm, said swathing was not an option for all growers.

"If you've got nice flat soil, nice flat country and it's a little bit harder and your sprayer doesn't sink in quite so much … that's fantastic," he said.

"We have contour banks, we have rocks, we're in controlled traffic on very soft soil.

"You go and swath your mung beans, but for us, that's virtually impossible."

Darren Jensen believes swathing doesn't work for central Queensland's soil conditions. (Supplied: Darren Jensen)

Glyphosate-free mung beans do attract a premium price, but Mr Jensen said that was not enough to cover the cost of specialised equipment for a new method.

"We seem to be self-destroying ourselves by creating a problem that isn't there. If everyone does the right thing, I don't believe it's a problem at all."

Swathing the way of the future

But Mr Johnstone said swathers could modified to suit central Queensland's growing conditions.

"I reckon there's ways around that we should be able to work out," he said.

At a swathing field day at Mr Allenden's farm near Goovigen, viability was a key barrier for growers.

"There were a lot of unknowns," he said.

But as restrictions on chemical residues tighten around the world, Mr Allenden said swathing could become the way of the future.

"I think the cost of not doing it's going to cost a lot more than doing it," he said.

"I won't speak for other people, but … if you get your beans rejected because you've got excess, I think it's going to come back directly straight to the farmer."

World.title: ASX set to slide; ANZ posts $1.9b quarterly profit, home loan applications fall
World.content:
Updated BusinessMarketsWorld markets ASX set to slide; ANZ posts $1.9b quarterly profit, home loan applications fall Stan Choe Updated August 13, 2026 — 8:11am ,first published 5:15am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Wall Street edged near its record after several AI stocks reported better growth than analysts expected, while a report showed inflation across the United States was slightly less bad last month. The S&P 500 added 0.3 per cent and marked its first gain since setting its all-time high on Friday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped less than 0.1 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 0.5 per cent. Stocks like Nvidia and Super Micro Computer helped lead the way on signals that businesses continue to spend big dollars on AI infrastructure. Treasury yields eased following the latest inflation data. Wall Street jumped as the AI trade reignited after some positive results while a report showed inflation across the United States dipped. Bloomberg The Australian sharemarket is set to fall, with futures at 5.54am AEST pointing to a fall of 19 points or 0.2 per cent, at the open. The ASX lost 0.5 per cent on Wednesday. The Australian dollar was trading at US70.62¢. ANZ Bank says home loan applications have fallen 12 per cent since the May budget, excluding applications it received via a government deposit guarantee scheme, as it also reported $1.9 billion in cash profits for the latest quarter.



In a trading update for the June quarter, ANZ said its cash profits rose 1 per cent compared with the quarterly average for the March half. On Wall Street, stocks in the artificial-intelligence technology business helped lead the way after strong profit reports bolstered hopes they can continue to deliver big-enough growth to justify the huge gains their prices have made. Super Micro Computer, which sells servers and other equipment, jumped 19.6 per cent after reporting earnings per share for the latest quarter that were 84 per cent higher than analysts expected. It also gave forecasts for upcoming profit and revenue that topped analysts’ expectations. Related Article Opinion

Gold Gold is glittering again – but that’s not necessarily good news Stephen Bartholomeusz Senior business columnist CoreWeave, which offers AI computing power to customers over the cloud, leaped 19 per cent after reporting better revenue for the latest quarter than analysts expected, along with a milder loss. CEO Michael Intrator said demand is accelerating from customers as big businesses adopt AI.



CoreWeave gives its customers access to AI chips from Nvidia, and Nvidia climbed 3 per cent. It was the single strongest force lifting the S&P 500. It’s a return to strength for AI stocks, which have been veering on a roller-coaster ride. After surging to records, AI stocks came under pressure on worries that they shot too high. Investors wanted to see big spenders on AI prove that their investments are yielding enough in profits and productivity to make them worth it. That in turn could lead to continued demand for chips and other AI infrastructure. Wall Street also got some support from easing yields in the bond market. Treasury yields fell after a report showed that US consumers paid prices for gasoline, groceries and other costs of living last month that were 3.4 per cent higher than a year earlier. That’s higher than anyone would like, but it’s not as bad as June’s 3.5 per cent inflation rate. The deceleration could give the Federal Reserve more leeway to hold off on hikes to interest rates. Higher rates would help keep a lid on inflation, but it would do so by making it more expensive for US households and companies to borrow and forcing a slowdown in the economy. Higher interest rates also would undercut prices for stocks and other investments.



The Fed’s members have been notably split about whether they should have already begun hiking interest rates. But Wednesday’s update on inflation pushed traders to pull back on bets the Fed will hike its main interest rate at its next meeting in September. Traders are betting on just a 40 per cent chance of it, down from the coin flip’s chance seen the day before, according to data from CME Group. That helped pull the yield on the 10-year Treasury down to 4.68 per cent from 4.70 per cent late Tuesday. It, though, still remains well above its 3.97 per cent level from before the war with Iran, which sent oil prices and worries about inflation spiking. Related Article Opinion

Property market Is it time to buy a house? Here is what the CBA chief would tell his kids Elizabeth Knight Business columnist Oil prices swung between modest gains and losses Wednesday, and the price for a barrel of Brent crude slipped 0.2 per cent to $US88.74.



Higher yields have already pulled long-term mortgage rates to their highest levels in a year. That’s hurting the housing industry, and losses for homebuilders on Wednesday helped keep the market in check. D.R. Horton fell 3.3 per cent, and PulteGroup lost 2.5 per cent. Builders FirstSource, which sells countertops and other building materials, dropped 1.9 per cent. In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed across Europe and Asia. South Korea’s Kospi jumped 3.7 per cent for one of the world’s bigger gains. It’s been at the center of the jarring swings for AI stocks because it’s dominated by two tech giants, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. AP The Market Recap newsletter is a wrap of the day’s trading. Get it each weekday afternoon.

ANZ Bank says home loan applications have fallen 12 per cent since the May budget, excluding applications it received via a government deposit guarantee scheme, as it also reported $1.9 billion in cash profits for the latest quarter.

In a trading update for the June quarter, ANZ said its cash profits rose 1 per cent compared with the quarterly average for the March half.

A key focus for investors is how the government’s move to rein in tax concessions for property investors is affecting mortgage lending, and rival banks have all revealed a significant drop in loan applications since the May budget.

Home loan applications for ANZ have fallen 12 per cent since the May budget. Will Willitts

ANZ reported applications were “broadly flat” in the June quarter compared with March, though this was supported by the bank joining the federal government’s 5 per cent deposit guarantee scheme from late March.

Joining the scheme meant the bank’s loan growth was stronger than it would have been otherwise.

Excluding the impact of the scheme, ANZ said the value of new mortgage applications fell 12 per cent in the period from the budget to late July, compared with the March quarter.

World.title: ‘Once in a lifetime’: Millions gather in Europe to see first total solar eclipse in decades
World.content:
WorldEuropeSpace ‘Once in a lifetime’: Millions gather in Europe to see first total solar eclipse in decades Corina Pons and Tom Little August 13, 2026 — 6:21am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Madrid/Reykjavik: The skies above Iceland fell into total darkness as a full solar eclipse occurred over the country’s westernmost coast, as a break in the clouds allowed holidaymakers and locals to glimpse the celestial phenomenon. Live footage from Reykjavik showed on Wednesday (Iceland time) that, despite the overcast sky, a cheer went up from the crowd gathered in front of Hallgrimskirkja church when everything went black above them. The total solar eclipse is seen in Palencia, Spain. Getty Images Millions of people gathered in Iceland and northern Spain to witness Western Europe’s first total solar eclipse in 27 years, with Spanish officials warning people to avoid areas where a heatwave has raised the risk of wildfires. Authorities were expecting up to 6 million visitors in mostly rural areas within the eclipse’s path across the north of Spain and the Balearic Islands, said Juan Cruz, Spain’s Secretary of State for Science.



“I hope that tonight will see the emergence of a wonderful generation of astrophysicists,” he said. “It’s such a special moment.” The eclipse was quickly followed by the sunset in Spain, making the event particularly alluring. The uncanny sensation when day briefly turns into twilight and some animals fall quiet as the moon passes directly between Earth and the sun, was often treated as an omen in the past, a cosmic struggle or a sign of divine power.



Now, Spain sees it as a chance to showcase seldom-visited regions and draw tourists away from its overcrowded beach resorts, while also rolling out a massive police operation and public safety campaign to prevent them from causing wildfires. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska told reporters that 25,000 police officers had been assigned to guarantee security around the eclipse observation while nearly 100 planes and helicopters were also being deployed. People observing a partial eclipse at Northala Fields in London. AP Photo/Frank Augstein A man watches with a welding shield in Herten, Germany. AP Photo/Martin Meissner Lola Guerreiro spent the night in the mountains near Arcos de las Salinas in eastern Spain, home to Galactica – Europe’s largest educational astronomy centre – as well as the Javalambre observatory, after making the long drive from Extremadura to view the eclipse.



“Watching a total solar eclipse has been a dream of mine for many, many years, and I didn’t want to miss the chance to experience it, even though it meant a seven-hour journey,” she said. Sergio, a 60-year-old Italian, had made the trek in a camping van with his family to Arija in northern Spain. The eclipse seen at El Monte De San Pedro park in Spain. Getty Images People cast long shadows while watching from the top of a mine dump in Gremany. AP Photo/Martin Meissner “I do feel a little emotional. Yes, because I know I won’t have another chance in my life to see an eclipse, a phenomenon like this,” he said.



The Iberian Peninsula last saw a total solar eclipse in 1912. It is set to experience another one on August 2, 2027, and an annular eclipse in January 2028, completing the so-called “Iberian Eclipse Trio”. In Iceland’s capital Reykjavik, glasses to allow people to look at the phenomenon without damaging their eyes have been sold out for days as the Nordic country of roughly 400,000 people expects to welcome up to 80,000 visitors. The eclipse seen form Palencia, Spain. Millions gathered across the country to witness the event. Getty Images People observe the partial eclipse with special protective glasses in Liverpool, England. AP Photo/Jon Super Totality – when the moon completely covers the sun’s light – reached Iceland’s westernmost coast at about 5:44 pm local time (3.44am on Thursday, AEST). It cast the far west of the island nation into total darkness for more than two minutes, though most cities saw shorter periods of darkness. The moon’s shadow then continued its trajectory eastwards.



Authorities had warned of heavy traffic and urged viewers to arrive early. Singer Björk was due to perform a DJ set at an eclipse-themed event south of Reykjavik. US space agency NASA plans to fly a high-altitude WB-57 aircraft from Iceland to follow the moon’s shadow, and NASA-funded teams will launch balloons to study how the sudden darkness and cooling affect the lower atmosphere. A beachgoer wearing special eclipse glasses looks up from Puerto de Sagunto beach near Valencia, Spain. AP Photo/Alberto Saiz The moon and the sun set in the Gulf of Finland, seen from St. Petersburg, Russia. AP Photo/Dmitri Lovetsky Aside from casual observers, the event also draws “eclipse chasers”, enthusiasts who crisscross the globe to be in the path of totality whenever an eclipse occurs.



Gordon Telepun, a retired plastic surgeon and amateur astronomer from the U.S. who has photographed six total eclipses, said he would watch from the island of Mallorca because Spain checked all the boxes for eclipse chasers. World.title: LA Lakers sold in record $17.7b deal as Trump associate and former Disney chief swoop
World.content:
BusinessCompaniesMergers & acquisitions LA Lakers sold in record $17.7b deal as Trump associate and former Disney chief swoop Randall Williams , Natasha Mascarenhas and Hannah Miller August 13, 2026 — 6:11am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Josh Kushner and Bob Iger are buying the Los Angeles Lakers basketball team for a record-breaking price of $US12.5 billion ($17.7 billion), according to people familiar with the matter. Kushner, managing partner and co-founder at Thrive Capital, and Iger, former chief executive officer of Walt Disney Co. who is also an adviser at Thrive, had been seeking to acquire an NBA expansion team in Las Vegas but pivoted to make an offer to buy the Lakers from financier Mark Walter, whose sprawling investment empire is under federal investigation. Joshua Kushner, with wife Karlie Kloss, is the younger brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner. Bloomberg The first inquiry came from Iger-Kushner side and the deal moved quickly, with talks unfolding over a matter of three or four days and the final agreement coming together in the past 24 hours, Iger said in an interview with Bloomberg News on Wednesday. The deal represents a longtime dream of Iger, who has overseen billion-dollar NBA rights contracts for Disney’s ESPN division, but not owned a professional basketball team. It underscores the booming prices private equity firms are willing to pay for the top-tier sports franchises globally as those media rights continue to climb.



The executive recalled that Kushner, who is the brother of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, likened buying the Lakers to purchasing the Mona Lisa. “This is a beachfront property on one of the best beaches in the world as I see it,” Iger said. Founded in 1947, the Los Angeles Lakers have been a powerhouse in the NBA. After moving from Minneapolis in 1960 to become the NBA’s first West Coast team, the Lakers have been in the finals 32 times and won 17 championships, establishing them as one of the most successful legacies in professional sports. Their “Showtime” era in the 1980s was led by superstar players like Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Magic Johnson. The fast-paced game the Lakers pioneered continues to influence the sport to this day. The Lakers are one of the most prestigious sports franchises in the world. AP The Lakers’ sale price is the highest ever for a US professional sports franchise, exceeding the $US9.6 billion paid for the National Football League’s Seattle Seahawks in July. “It’s stunning in terms of the amount and size,” said Lee Berke, CEO of sports media consultancy LHB Sports, Entertainment & Media. “If I was an NBA team, I’d be thrilled.”



Walter, who also owns the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team and is an investor in English Premier League club Chelsea, bought a majority stake in the Lakers from the Buss family just over a year ago, in a deal valued at $US10 billion. Despite the change in majority owner, the league said at the time that Jeanie Buss, one of the children of the longtime owner Jerry Buss, would remain the team’s controlling governor for the foreseeable future. Former Disney chief Bob Iger. Bloomberg The billionaire CEO of Guggenheim Partners is dealing with a federal investigation into potential improprieties at two of his insurance companies and his global investment firm. Walter’s holding company, TWG Global, holds stakes in the sports teams as well as Walter’s insurance companies and in Guggenheim. Part of the inquiry involved representations Guggenheim made to outside parties about its revenue, Bloomberg reported in July. “Mark Walter and TWG have always acted in good faith, and those who have done business with Mark know him as honest and straightforward,” TWG Global, Walter’s holding company, said in a statement at the time. “We are cooperating with authorities, and we are confident these matters will be resolved favourably.”



Iger stepped down from the head of Disney, the parent company of ESPN, earlier this year but his association with sports goes back decades. A longtime Clippers fan, Iger previously worked at ABC Sports under media legend Roone Arledge and became the division’s vice president of programming in 1987. He joined Disney following the company’s acquisition of ABC and ESPN in 1996. The NBA aired on ABC from 1965 until 1973 and on ESPN between 1982 and 1984 before returning to both channels in 2002. Disney, Comcast Corp. and Amazon.com Inc. signed an 11-year, $US76 billion deal with the NBA in 2024 that kicked in with the league’s most recent season. Kushner and his newly formed holding company Thrive Eternal, which targets cultural institutions and sports franchises, made waves in the last two weeks when soccer’s governing body FIFA attempted to raise $US4.2 billion from investors including Thrive that would have created a for-profit arm housing the organisation’s media and commercial rights. The deal died after extreme pushback from UEFA and Concacaf. Mark Walter, pictured here with US President Donald Trump, bought a majority stake in the Lakers just over a year ago, in a deal valued at $US10 billion. Walter’s investment empire is under investigation. Getty Images One of Thrive Eternal’s first moves was buying a piece of the San Francisco Giants earlier this year, ploughing the money into the team’s stadium and surrounding real estate. Individually, Kushner had purchased stakes in the Memphis Grizzlies before selling that slice to acquire a piece of the Miami Heat. His aspirations to be the controlling owner of an NBA team went so far that he and Iger were interested in buying one of the potential NBA expansion teams in Las Vegas. As a result of the Lakers’ deal, Kushner will have to sell his piece of the Miami Heat. Karlie Kloss, Kushner’s wife, is a minority owner in WNBA team New York Liberty.
